title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
四川鄉試錄序
嘉靖丙午側當天下貢士四
川守臣如
制奉行巡按御史袁〔鳳 鳴〕寔監臨
之祗肅風紀約飭執事兼采
虛受惟恐弗勝維時巡撫都
御史張〔時 徹〕經畧懋著造就
===
靡遺身教所孚士萌闓懌先
是巡按御史朱〔徵〕以禮聘學
正周〔文 龍〕教諭李〔鴻 漸〕爲考
試官教諭翟〔宗 魯〕吴〔雲 臺〕艾
〔儒〕李〔梧〕王〔鎮〕張〔價〕爲同考試
官俱如期而至提調則左布
政使嚴〔時 泰〕左參政李〔義 壯〕
punctuated:
四川鄉試錄序

嘉靖丙午，側當天下貢士，四川守臣如制奉行。巡按御史袁〔鳳 鳴〕寔監臨之，祗肅風紀，約飭執事，兼采虛受，惟恐弗勝。維時巡撫都御史張〔時 徹〕經畧懋著，造就靡遺，身教所孚，士萌闓懌。先是，巡按御史朱〔徵〕以禮聘學正周〔文 龍〕、教諭李〔鴻 漸〕爲考試官，教諭翟〔宗 魯〕、吴〔雲 臺〕、艾〔儒〕、李〔梧〕、王〔鎮〕、張〔價〕爲同考試官，俱如期而至。提調則左布政使嚴〔時 泰〕、左參政李〔義 壯〕，
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Sichuan Provincial Examination

In the bingwu year of the Jiajing reign (1546), when candidates were being presented throughout the empire [?], the officials governing Sichuan carried out the prescribed procedures. Regional Inspecting Censor Yuan Fengming served as Supervising Official. He reverently upheld discipline, instructed and admonished those administering the examination, and sought counsel widely, receiving it with an open mind, ever fearful of failing in his responsibilities. At that time, Grand Coordinator and Censor-in-chief Zhang Shiche had achieved distinguished results in his administration and had spared no effort in cultivating talent. His personal example inspired trust, and scholars and common people [?] were delighted.

Previously, Regional Inspecting Censor Zhu Zheng had courteously invited Zhou Wenlong, a subprefectural school instructor, and Li Hongjian, a county school instructor, to serve as Examiners. He invited county school instructors Zhai Zonglu, Wu Yuntai, Ai Ru, Li Wu, Wang Zhen, and Zhang Jia to serve as Associate Examiners. All arrived at the appointed time. The Proctors were Left Provincial Administration Commissioner Yan Shitai and Left Administration Vice Commissioner Li Yizhuang…

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
監試則按察使紀常副使沈
應龍綜理惟寅均任厥責其
防範於外則右布政使王崇
慶右參政宋宜曾鈞左參議
高翀右參議丁湛副使胡鳳
夏雷繆宗周朱篚翁溥僉事
張朝聘李實陳乙陳位劉世
===
用畫謀惟協聿求厥成都指
揮僉事徐昺則嚴督巡邏恪
慎其所有事迺以壬辰入院
矢於有衆合提學副使易寬
所簡士二千八百有奇三試
之見其馳騁藝苑瓊藻璀錯
有不勝選者如額拔七十人
punctuated: 監試則按察使紀常、副使沈應龍，綜理惟寅，均任厥責。其防範於外，則右布政使王崇慶、右參政宋宜、曾鈞、左參議高翀、右參議丁湛、副使胡鳳、夏雷、繆宗周、朱篚、翁溥、僉事張朝聘、李實、陳乙、陳位、劉世用，畫謀惟協，聿求厥成。都指揮僉事徐昺，則嚴督巡邏，恪慎其所有事。迺以壬辰入院，矢於有衆，合提學副使易寬所簡士二千八百有奇，三試之。見其馳騁藝苑，瓊藻璀錯，有不勝選者，如額拔七十人
translation_en:
For oversight of the examination, Surveillance Commissioner Ji Chang and Surveillance Vice Commissioner Shen Yinglong managed affairs with reverent care, each bearing his share of responsibility. Precautions outside the examination compound were entrusted to Right Provincial Administration Commissioner Wang Chongqing; Provincial Administration Vice Commissioners of the Right Song Yi and Zeng Jun; Provincial Administration Assistant Commissioner of the Left Gao Chong; Provincial Administration Assistant Commissioner of the Right Ding Zhan; Surveillance Vice Commissioners Hu Feng, Xia Lei, Miu Zongzhou, Zhu Fei, and Weng Pu; and Surveillance Assistant Commissioners Zhang Chaopin, Li Shi, Chen Yi, Chen Wei, and Liu Shiyong. They coordinated their plans and sought to bring the undertaking to completion. Assistant Regional Military Commissioner Xu Bing strictly supervised the patrols and attended conscientiously to his duties.
On the renchen day, we entered the examination compound and made a solemn pledge before the assembled company. We gathered the more than 2,800 candidates selected by Education Intendant Yi Kuan, a Surveillance Vice Commissioner, and examined them in three sessions. We saw them range freely through the garden of literary accomplishment, their gemlike compositions glittering in profusion; there were more worthy of selection than could be chosen. In accordance with the quota, we selected seventy men…

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
爲最次第其名氏錄其文以
獻予觀鉅典告竣俊乂趨蹌作
而嘆曰西蜀文教之興於茲
爲極仰見我
聖皇文明之化于茲爲盛也昔者
有周論次德義宣暨禮樂殊
方絶域聞風慕義是時庸蜀
===
雖已若訓而雅頌絃歌之被
未能無閡焉者孔氏陳述六
經脩明四教闡關王路裁除
雜術弟子散游列國取重諸
侯其徒分授各有所傳蜀雖
嶮遠而風敎已渢渢乎迫昔
尚矣漢置益州部刺史務在
punctuated: 爲最，次第其名氏，錄其文以獻。予觀鉅典告竣，俊乂趨蹌，作而嘆曰：「西蜀文教之興，於茲爲極，仰見我聖皇文明之化，于茲爲盛也。昔者有周，論次德義，宣暨禮樂，殊方絶域，聞風慕義。是時庸蜀雖已若訓，而雅頌絃歌之被，未能無閡焉者。孔氏陳述六經，脩明四教，闡關王路，裁除雜術。弟子散游列國，取重諸侯，其徒分授，各有所傳。蜀雖嶮遠，而風敎已渢渢乎迫昔尚矣。漢置益州部刺史，務在
translation_en:
…as the best. Their names were arranged in order, and their compositions transcribed for presentation to the throne. As I witnessed the completion of this grand undertaking and the dignified movements of these talented men, I rose and exclaimed: “The flourishing of literary cultivation in western Shu has now reached its height. Looking upward in reverence, we see that the civilizing influence of our sage emperor has attained its fullness here.

“In ancient times, the Zhou assessed and ranked virtue and righteousness and spread rites and music. Even distant lands and remote regions heard of their influence and admired their righteousness. At that time, although Yong and Shu already followed their instructions, the dissemination of the Odes and Hymns through singing to stringed accompaniment still encountered obstacles. Confucius expounded the Six Classics, cultivated and elucidated the four teachings, opened the way of the ancient kings [?], and eliminated miscellaneous doctrines. His disciples traveled throughout the various states and won the esteem of the feudal lords. His followers taught in different places, each transmitting what he had received. Although Shu was rugged and remote, its moral instruction already flourished abundantly, approaching that of high antiquity [?]. The Han established a Regional Inspector for the Yizhou region, whose principal concern was …

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
開拓禮樂未遑蜀郡太守文
翁興教遣弟子十餘詣京師
受學比於博士故詩書之化
移乎風俗王襃刺益州宣風
化於衆庶作中和樂職宣布
三詩選少年歌以鹿鳴之聲
當此之時郡國次舉學官博
===
士乃有司馬相如王褒楊雄
之革相繼以英茂精豔顯名
侍從士乃披揚洪煇蕩駘儒
林沿而自鳴者衆而悖篤之
行君子少之使漢於蜀力興
文學而本之以德教其作人
固若是乎自是以後唐制雜
punctuated: 開拓，禮樂未遑。蜀郡太守文翁興教，遣弟子十餘詣京師受學，比於博士，故詩書之化移乎風俗。王襃刺益州，宣風化於衆庶，作《中和》《樂職》《宣布》三詩，選少年歌以《鹿鳴》之聲。當此之時，郡國次舉學官博士。乃有司馬相如、王褒、楊雄之革，相繼以英茂精豔顯名侍從。士乃披揚洪煇，蕩駘儒林，沿而自鳴者衆，而悖篤之行，君子少之。使漢於蜀力興文學，而本之以德教，其作人固若是乎？自是以後，唐制雜
translation_en: …opening up territory, with no leisure for rites and music. Wen Weng, Grand Administrator of Shu Commandery, promoted education, sending more than ten students to the capital to receive instruction alongside the Erudites. Thus the transforming influence of the Odes and Documents altered local customs. Wang Bao, serving as Regional Inspector of Yizhou, spread moral instruction among the common people. He composed three poems, “Central Harmony,” “Delight in Office,” and “Proclamation,” and selected youths to sing them to the tune of “The Deer Cry.” At this time, the commanderies and kingdoms successively appointed educational officials and Erudites. Then came men such as Sima Xiangru, Wang Bao, and Yang Xiong [?], who one after another won distinction as court attendants through their outstanding talents and refined, splendid writing. Scholars thus displayed their great brilliance and roamed freely through the world of Confucian learning. Many followed this course and made their voices heard, yet gentlemen found little steadfastness in their conduct [?]. Had the Han vigorously promoted literary learning in Shu while grounding it in moral instruction, would its cultivation of men really have produced such results? Thereafter, under the Tang, the institutions became mixed…

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
夷宋勢卑弱禮讓規制蓋有
闕焉仰惟我
太祖高皇帝聖謨神策驅胡靖華
偃干戈之習敷文德之化西
除僞夏以大一統蜀之人士
翕然誦法姬孔之道迨我
成祖文命大行公卿吉士蒙徵抜
===
者悉置左右郡國無論遐邇
申庠序之教蜀郡縣穎秀咸
收育學宫三歲校文抜其儁
升之禮官禮官遴之得待
詔丹陛以次進用
列聖繩武大化旁洽周雅曰鎬京
辟雍自西自東自南自北無
punctuated: 夷，宋勢卑弱，禮讓規制蓋有闕焉。仰惟我太祖高皇帝，聖謨神策，驅胡靖華，偃干戈之習，敷文德之化，西除僞夏，以大一統。蜀之人士翕然誦法姬孔之道。迨我成祖文命大行，公卿吉士蒙徵抜者，悉置左右。郡國無論遐邇，申庠序之教，蜀郡縣穎秀咸收育學宫。三歲校文，抜其儁，升之禮官；禮官遴之，得待詔丹陛，以次進用。列聖繩武，大化旁洽。《周雅》曰：「鎬京辟雍，自西自東，自南自北，無
translation_en: …barbarian elements; the Song was weak in power, and its institutions of ritual and deference were consequently deficient. We reverently reflect upon how our Emperor Taizu Gao, through sagely designs and divinely inspired strategies, expelled the northern barbarians and pacified the Chinese realm, put an end to the habit of warfare, and spread the transforming influence of civil virtue. In the west he eliminated the illegitimate Xia regime, thereby completing the great unification. The scholars of Shu unanimously recited and took as their model the Way of the Duke of Zhou and Confucius. When the civilizing commands of our Chengzu spread widely, the high ministers and worthy scholars summoned and selected for service were all placed at his side. Throughout the realm, far and near alike, instruction in the schools was strengthened. Talented youths from the prefectures and counties of Shu were all admitted to the government schools and nurtured there. Every three years their compositions were assessed, the outstanding candidates selected and advanced to the officials of the Ministry of Rites. Those officials selected from among them, and the successful candidates were permitted to await imperial commands at the vermilion steps and were appointed to service in due order. Successive sage emperors continued the achievements of their predecessors, and their great transforming influence spread everywhere. The Odes of Zhou say: “At Haojing’s Biyong ceremonial academy, from the west and from the east, from the south and from the north, none …

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
思不服於乎盛哉我
皇上御極敷玄德錫四方本彛倫
昭上下
敬一安安德教洋溢協氣四涌
瑞徵類集人文煥然草木賁
若實往古風化所無也故曰
觀乎人文以化成天下今多
===
士宴鹿鳴揚休澤金追玉琢
比於聲音彬彬乎弗軌而肅
弗序而章豈非涵濡文明之
化而有得哉雖然占之以文
多士美矣吾慮夫進也以文
而行或違之非爾多士純心
效用之學豈於我
punctuated: 思不服。」於乎盛哉！我皇上御極，敷玄德，錫四方，本彛倫，昭上下。敬一安安，德教洋溢，協氣四涌，瑞徵類集，人文煥然，草木賁若，實往古風化所無也。故曰：「觀乎人文，以化成天下。」今多士宴鹿鳴，揚休澤，金追玉琢，比於聲音，彬彬乎弗軌而肅，弗序而章，豈非涵濡文明之化而有得哉？雖然，占之以文，多士美矣。吾慮夫進也以文，而行或違之，非爾多士純心效用之學，豈於我
translation_en:
…fail to submit.” Ah, how flourishing it is! Our Emperor has ascended the throne, spread his profound virtue, and bestowed blessings upon the four quarters. He takes the enduring human relationships as his foundation and illuminates the proper relations between those above and below. Reverently maintaining unity of purpose, he rests naturally in tranquillity. His virtuous teaching overflows; harmonious influences surge in every direction; auspicious signs gather in abundance. Human culture shines brilliantly, and even the grasses and trees appear adorned. Such transforming moral influence was truly unknown in antiquity. Thus it is said: “Observe human culture, and thereby transform and perfect all under Heaven.” Now the assembled scholars feast at the Deer-Calling Banquet and extol his beneficent bounty. Like worked metal and carved jade, they are attuned to harmonious sounds. Refined and accomplished, they are disciplined without imposed rules and display order without being arranged. Surely this is because they have been steeped in the transforming influence of enlightened culture and have gained something from it?

Nevertheless, judged by their writing, these scholars are admirable. My concern is that they may advance through their writing while their conduct departs from it. This would not be the learning by which you scholars purify your hearts and render useful service. How could this, with regard to our …

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
皇上敬一之訓求之思也乎孔子
曰文莫吾猶人也躬行君子
則吾未之有得聖人匪抑文
也固不貴言也不然則爾蜀
先哲長卿淵雲縱橫詞賦搜
剔玄微文非不工也而君子
至今訾之神禹左準繩右規
===
矩不專尚文而天地平成之
績萬世永賴何也蘊之爲德
行行之爲事業措之爲文辭
一以貫之者也顏淵曰舜何
人也予何人也有爲者亦若
是爾多士鑒於神禹之不自
滿假而昌言是諮師其薄於
punctuated: 皇上敬一之訓求之思也乎？孔子曰：「文莫吾猶人也，躬行君子，則吾未之有得。」聖人匪抑文也，固不貴言也。不然，則爾蜀先哲長卿、淵、雲，縱橫詞賦，搜剔玄微，文非不工也，而君子至今訾之。神禹左準繩，右規矩，不專尚文，而天地平成之績，萬世永賴，何也？蘊之爲德行，行之爲事業，措之爲文辭，一以貫之者也。顏淵曰：「舜何人也？予何人也？有爲者亦若是。」爾多士鑒於神禹之不自滿假，而昌言是諮，師其薄於
translation_en: …in seeking and reflecting upon His Majesty’s instruction to “revere the One”? Confucius said: “In literary learning, perhaps I am the equal of others; but as for putting the conduct of a gentleman into practice, I have not yet attained it.” The sage was not disparaging literary accomplishment; he certainly did not prize words alone. Otherwise, consider the earlier worthies of your own Shu: Changqing, Yuan, and Yun—that is, Sima Xiangru, Wang Bao, and Yang Xiong. They ranged freely through lyric poetry and rhapsodies, probing the abstruse and subtle. Their writing was certainly accomplished, yet gentlemen criticize them to this day. Divine Yu held the leveling instrument and marking cord in his left hand, the compass and square in his right. He did not esteem literary accomplishment alone, yet the achievement by which he brought Heaven and Earth into order has benefited all subsequent ages. Why is this? What is stored within becomes virtuous conduct; what is put into practice becomes achievement; what is expressed becomes literary composition. One principle runs through them all. Yan Yuan said: “What sort of man was Shun? What sort of man am I? Whoever strives can become like him.” You assembled scholars should take as your mirror Divine Yu’s refusal to grow complacent or conceited and his seeking out sound counsel, and emulate his frugality in …

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
自奉而利欲是戒嚴危微之
辨繹精一之旨以求佩服我
皇上敬一之訓而諸子之末技弗
襲焉則有以明乎克艱厥臣
之義而他日熈載亮工功不
在禹下矣兹邦家之光亦有
司之慶也爾多士遭逢
===
明盛日近
耿光忍自負乎哉兹舉也大理寺
正皮〔東山〕以恤刑適至樂觀
賓興之典右參議劉〔儒〕僉事
喬〔世寧〕都指揮僉事蕭〔鼐〕又
皆先期入
賀夙與賛襄之勞者也法得併
punctuated:
自奉而利欲是戒，嚴危微之辨，繹精一之旨，以求佩服我皇上敬一之訓，而諸子之末技弗襲焉，則有以明乎克艱厥臣之義，而他日熈載亮工，功不在禹下矣。兹邦家之光，亦有司之慶也。爾多士遭逢明盛，日近耿光，忍自負乎哉？
兹舉也，大理寺正皮〔東山〕以恤刑適至，樂觀賓興之典。右參議劉〔儒〕、僉事喬〔世寧〕、都指揮僉事蕭〔鼐〕，又皆先期入賀，夙與賛襄之勞者也。法得併
translation_en:
…in his frugality in providing for himself, and guard against desires for profit. Draw a strict distinction between the precarious human mind and the subtle mind of the Way, and explore the meaning of refinement and single-mindedness, seeking thereby to take to heart and practice our Emperor’s teaching of reverent single-mindedness. If you refrain from copying the minor arts of the various philosophical masters, you will be able to understand what it means to shoulder the difficulties of serving as a minister. Then, in days to come, when you advance affairs and assist in accomplishing the work of government, your achievements will be no less than those of Yu. This will bring glory to the country and be a cause for rejoicing among the responsible officials. You scholars have encountered an enlightened and flourishing age and draw daily closer to the sovereign’s radiant virtue. Could you bear to fail yourselves?
On the occasion of this examination, Pi Dongshan 皮東山, Case Reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review, happened to arrive on a mission to review penal cases and gladly witnessed the ceremony of honoring and recommending worthy men. Liu Ru 劉儒, Right Assistant Administration Commissioner; Qiao Shining 喬世寧, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner; and Xiao Nai 蕭鼐, Assistant Regional Military Commissioner, also all arrived before the appointed date to offer congratulations. They had already shared in the labor of assisting with the proceedings. By established practice, they may be jointly…

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
書云
湖廣長沙府茶陵州儒學學
正周〔文龍〕謹序
punctuated:
書云。

湖廣長沙府茶陵州儒學學正周〔文龍〕謹序。
translation_en:
…recorded here.

Preface respectfully composed by Zhou Wenlong 周文龍, Instructor in the Confucian School of Chaling Subprefecture, Changsha Prefecture, Huguang.

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試
監臨官
巡按四川監察御史袁鳳鳴〔子時湖廣辰州衛官籍 直隸盱眙縣人戊戌進士〕
提調官
四川等處承宣布政使司左布政使嚴時泰〔應階湖廣江夏縣籍浙 江餘姚縣人辛未進士〕
四川等處承宣布政使司左叅政李義壯〔稚大廣東南海縣人 癸未進士〕
監試官
四川等處提刑按察司按察使紀　常〔元正順天府文安縣人 丙戌進士〕
四川等處提刑按察司副使沈應龍〔翔卿浙江烏程縣人 乙未進士〕
===
考試官
湖廣長沙府茶陵州儒學學正周文龍〔應乾江西南昌縣人 庚子貢士〕
河南開封府太康縣儒學教諭李鴻漸〔于磐山西蒲州人 甲午貢士〕
同考試官
浙江處州府宣平縣儒學教諭翟宗魯〔一東廣東博羅縣人 辛卯貢士〕
江西饒州府萬年縣儒學教諭吳雲臺〔文相福建莆田縣人 辛卯貢士〕
河南南陽府裕州葉縣儒學教諭艾　儒〔宗道江西崇仁縣人 庚子貢士〕
直隸寧國府太平縣儒學教諭朱　梧〔子容福建晉江縣人 丁酉貢士〕
應天府六合縣儒學教諭王　鎮〔國柱福建閩縣籍福 州右衛人庚子貢士〕
punctuated:
嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試。

監臨官：
巡按四川監察御史袁鳳鳴〔子時，湖廣辰州衛官籍，直隸盱眙縣人，戊戌進士〕。

提調官：
四川等處承宣布政使司左布政使嚴時泰〔應階，湖廣江夏縣籍，浙 江餘姚縣人，辛未進士〕。
四川等處承宣布政使司左叅政李義壯〔稚大，廣東南海縣人，癸未進士〕。

監試官：
四川等處提刑按察司按察使紀　常〔元正，順天府文安縣人，丙戌進士〕。
四川等處提刑按察司副使沈應龍〔翔卿，浙江烏程縣人，乙未進士〕。

考試官：
湖廣長沙府茶陵州儒學學正周文龍〔應乾，江西南昌縣人，庚子貢士〕。
河南開封府太康縣儒學教諭李鴻漸〔于磐，山西蒲州人，甲午貢士〕。

同考試官：
浙江處州府宣平縣儒學教諭翟宗魯〔一東，廣東博羅縣人，辛卯貢士〕。
江西饒州府萬年縣儒學教諭吳雲臺〔文相，福建莆田縣人，辛卯貢士〕。
河南南陽府裕州葉縣儒學教諭艾　儒〔宗道，江西崇仁縣人，庚子貢士〕。
直隸寧國府太平縣儒學教諭朱　梧〔子容，福建晉江縣人，丁酉貢士〕。
應天府六合縣儒學教諭王　鎮〔國柱，福建閩縣籍，福 州右衛人，庚子貢士〕。
translation_en:
Sichuan Provincial Examination, the twenty-fifth year of Jiajing (1546).

Supervising Official:
Yuan Fengming, Regional Inspecting Censor for Sichuan, courtesy name Zishi, held official registration in Chenzhou Guard, Huguang, and was a native of Xuyi County in the directly administered metropolitan region (Zhili). He became a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) in the wuxu year.

Proctors:
Yan Shitai, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Sichuan, courtesy name Yingjie, was registered in Jiangxia County, Huguang, and was a native of Yuyao County, Zhejiang. He became a metropolitan graduate in the xinwei year.
Li Yizhuang, Left Administration Vice Commissioner of Sichuan, courtesy name Zhida, was a native of Nanhai County, Guangdong. He became a metropolitan graduate in the guiwei year.

Examination Oversight Officials:
Ji Chang, Surveillance Commissioner of Sichuan, courtesy name Yuanzheng, was a native of Wen’an County, Shuntian Prefecture. He became a metropolitan graduate in the bingxu year.
Shen Yinglong, Surveillance Vice Commissioner of Sichuan, courtesy name Xiangqing, was a native of Wucheng County, Zhejiang. He became a metropolitan graduate in the yiwei year.

Examiners:
Zhou Wenlong, Instructor at the Confucian School of Chaling Subprefecture, Changsha Prefecture, Huguang, courtesy name Yingqian, was a native of Nanchang County, Jiangxi. He became a tribute scholar (gongshi) in the gengzi year.
Li Hongjian, Instructor at the Confucian School of Taikang County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, courtesy name Yupan, was a native of Puzhou, Shanxi. He became a tribute scholar in the jiawu year.

Associate Examiners:
Zhai Zonglu, Instructor at the Confucian School of Xuanping County, Chuzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, courtesy name Yidong, was a native of Boluo County, Guangdong. He became a tribute scholar in the xinmao year.
Wu Yuntai, Instructor at the Confucian School of Wannian County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, courtesy name Wenxiang, was a native of Putian County, Fujian. He became a tribute scholar in the xinmao year.
Ai Ru, Instructor at the Confucian School of Ye County, Yuzhou Subprefecture, Nanyang Prefecture, Henan, courtesy name Zongdao, was a native of Chongren County, Jiangxi. He became a tribute scholar in the gengzi year.
Zhu Wu, Instructor at the Confucian School of Taiping County, Ningguo Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region (Zhili), courtesy name Zirong, was a native of Jinjiang County, Fujian. He became a tribute scholar in the dingyou year.
Wang Zhen, Instructor at the Confucian School of Liuhe County, Yingtian Prefecture, courtesy name Guozhu, was registered in Min County, Fujian, and was a native of Fuzhou Right Guard. He became a tribute scholar in the gengzi year.

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
江西饒州府浮梁縣儒學教諭張價〔席珍湖廣廣濟縣人 庚子貢士〕
印卷官
四川布政使司經歷司經歷忽雲漢〔天章陝西富平縣人 監生〕
四川按察司經歷司經歷趙漢〔子倬直隸沛縣人 監生〕
收掌試卷官
成都府知府馬九德〔吉甫直隸德州衛人 乙未進士〕
保寧府知府南逢吉〔元貞陝西渭南縣人 戊戌進士〕
順慶府知府錢泮〔鳴教直隸常熟縣人 乙未進士〕
重慶府知府劉繪〔子素河南光州人 乙未進士〕
===
敘州府知府陳天資〔汝學廣東饒平縣人 乙未進士〕
夔州府知府許應元〔子春浙江錢塘縣人 壬辰進士〕
受卷官
夔州府同知劉楷〔汝範直隸完縣人 癸酉貢士〕
成都府推官任瓚〔北下陝西臨潼縣人 甲辰進士〕
夔州府達州同知羅椿枝〔日新浙江桐廬縣人 乙未進士〕
夔州府奉節縣知縣趙鳴鳳〔子和貴州普定衛籍 直隸崑山縣人辛卯貢士〕
敘州府富順縣知縣嚴清〔直甫雲南後衛籍浙 江嘉興縣人甲辰進士〕
成都府新津縣知縣楊錫文〔禹疇雲南安寧州人 丁酉貢士〕
punctuated:
江西饒州府浮梁縣儒學教諭張價〔席珍，湖廣廣濟縣人，庚子貢士〕。

印卷官：四川布政使司經歷司經歷忽雲漢〔天章，陝西富平縣人，監生〕。四川按察司經歷司經歷趙漢〔子倬，直隸沛縣人，監生〕。

收掌試卷官：成都府知府馬九德〔吉甫，直隸德州衛人，乙未進士〕。保寧府知府南逢吉〔元貞，陝西渭南縣人，戊戌進士〕。順慶府知府錢泮〔鳴教，直隸常熟縣人，乙未進士〕。重慶府知府劉繪〔子素，河南光州人，乙未進士〕。敘州府知府陳天資〔汝學，廣東饒平縣人，乙未進士〕。夔州府知府許應元〔子春，浙江錢塘縣人，壬辰進士〕。

受卷官：夔州府同知劉楷〔汝範，直隸完縣人，癸酉貢士〕。成都府推官任瓚〔北下，陝西臨潼縣人，甲辰進士〕。夔州府達州同知羅椿枝〔日新，浙江桐廬縣人，乙未進士〕。夔州府奉節縣知縣趙鳴鳳〔子和，貴州普定衛籍，直隸崑山縣人，辛卯貢士〕。敘州府富順縣知縣嚴清〔直甫，雲南後衛籍，浙江嘉興縣人，甲辰進士〕。成都府新津縣知縣楊錫文〔禹疇，雲南安寧州人，丁酉貢士〕。
translation_en:
Zhang Jia, Instructor in the Confucian School of Fuliang County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, had the courtesy name Xizhen. He was from Guangji County, Huguang, and was a tribute scholar (gongshi) of the gengzi year.

Officials responsible for printing examination papers:
Hu Yunhan, Registrar in the Registry of the Sichuan Provincial Administration Commission, had the courtesy name Tianzhang. He was from Fuping County, Shaanxi, and was an Imperial Academy student.
Zhao Han, Registrar in the Registry of the Sichuan Provincial Surveillance Commission, had the courtesy name Zizhuo. He was from Pei County, Zhili, and was an Imperial Academy student.

Officials responsible for collecting and keeping examination scripts:
Ma Jiude, Prefect of Chengdu, had the courtesy name Jifu. He was from Dezhou Guard, Zhili, and was a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the yiwei year.
Nan Fengji, Prefect of Baoning, had the courtesy name Yuanzhen. He was from Weinan County, Shaanxi, and was a metropolitan graduate of the wuxu year.
Qian Pan, Prefect of Shunqing, had the courtesy name Mingjiao. He was from Changshu County, Zhili, and was a metropolitan graduate of the yiwei year.
Liu Hui, Prefect of Chongqing, had the courtesy name Zisu. He was from Guangzhou Subprefecture, Henan, and was a metropolitan graduate of the yiwei year.
Chen Tianzi, Prefect of Xuzhou, had the courtesy name Ruxue. He was from Raoping County, Guangdong, and was a metropolitan graduate of the yiwei year.
Xu Yingyuan, Prefect of Kuizhou, had the courtesy name Zichun. He was from Qiantang County, Zhejiang, and was a metropolitan graduate of the renchen year.

Officials responsible for receiving examination scripts:
Liu Kai, Vice Prefect of Kuizhou, had the courtesy name Rufan. He was from Wan County, Zhili, and was a tribute scholar (gongshi) of the guiyou year.
Ren Zan, Prefectural Judge of Chengdu, had the courtesy name Beixia [?]. He was from Lintong County, Shaanxi, and was a metropolitan graduate of the jiachen year.
Luo Chunzhi, Vice Magistrate of Dazhou Subprefecture, Kuizhou Prefecture, had the courtesy name Rixin. He was from Tonglu County, Zhejiang, and was a metropolitan graduate of the yiwei year.
Zhao Mingfeng, Magistrate of Fengjie County, Kuizhou Prefecture, had the courtesy name Zihe. He was registered with Puding Guard, Guizhou, was originally from Kunshan County, Zhili, and was a tribute scholar of the xinmao year.
Yan Qing, Magistrate of Fushun County, Xuzhou Prefecture, had the courtesy name Zhifu. He was registered with Yunnan Rear Guard, was originally from Jiaxing County, Zhejiang, and was a metropolitan graduate of the jiachen year.
Yang Xiwen, Magistrate of Xinjin County, Chengdu Prefecture, had the courtesy name Yuchou. He was from Anning Subprefecture, Yunnan, and was a tribute scholar of the dingyou year.

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
潼川州安岳縣知縣董性〔原善湖廣麻城縣人 丁酉貢士〕
彌封官
順慶府推官何海晏〔治象山東平陰縣人 甲辰進士〕
重慶府涪州彭水縣知縣吳鳳〔時鳴江西貴溪縣人 壬午貢士〕
成都府資陽縣知縣潘大武〔宗周貴州普定衛籍直 隸無錫縣人戊子貢士〕
順慶府南充縣知縣鄒星〔景昭雲南臨安衛籍江 西新淦縣人辛卯貢士〕
重慶府巴縣知縣胡良臣〔汝鄰湖廣松滋縣人 甲午貢士〕
雅州蘆山縣知縣史筆〔公甫雲南曲靖衛籍 河南汝州人甲午貢士〕
謄錄官
===
成都府漢州知州劉琮〔仲采江西安福縣人 官生〕
夔州府達州知州楊振文〔宗周貴州前衛人 壬午貢士〕
夔州府巫山縣知縣劉昇〔誠之湖廣監利縣人 辛卯貢士〕
成都府雙流縣知縣舒魁〔應奎貴州思州府人 戊子貢士〕
敘州府宜賓縣知縣呂鳳來〔致甫雲南人羅衛籍 浙江蕭山縣人甲午貢士〕
重慶府黔江縣知縣䍐源〔子濬建昌儀衛司籍 監生〕
對讀官
成都府同知高登〔應明貴州威清衛官 籍直隸儀真縣人酉貢士〕
潼川州知州楊謨〔汝承山西澤州籍大 同縣人辛丑進士〕
punctuated:
潼川州安岳縣知縣董性〔原善，湖廣麻城縣人，丁酉貢士〕。

彌封官：
順慶府推官何海晏〔治象，山東平陰縣人，甲辰進士〕。重慶府涪州彭水縣知縣吳鳳〔時鳴，江西貴溪縣人，壬午貢士〕。成都府資陽縣知縣潘大武〔宗周，貴州普定衛籍，直隸無錫縣人，戊子貢士〕。順慶府南充縣知縣鄒星〔景昭，雲南臨安衛籍，江西新淦縣人，辛卯貢士〕。重慶府巴縣知縣胡良臣〔汝鄰，湖廣松滋縣人，甲午貢士〕。雅州蘆山縣知縣史筆〔公甫，雲南曲靖衛籍，河南汝州人，甲午貢士〕。

謄錄官：
成都府漢州知州劉琮〔仲采，江西安福縣人，官生〕。夔州府達州知州楊振文〔宗周，貴州前衛人，壬午貢士〕。夔州府巫山縣知縣劉昇〔誠之，湖廣監利縣人，辛卯貢士〕。成都府雙流縣知縣舒魁〔應奎，貴州思州府人，戊子貢士〕。敘州府宜賓縣知縣呂鳳來〔致甫，雲南人羅衛籍，浙江蕭山縣人，甲午貢士〕。重慶府黔江縣知縣䍐源〔子濬，建昌儀衛司籍，監生〕。

對讀官：
成都府同知高登〔應明，貴州威清衛官籍，直隸儀真縣人，酉貢士〕。潼川州知州楊謨〔汝承，山西澤州籍，大同縣人，辛丑進士〕。
translation_en:
Dong Xing, Magistrate of Anyue County in Tongchuan Department, had the courtesy name Yuanshan and was from Macheng County, Huguang. He was a tribute scholar (gongshi) of the dingyou year.

Officials for Sealing Candidates’ Names:
He Haiyan, Prefectural Judge of Shunqing Prefecture, had the courtesy name Zhixiang and was from Pingyin County, Shandong. He was a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the jiachen year.
Wu Feng, Magistrate of Pengshui County in Fuzhou Department, Chongqing Prefecture, had the courtesy name Shiming and was from Guixi County, Jiangxi. He was a tribute scholar of the renwu year.
Pan Dawu, Magistrate of Ziyang County in Chengdu Prefecture, had the courtesy name Zongzhou. He was registered with Puding Guard in Guizhou, was from Wuxi County in the directly administered metropolitan region, and was a tribute scholar of the wuzi year.
Zou Xing, Magistrate of Nanchong County in Shunqing Prefecture, had the courtesy name Jingzhao. He was registered with Lin’an Guard in Yunnan, was from Xingan County, Jiangxi, and was a tribute scholar of the xinmao year.
Hu Liangchen, Magistrate of Ba County in Chongqing Prefecture, had the courtesy name Rulin and was from Songzi County, Huguang. He was a tribute scholar of the jiawu year.
Shi Bi, Magistrate of Lushan County in Yazhou Department, had the courtesy name Gongfu. He was registered with Qujing Guard in Yunnan, was from Ruzhou Department, Henan, and was a tribute scholar of the jiawu year.

Transcription Officials:
Liu Cong, Magistrate of Hanzhou Department in Chengdu Prefecture, had the courtesy name Zhongcai and was from Anfu County, Jiangxi. He was a student admitted through official privilege.
Yang Zhenwen, Magistrate of Dazhou Department in Kuizhou Prefecture, had the courtesy name Zongzhou and was from Guizhou Front Guard. He was a tribute scholar of the renwu year.
Liu Sheng, Magistrate of Wushan County in Kuizhou Prefecture, had the courtesy name Chengzhi and was from Jianli County, Huguang. He was a tribute scholar of the xinmao year.
Shu Kui, Magistrate of Shuangliu County in Chengdu Prefecture, had the courtesy name Yingkui and was from Sizhou Prefecture, Guizhou. He was a tribute scholar of the wuzi year.
Lü Fenglai, Magistrate of Yibin County in Xuzhou Prefecture, had the courtesy name Zhifu. He was registered with Renluo Guard [?] in Yunnan, was from Xiaoshan County, Zhejiang, and was a tribute scholar of the jiawu year.
Han Yuan (䍐源), Magistrate of Qianjiang County in Chongqing Prefecture, had the courtesy name Zijun. He was registered with the Jianchang Ceremonial Guard Office and was a student of the Imperial Academy.

Proofreading Officials:
Gao Deng, Vice Prefect of Chengdu Prefecture, had the courtesy name Yingming. He held official household registration with Weiqing Guard in Guizhou, was from Yizhen County in the directly administered metropolitan region, and was a tribute scholar of a you year [the first character of the cyclical year is missing].
Yang Mo, Magistrate of Tongchuan Department, had the courtesy name Rucheng. He was registered in Zezhou Department, Shanxi, was from Datong County, and was a metropolitan graduate of the xinchou year.

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
唯天爲大唯堯則之
大哉聖人之道洋洋乎發育萬物峻極于
天優優大哉禮儀三百威儀三千待其
人而後行故曰苟不至德至道不凝焉
詩曰天生蒸民有物有則民之秉夷好是
懿德孔子曰爲此詩者其知道乎故有
物必有則民之秉夷也故好是懿德
===
易
文言曰元者善之長也亨者嘉之會也利
者義之和也貞者事之幹也君子體仁
足以長人嘉會足以合禮利物足以和
義貞固足以幹事君子行此四德者故
曰乾元亨利貞
象曰元吉在上大成也
夫易聖人所以崇德而廣業也知崇禮卑
崇效天卑法地
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

唯天爲大，唯堯則之。

大哉，聖人之道！洋洋乎，發育萬物，峻極于天！優優大哉！禮儀三百，威儀三千，待其人而後行。故曰：「苟不至德，至道不凝焉。」

詩曰：「天生蒸民，有物有則。民之秉夷，好是懿德。」孔子曰：「爲此詩者，其知道乎！」故有物必有則，民之秉夷也，故好是懿德。

易

文言曰：「元者，善之長也；亨者，嘉之會也；利者，義之和也；貞者，事之幹也。君子體仁，足以長人；嘉會，足以合禮；利物，足以和義；貞固，足以幹事。君子行此四德者，故曰：『乾，元亨利貞。』」

象曰：「元吉在上，大成也。」

夫易，聖人所以崇德而廣業也。知崇禮卑，崇效天，卑法地。
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

Heaven alone is great; Yao alone took it as his model.

Great indeed is the Way of the sage! Vast and flowing, it brings forth and nourishes the myriad things and rises to the utmost height of Heaven! How abundant and great! The three hundred rules of ceremony and the three thousand rules of deportment await the right person before they can be put into practice. Thus it is said: “Unless virtue reaches its utmost perfection, the utmost Way cannot become firmly established.”

The Book of Odes says: “Heaven gives birth to the multitude of people; for every thing there is a norm. The people hold fast to their constant nature and love this admirable virtue.” Confucius said: “The author of this ode surely understood the Way!” Thus, wherever there is a thing, there must be a norm. Because the people hold fast to their constant nature, they love this admirable virtue.

Book of Changes

The Commentary on the Words of the Text says: “The primal is foremost among all that is good; success is the coming together of excellence; benefit is the harmony of righteousness; firmness is the mainstay of affairs. The noble man embodies benevolence and is thereby able to lead others; he brings excellence together and is thereby able to accord with ritual propriety; he benefits things and is thereby able to harmonize with righteousness; he is steadfast and firm and is thereby able to manage affairs. The noble man practices these four virtues. Thus it is said: ‘Qian: primal, successful, beneficial, and firm.’”

The Commentary on the Images says: “‘Supreme good fortune’ in the upper position signifies great accomplishment.

The Book of Changes is that by which the sages exalt their virtue and broaden their achievements. Wisdom is lofty, while ritual propriety is humble. The lofty emulates Heaven; the humble models itself on Earth.

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
聖人南面而聽天下嚮明而治蓋取諸此
也
書
水火金木土穀惟修正德利用厚生惟和
五百里甸服百里賦納總二百里納銍三
百里納秸服四百里粟五百里米
惟助成王德顯越尹人祗辟
爾克敬典在德時乃罔不變允升于大猷
詩
===
于以盛之維筐及筥于以湘之維錡及釜
允矣君子展也大成
荏菽旆旆禾役穟穟麻麥幪幪瓜瓞唪唪
商之先后受命不殆在武丁孫子武丁孫
子武王靡不勝龍旂十乘大糦是承邦
畿千里維民所止肇域彼四海四海來
假來假祁祁景員維河殷受命咸宜百
祿是何
春秋
punctuated:
聖人南面而聽天下，嚮明而治，蓋取諸此也。

書
水火金木土穀惟修，正德利用厚生惟和。
五百里甸服：百里賦納總，二百里納銍，三百里納秸服，四百里粟，五百里米。
惟助成王德，顯越尹人，祗辟。
爾克敬典在德，時乃罔不變，允升于大猷。

詩
于以盛之？維筐及筥。于以湘之？維錡及釜。
允矣君子，展也大成。
荏菽旆旆，禾役穟穟，麻麥幪幪，瓜瓞唪唪。
商之先后，受命不殆，在武丁孫子。武丁孫子，武王靡不勝。龍旂十乘，大糦是承。邦畿千里，維民所止。肇域彼四海，四海來假。來假祁祁，景員維河。殷受命咸宜，百祿是何。

春秋
translation_en:
The sage faces south to hear the affairs of all under Heaven, turning toward the light to govern: this is presumably where he took the example.

Book of Documents
Water, fire, metal, wood, earth, and grain must be properly managed; rectifying virtue, making resources useful, and enriching the people’s livelihood must be brought into harmony.
The royal domain extends five hundred li. Within the first hundred li, the levy is delivered as grain with its stalks; within the second hundred, as cut ears; within the third hundred, as grain on shortened stalks; within the fourth hundred, as unhusked grain; and within the fifth hundred, as husked grain.
Help perfect the king’s virtue, make it manifest, govern the people, and reverently serve the sovereign.
If you can reverently uphold the established norms through virtue, then none will fail to be transformed, and you will truly advance to the great Way.

Book of Odes
In what shall we put them? In square baskets and round baskets. In what shall we boil them? In tripod cauldrons and cooking pots.
Trustworthy indeed is the gentleman; truly, he has achieved great perfection.
The beans grow luxuriantly; the grain hangs heavy with ears [?]; hemp and wheat grow thickly; gourds large and small abound.
The former kings of Shang received the mandate without peril; it rests with the descendants of Wuding. The descendants of Wuding, martial kings, conquer all. Ten chariots bear dragon banners and present the great sacrificial offerings. The royal domain extends a thousand li: here the people dwell. They established boundaries throughout the lands within the Four Seas, and from the Four Seas people come to pay homage. In multitudes they come to pay homage; their territory extends far, to the Yellow River. Yin received the mandate in full fitness, bearing every blessing.

Spring and Autumn Annals

邾子齊世子光己未同盟于雞澤〔襄公〕
三年
晉人齊人宋人衛人鄭人曹人莒人邾人
滕人薛人杞人小邾人會于澶淵〔襄公〕
三十年
===
三十年三月公會劉子晉侯宋公蔡侯
衛侯陳子鄭伯許男曹伯莒子邾子頓
子胡子滕子薛伯杞伯小邾子齊國夏
于召陵侵楚〔定公四年〕
禮記
忠信禮之本也義理禮之文也
是故樂在宗廟之中君臣上下同聽之則
莫不和敬

punctuated:
十有一月，衛侯朔出奔齊。〔桓公十有六年〕
楚人使宜申來獻捷。十有二月癸丑，公會諸侯盟于薄，釋宋公。〔俱僖公二十有〕一年。

晉人、齊人、宋人、衛人、鄭人、曹人、莒人、邾人、滕人、薛人、杞人、小邾人會于澶淵。〔襄公〕三十年。
三十年，三月，公會劉子、晉侯、宋公、蔡侯、衛侯、陳子、鄭伯、許男、曹伯、莒子、邾子、頓子、胡子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子、齊國夏于召陵，侵楚。〔定公四年〕
禮記
忠信，禮之本也；義理，禮之文也。
是故樂在宗廟之中，君臣上下同聽之，則莫不和敬。
民以君爲心，君以民爲體。
translation_en:
In the eleventh month, Shuo, Marquis of Wei, fled to Qi. [Sixteenth year of Duke Huan.]

The men of Chu sent Yishen to present the spoils of victory. In the twelfth month, on the guichou day, the Duke met the feudal lords and made a covenant at Bo; they released the Duke of Song. [Both entries: twenty-first year of Duke Xi.]

In the sixth month, the Duke met the Viscount of Shan, the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, and Guang, heir apparent of Qi. On the jiwei day, they jointly entered into a covenant at Jize. [Third year of Duke Xiang.]

Men of Jin, Qi, Song, Wei, Zheng, Cao, Ju, Zhu, Teng, Xue, Qi 杞, and Xiao Zhu met at Chanyuan. [Thirtieth year of Duke Xiang.]

In the thirtieth year [?], in the third month, the Duke met the Viscount of Liu, the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Cai, the Marquis of Wei, the Viscount of Chen, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, the Earl of Cao, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Dun, the Viscount of Hu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi 杞, the Viscount of Xiao Zhu, and Guo Xia of Qi 齊 at Shaoling, and they invaded Chu. [Fourth year of Duke Ding. The opening “thirtieth year” appears to be a duplicated date.]

Record of Rites (Liji)

Loyalty and trustworthiness are the foundation of ritual; righteousness and proper order are its outward expression.

Therefore, when music is performed within the ancestral temple and ruler and ministers, superiors and inferiors, listen to it together, none fails to become harmonious and reverent.

The people take their ruler as their heart; the ruler takes the people as his body.

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
古之制禮也經之以天地紀之以日月參
之以三光政教之本也
第貳場
論
至誠賛天地之化育
詔誥表〔内科一道〕
擬漢定振窮養老之令詔〔文帝元年〕
擬唐以房玄齡杜如晦爲僕射魏徵爲秘
書監誥〔貞觀三年〕
===
擬翰林學士承旨兼吏部尚書詹同等
進
大明日曆表〔洪武七年〕

古之制禮也，經之以天地，紀之以日月，參之以三光，政教之本也。

第貳場

論：至誠賛天地之化育。

詔誥表〔内科一道〕

translation_en:
When the ancients established ritual, they took Heaven and Earth as its guiding framework, the sun and moon as its ordering principles, and the three luminaries as its further reference. This was the foundation of government and instruction.

Second Session

Discourse: Utmost sincerity assists the transforming and nourishing work of Heaven and Earth.

Edicts, proclamations, and memorials 〔One question from these categories [?].〕
Compose an edict in the voice of the Han emperor establishing regulations for relieving the destitute and supporting the elderly. 〔First year of Emperor Wen’s reign.〕
Compose a proclamation in the voice of the Tang emperor appointing Fang Xuanling and Du Ruhui as Vice Directors of the Department of State Affairs, and Wei Zheng as Director of the Palace Library. 〔Third year of Zhenguan.〕
Compose a memorial in the voice of Zhan Tong, Hanlin Academician Recipient of Edicts and concurrently Minister of Personnel, and his colleagues, presenting the Daily Record of the Great Ming. 〔Seventh year of Hongwu.〕

Legal Judgments 〔Five items.〕
Credential tablets.
Paper-currency regulations.
Sacrificial offerings.
Nighttime curfew.
Appeals bypassing the prescribed judicial hierarchy.

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
第叅場
策〔五道〕
問千聖傳心之要法尚矣我
太祖高皇帝嘗語侍臣曾魯曰朕求古帝王之
治莫盛於堯舜觀其授受其要在允執
厥中
成祖文皇帝又製爲聖學心法一書首以君道
父道子道臣道而揭其綱其下分而爲
目有統言者有專言者而後心學粲然
大明於世可一一聞其詳乎自昔虞廷
===
惟君臣相爲授受而已有非他人所能
與者今君道臣道之外而又列爲父道
子道何也
聖序首曰古之帝王平治天下有至要之道詒
訓子孫有不易之法而尤獨有取於唐
帝範之十二篇
聖意果安在耶不知所謂道與法云者其一以
貫之耶抑分而爲二耶恭惟
punctuated:
第叅場
策〔五道〕
問：千聖傳心之要法尚矣。我太祖高皇帝嘗語侍臣曾魯曰：「朕求古帝王之治，莫盛於堯舜。觀其授受，其要在允執厥中。」成祖文皇帝又製爲《聖學心法》一書，首以君道、父道、子道、臣道而揭其綱，其下分而爲目，有統言者，有專言者，而後心學粲然大明於世。可一一聞其詳乎？自昔虞廷，惟君臣相爲授受而已，有非他人所能與者。今君道、臣道之外，而又列爲父道、子道，何也？聖序首曰：「古之帝王平治天下，有至要之道；詒訓子孫，有不易之法。」而尤獨有取於唐《帝範》之十二篇，聖意果安在耶？不知所謂道與法云者，其一以貫之耶？抑分而爲二耶？恭惟
translation_en:
Third Session
Policy Questions〔Five〕
Question: The essential method by which the myriad sages transmitted the mind is ancient indeed. Our Emperor Taizu Gao once said to his attendant official Zeng Lu: “When I examine the governance of the ancient emperors and kings, none surpasses that of Yao and Shun. Looking at what they transmitted and received, its essence lies in sincerely holding fast to the Mean.” Emperor Chengzu Wen also composed a book, Essential Methods of the Sages’ Learning (Shengxue xinfa). At its beginning, he set out its framework under the Way of the ruler, the Way of the father, the Way of the son, and the Way of the minister. Beneath these he arranged subdivisions, some treating matters comprehensively and others treating particular subjects. Thereafter, the learning of the mind shone forth brilliantly in the world. Can you explain its details one by one?
In the ancient court of Shun, transmission and reception took place only between ruler and minister; there were matters in which others could not participate. Why, then, are the Way of the father and the Way of the son now set alongside the Way of the ruler and the Way of the minister?
The imperial preface begins: “The emperors and kings of antiquity had a supremely essential Way for bringing peace and order to All under Heaven, and unchanging methods for bequeathing instruction to their descendants.” Yet it singles out for particular approval the twelve chapters of the Tang work A Model for Emperors (Difan). What precisely was the imperial intention? Are what are called the Way and the methods pervaded by a single principle, or are they divided into two distinct things? We reverently consider…

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
皇上卽位之初首揭敬一數錫群工實與虞廷
互相表裏不知揆之
聖學心法之旨其亦有同乎否耶諸士涵濡
聖化蓋亦有年願鋪張而揚厲之以爲
今日緝熙之助
問學者始而爲士終而爲聖人期必如是
而已自此學不講而士之趨於異端者
紛如也有宋諸賢彙興相與印證其說
然其微辭奥旨間有不同使人不能無
===
可疑者如曰道爲太極矣又曰心爲太
極曰一起於震矣又曰一起於乾曰有
主則虛矣又曰有主則實曰收之使入
矣又曰推之使出曰仁者愛之體矣又
曰惟公可以近之曰義者仁之用矣又
曰義者仁之質曰君子愼動矣又曰惟
靜可以爲學曰學貴力行矣又曰進學
以致知爲先曰定性矣又曰只當作定
心看曰形而後有氣質之性矣又曰二
punctuated:
皇上卽位之初，首揭敬一，數錫群工，實與虞廷互相表裏。不知揆之聖學心法之旨，其亦有同乎否耶？諸士涵濡聖化，蓋亦有年，願鋪張而揚厲之，以爲今日緝熙之助。

問：學者始而爲士，終而爲聖人，期必如是而已。自此學不講，而士之趨於異端者紛如也。有宋諸賢彙興，相與印證其說，然其微辭奥旨間有不同，使人不能無可疑者。如曰：「道爲太極矣。」又曰：「心爲太極。」曰：「一起於震矣。」又曰：「一起於乾。」曰：「有主則虛矣。」又曰：「有主則實。」曰：「收之使入矣。」又曰：「推之使出。」曰：「仁者，愛之體矣。」又曰：「惟公可以近之。」曰：「義者，仁之用矣。」又曰：「義者，仁之質。」曰：「君子愼動矣。」又曰：「惟靜可以爲學。」曰：「學貴力行矣。」又曰：「進學以致知爲先。」曰：「定性矣。」又曰：「只當作定心看。」曰：「形而後有氣質之性矣。」又曰：「二
translation_en:
…At the beginning of His Majesty’s reign, he first proclaimed “reverent unity” and repeatedly bestowed this teaching upon the assembled officials. This indeed complements the teachings of Shun’s court. Measured against the purport of the mind-method of sagely learning, does it likewise accord with it or not? You candidates have been steeped in the transforming influence of His Majesty for many years. We ask you to expound and celebrate this teaching, thereby assisting the continuing cultivation of luminous virtue today.

Question: Those who pursue learning begin as scholars and ultimately become sages: this alone must be their goal. Since this learning ceased to be expounded, scholars have flocked to heterodox teachings. The worthies of the Song arose together and mutually confirmed their explanations. Yet their subtle formulations and profound meanings sometimes differ, leaving readers with points of doubt. For example, one says, “The Way is the Supreme Ultimate,” while another says, “The mind is the Supreme Ultimate.” One says, “The One begins in Zhen,” while another says, “The One begins in Qian.” One says, “With a governing principle, the mind is empty,” while another says, “With a governing principle, the mind is full.” One says, “Gather it and bring it inward,” while another says, “Extend it and bring it outward.” One says, “Benevolence is the substance of love,” while another says, “Only through impartiality can one approach it.” One says, “Righteousness is the functioning of benevolence,” while another says, “Righteousness is the substance of benevolence.” One says, “The gentleman is cautious in activity,” while another says, “Only through stillness can one pursue learning.” One says, “Learning prizes vigorous practice,” while another says, “In advancing one’s learning, extending knowledge comes first.” One speaks of “stabilizing the nature,” while another says, “This should simply be understood as stabilizing the mind.” One says, “Only after physical form exists is there a nature constituted by material endowment,” while another says, “To divide it in two…

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
之則不是凡此數者皆聖學之標的也
蓋嘗沉潛反覆亦有年矣求其致一卒
難湊泊不知諸儒之言其各有攸當否
乎又不知數言之中其孰爲第一義乎
子之先儒如張南軒魏鶴山輩正惟深
造於此者今其道固如在也願諸士其
詳言之以觀希聖之學
問昔之論治者謂天下根本在蜀蜀根本
在兵與民憂在民則不恤兵憂在兵則
===
不恤民是故合而一之當使愛根本如
愛吾命而後可國也蜀之軍民其在今
日水旱相仍賦役愈蹙饑者弗食勞者
弗息根本之撥誠有不忍言者今欲反
而求之以爲優恤之政則將何先耶或
曰邊事有三又曰急務有五其果然否
耶又不知數者之外其尚有遺論否耶
蜀以官名者由秦漢唐宋而來不爲少
矣其間卓然名世真可爲軍民之怙恃
punctuated:
之則不是」。凡此數者，皆聖學之標的也。蓋嘗沉潛反覆，亦有年矣，求其致一，卒難湊泊。不知諸儒之言，其各有攸當否乎？又不知數言之中，其孰爲第一義乎？子之先儒，如張南軒、魏鶴山輩，正惟深造於此者。今其道固如在也，願諸士其詳言之，以觀希聖之學。

問：昔之論治者謂天下根本在蜀，蜀根本在兵與民。憂在民則不恤兵，憂在兵則不恤民。是故合而一之，當使愛根本如愛吾命，而後可國也。蜀之軍民，其在今日，水旱相仍，賦役愈蹙，饑者弗食，勞者弗息，根本之撥，誠有不忍言者。今欲反而求之，以爲優恤之政，則將何先耶？或曰邊事有三，又曰急務有五，其果然否耶？又不知數者之外，其尚有遺論否耶？蜀以官名者，由秦漢唐宋而來，不爲少矣。其間卓然名世，真可爲軍民之怙恃
translation_en:
…to treat it as two is incorrect.” All these statements are guiding standards for the learning of the sages. I have immersed myself in them and pondered them repeatedly for years, yet in seeking to bring them into unity, I have ultimately found it difficult to arrive at a coherent understanding. Do the statements of these various Confucian scholars each have their particular application? And among these statements, which expresses the foremost principle? Your scholarly predecessors, such as Zhang Nanxuan and Wei Heshan, were precisely men who attained profound understanding in these matters. Their Way remains as though still present today. I ask you candidates to explain it in detail, so that we may observe your learning in aspiring to sagehood.

Question: Those who discussed government in former times said that the foundation of the realm lay in Shu, and the foundation of Shu lay in its soldiers and people. If concern centers on the people, the soldiers receive no care; if concern centers on the soldiers, the people receive no care. Thus the two must be united as one, and this foundation must be cherished as one cherishes one’s own life; only then can the state be governed. As for the soldiers and people of Shu today, floods and droughts follow one another, taxes and labor services press ever harder, the hungry go unfed, and the weary find no rest. The undermining of this foundation is truly something one cannot bear to speak of. If we now wish to turn back and seek a remedy through policies of generous relief, what should take precedence? Some say that there are three matters concerning the frontier, and also that there are five urgent tasks. Is this indeed so? Beyond these several matters, are there further considerations that have been overlooked? From the Qin and Han through the Tang and Song, no few men have won renown through service as officials in Shu. Among them were those who stood out in their age and could truly serve as a source of support and protection for soldiers and people…

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
而民到于今受其賜者可得聞乎樞機
品式今皆森載志乘流傳郡邑夫人能
知之亦能言之不知當時文武並用之
術寬猛相濟之宜張弛不悖之方軍民
合一之道果何如也夫有天下之慮者
必不屁於一方有萬世之圖者必不限
於一時願諸士其詳言之固執事者所
樂聞也
問水利鹽法屯田茶馬四者皆今日裕國
===
足邊之助其在于蜀則尤不可一日而
不之講者也
祖宗立法之初法有定則官有常員世守行之
較若畫一故在當時農有餘粟商有遺
利軍有宿儲馬有良乘尋常無事上下
相安卒遇有警備皆先具於乎盛矣其
後射利之徒奸究朋興倡邪說以奪正
議破常調以便私圖浸淫至于今日而
悉非其舊矣嘗稽載籍自昔講裕國足
punctuated:
而民到于今受其賜者，可得聞乎？樞機品式，今皆森載志乘，流傳郡邑，夫人能知之，亦能言之。不知當時文武並用之術、寬猛相濟之宜、張弛不悖之方、軍民合一之道，果何如也？夫有天下之慮者，必不屁於一方；有萬世之圖者，必不限於一時。願諸士其詳言之，固執事者所樂聞也。
問：水利、鹽法、屯田、茶馬四者，皆今日裕國足邊之助。其在于蜀，則尤不可一日而不之講者也。祖宗立法之初，法有定則，官有常員，世守行之，較若畫一。故在當時，農有餘粟，商有遺利，軍有宿儲，馬有良乘。尋常無事，上下相安；卒遇有警，備皆先具。於乎，盛矣！其後射利之徒，奸究朋興，倡邪說以奪正議，破常調以便私圖，浸淫至于今日，而悉非其舊矣。嘗稽載籍，自昔講裕國足
translation_en:
…and whose beneficence the people still enjoy today—may we hear of them? Their pivotal measures and administrative rules [?] are now amply recorded in gazetteers and transmitted throughout the prefectures and counties; everyone can know and discuss them. Yet what, precisely, were their methods of employing civil and military measures together, their appropriate balance of leniency and severity, their means of tightening and relaxing controls without contradiction, and their way of bringing soldiers and civilians into unity? Those who consider the concerns of all under Heaven surely do not confine themselves [?] to a single region; those who plan for ten thousand generations surely do not limit themselves to a single age. We hope that you gentlemen will explain these matters fully. This is certainly what those conducting this examination would gladly hear.
Question: Water management, salt administration, agricultural colonies, and the tea-for-horses trade are all means of enriching the state and adequately supplying the frontier today. In Shu especially, they cannot go even a day without attention. When our imperial ancestors first established these institutions, the laws had fixed standards and the offices had regular complements of officials. These were observed and implemented generation after generation, with clear and consistent uniformity. Thus, in those days, farmers had grain to spare, merchants retained profits, the army had accumulated reserves, and fine horses were available for service. In ordinary, peaceful times, superiors and subordinates lived in mutual security; if an alarm suddenly arose, all preparations had already been made. Ah, how flourishing it was! Subsequently, profit-seekers and bands of malefactors [?] arose, promoting pernicious doctrines to displace sound deliberations and breaking established arrangements to facilitate private schemes. These abuses have gradually spread down to the present day, until nothing remains as it was. I have examined the written records: since ancient times, in discussions of enriching the state and adequately supplying…

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
邊之策未有舍是四者往往行之皆臻
實用不知亦有同於我
祖宗之法之意否耶夫制而用之者法也推而
行之者人也玆欲導江以惠農牢盆以
通商鹽屯以治軍榷茶以市馬必如昔
人所謂制法而不制於法更化而不更
於化以求不失乎立法之初意不知何
脩而後可願與諸士究言之毋爲紛紛
邪說所惑斯可也
===
問蠻夷猾夏雖堯舜之世所不能免然古
今論致治者必首稱焉不知當時所以
制馭之道何如也我
太祖高皇帝監古法天弘基肇極爲萬世法於
番夷戎貊悉置酋長若衆衛然域以山
谿寬其法綱
聖意果安在耶邇者白草諸番歲有出沒至厪
皇上西顧之憂然觀之西南會要又以爲今日
諸番限隔大番之要道寔爲蜀部之藩
punctuated:
邊之策，未有舍是四者，往往行之，皆臻實用。不知亦有同於我祖宗之法之意否耶？夫制而用之者，法也；推而行之者，人也。玆欲導江以惠農，牢盆以通商，鹽屯以治軍，榷茶以市馬，必如昔人所謂制法而不制於法，更化而不更於化，以求不失乎立法之初意。不知何脩而後可？願與諸士究言之，毋爲紛紛邪說所惑，斯可也。

問：蠻夷猾夏，雖堯舜之世所不能免，然古今論致治者，必首稱焉。不知當時所以制馭之道何如也？我太祖高皇帝監古法天，弘基肇極，爲萬世法。於番夷戎貊，悉置酋長，若衆衛然，域以山谿，寬其法綱。聖意果安在耶？邇者白草諸番，歲有出沒，至厪皇上西顧之憂。然觀之《西南會要》，又以爲今日諸番限隔大番之要道，寔爲蜀部之藩
translation_en:
…plans for provisioning the frontier have never dispensed with these four measures. Whenever implemented, they have yielded practical benefits. Might their underlying intent also accord with the institutions of our imperial ancestors? Laws provide the framework for use; people extend them and put them into practice. Now, if we wish to channel the rivers to benefit agriculture, employ salt-boiling pans to facilitate commerce, use salt revenues and military agricultural colonies to maintain the army, and operate the tea monopoly to purchase horses, we must follow what men of old called “making laws without being constrained by laws, and instituting reforms without being changed by those reforms,” seeking thereby to preserve the original intent of the legislation. What must be put in order before this can be achieved? I wish you gentlemen to discuss this thoroughly. It will suffice if you do not let the profusion of pernicious doctrines mislead you.

Question: The disruption of the Chinese realm by the Man and Yi could not be avoided even in the age of Yao and Shun. Yet those who discuss the attainment of good government, past and present, invariably cite them first. What methods did they then employ to control and govern these peoples? Our Emperor Taizu Gao took antiquity as his mirror and Heaven as his model, laid broad foundations and established imperial rule, providing a model for ten thousand generations. Among the Fan, Yi, Rong, and Mo peoples, he appointed chieftains everywhere, organizing them like the various guards, defining their territories by mountains and streams, and relaxing the rigor of the laws governing them. What precisely was his sagely intention? Recently, the Baicao and other Fan peoples have made incursions every year, even causing His Majesty anxiety as he looks westward. Yet the Compendium of Essential Matters of the Southwest states that the various Fan peoples now block the strategic routes from the Greater Fan territories and indeed form a protective barrier for the region of Shu…

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
籬是致雲吐之二番不復內侵於中國
則又若未足爲重輕者其果然否耶自
昔封疆之臣從事於此不爲少矣或有
傾竭內資要結夷好南詔嶲州相率比
附或又以爲啓戎資盜養成癰疽特未
決耳迺反而規圖攻伐廣置雄邊吐番
震疊請以城降不知二者其孰爲得失
耶維州是非之辨自昔諸賢未有定論
不知由今日之事觀之其尚主盟以守
信乎抑亦從而取之也夫有文事者必
有武備爾多士生長鄉邦必有不易之
見其詳言之毋曰軍旅之事未之學也
punctuated: 籬，是致雲吐之二番不復內侵於中國，則又若未足爲重輕者，其果然否耶？自昔封疆之臣從事於此不爲少矣，或有傾竭內資，要結夷好，南詔嶲州相率比附；或又以爲啓戎資盜，養成癰疽，特未決耳。迺反而規圖攻伐，廣置雄邊，吐番震疊，請以城降。不知二者其孰爲得失耶？維州是非之辨，自昔諸賢未有定論。不知由今日之事觀之，其尚主盟以守信乎？抑亦從而取之也？夫有文事者必有武備，爾多士生長鄉邦，必有不易之見，其詳言之，毋曰軍旅之事未之學也。
translation_en: …a protective barrier, thereby keeping the two tribal peoples of Yun and Tu [?] from again invading China. Yet this would seem to suggest that they are insufficient to tip the balance. Is that really so? From earlier times, no small number of officials responsible for the frontiers have concerned themselves with this matter. Some exhausted domestic resources to secure friendly relations with the non-Chinese peoples, and Nanzhao and Xizhou followed one another in pledging allegiance. Others, however, considered this an invitation to war and a means of supplying bandits, nurturing an abscess that had merely not yet burst. They therefore turned instead to planning military attacks and establishing strong frontier forces on a broad scale. The Tibetans were overawed and asked to surrender their cities. Which of these two approaches brought success, and which failure? The worthies of earlier times never reached a settled judgment on the rights and wrongs of the Weizhou affair. Viewed in light of present circumstances, should one still uphold the covenant to preserve good faith? Or should one instead accept the surrender and take possession of the city? Those who engage in civil affairs must also maintain military preparedness. You candidates were born and raised in this region and surely have firmly held views. Explain them in detail; do not say that you have never studied military affairs.

“Only Heaven is great; only Yao modeled himself upon it.”

Wang Zuanzong

Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor, comments: 〔Emperor Yao united his virtue with Heaven. Writers often describe this with such phrases as “his radiance reached the four extremities,” which quite miss the original purport. This composition rests on principle and forms a seamless whole. It should be recorded as a model.〕

Associate Examiner Zhai, Instructor, comments: 〔Its understanding of principle is incisive and clear, and its wording concise and apt. Consider its sense of a transforming influence so seamless, and a virtue so deeply felt, that they are difficult to name [?]. I select it.〕

The sage unites his virtue with Heaven, and in this we can perceive his greatness. For by contemplating Heaven, we come to know the sage. Who but Emperor Yao could attain this? When the Master praised Yao in former times, his meaning was, in effect, as follows: Among rulers who govern all under Heaven, who does not wish to model his government upon Yao? Yet who understands what made Yao great? Now Heaven arches overhead, and the four seasons proceed beneath it; its light reaches downward, and the myriad things come into being. In stillness it is concentrated; in movement it is direct. Its all-embracing compass leaves nothing outside. It manifests benevolence and conceals its operation; though it accomplishes transformation, it does so without conscious intent. This is what makes Heaven Heaven. Nothing in all the world that is called great can measure up to it. Yet was Yao alone able to measure up to it? For he held Heaven within himself [?], and …

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
與垂衣端拱之下人但見其渾渾然已爾仰之
彌高泯篤恭於無迹嚮明而治正位凝命之餘
人但見其丕丕然已爾即之愈遠妙不顯以盡
神至德之淵微殆與溥博無涯者其致一也前
有作者弗可尚已堯之爲君其大君矣乎帝德
之廣運殆與於穆不已者其道同也後有作者
弗可及已堯之爲德其至德矣乎是則言聖而
至於堯則聖不可加矣言堯而擬諸天則堯不
可名矣自非天下之至聖其孰能知之抑嘗讀
===
堯典而知放勳之盛自親睦平章定時成歲命
官敷治之外無聞焉至于光被四表格于上下
允釐百工庶績咸熙則巍巍然煥煥然者矣然一言
以蔽之曰欽焉已耳吁此天地萬物之本也此
千聖傳心之始也此堯之所以爲大也有天下
者其尚念哉
大哉聖人之道洋洋乎發育萬物峻極于
天優優大哉禮儀三百威儀三千待其
人而後行故曰苟不至德至道不凝焉
punctuated:
與垂衣端拱之下，人但見其渾渾然已爾。仰之彌高，泯篤恭於無迹；嚮明而治，正位凝命之餘，人但見其丕丕然已爾。即之愈遠，妙不顯以盡神。至德之淵微，殆與溥博無涯者其致一也。前有作者，弗可尚已，堯之爲君，其大君矣乎！帝德之廣運，殆與於穆不已者其道同也。後有作者，弗可及已，堯之爲德，其至德矣乎！是則言聖而至於堯，則聖不可加矣；言堯而擬諸天，則堯不可名矣。自非天下之至聖，其孰能知之？抑嘗讀《堯典》，而知放勳之盛，自親睦平章、定時成歲、命官敷治之外，無聞焉。至于光被四表，格于上下，允釐百工，庶績咸熙，則巍巍然、煥煥然者矣。然一言以蔽之，曰欽焉已耳。吁！此天地萬物之本也，此千聖傳心之始也，此堯之所以爲大也。有天下者，其尚念哉！

大哉，聖人之道！洋洋乎，發育萬物，峻極于天！優優大哉！禮儀三百，威儀三千，待其人而後行。故曰：「苟不至德，至道不凝焉。」
translation_en:
…and, as he sat upright with hands folded and robes hanging down [?], people saw only his profound wholeness. The more they looked up to him, the higher he seemed: his deep reverence left no visible trace. Facing the light to govern, occupying his proper position and securing Heaven’s mandate, he appeared to people only as exceedingly great. The closer they approached him, the more distant he seemed: through the subtlety of what remained unseen, he fully realized spiritual efficacy. The depth and subtlety of his consummate virtue surely attained the same perfection as Heaven’s boundless vastness. None who arose before him could surpass him. Was not Yao, as a ruler, a great ruler indeed? The breadth and far-reaching operation of his imperial virtue surely followed the same Way as Heaven’s profound and unceasing activity. None who arose after him could equal him. Was not Yao’s virtue consummate virtue indeed? Thus, when speaking of sages, once one reaches Yao, nothing can be added to sagehood; when speaking of Yao and comparing him to Heaven, his greatness cannot be adequately named. Who but the utmost sage of the world could understand this?

Yet I have read the Canon of Yao and come to understand the greatness of Fangxun, “the Meritorious One.” Beyond bringing his kin into harmony, distinguishing and ordering the people, determining the seasons and completing the calendar year, and appointing officials to extend good government, nothing further is recorded. As for his radiance reaching the four outer bounds and extending above and below, his duly ordering the many offices, and all undertakings flourishing—these were indeed lofty and resplendent achievements. Yet a single word sums them up: reverence, and nothing more. Ah! This is the root of Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things; this is the beginning of the transmission of the mind through all the sages; this is what made Yao great. May those who possess all under Heaven bear it in mind!

Great indeed is the Way of the sage! Abundantly flowing, it brings forth and nourishes the myriad things, and rises to the very height of Heaven! How ample and great it is! The three hundred rules of ritual and the three thousand rules of deportment await the right person before they can be put into practice. Hence it is said: “Unless one possesses consummate virtue, the consummate Way cannot be firmly established.”

The Doctrine of the Mean traces what makes this Way great, while showing that putting it into practice must depend upon human beings. The Way originates in Heaven and is fully present in us. The Doctrine of the Mean sets forth what makes it great and entrusts it to human beings: the responsibility it imposes and the expectations it places upon them are of the highest order. Now this Way is present everywhere, yet the common people use it daily without knowing it. Let us seek its root. How great is the Way of the sage! How vast and overflowing! Speaking of its reach into the distant, nothing can restrain it. It orders and sustains the myriad kinds of beings through their birth, growth, gathering, and storage, ceaselessly directing Heaven’s primal creative force. Moving throughout the processes of creation and transformation, it fills and penetrates everything, extending transformative nurture without limit. This is its complete substance, an undivided whole: the Way in its fullness. How ample and great! Speaking of what is near at hand, it is still and correct. The three hundred rules of ceremony distinguish those above from those below for the people’s well-being, encompassing Heaven and Earth without exceeding their bounds. The three thousand rules of deportment establish instruction in accordance with human feelings, bringing each of the myriad things to fulfillment without omission. This is its great operation, clearly manifest: the Way revealed. With this Way so great, could mastery of it be easy? 以盡其大而無餘，文理密察，感而遂通，而後道之大用有以極其精而不亂。然或蔽於近小，涵養未裕乎真純；牿於見聞，神明不由乎中啓，則德有未至，而體用一源之妙不能合而爲一身；道有未孚，而顯微無間之理未免判而爲二物。是何也？黙而成之，不言而信，存乎德行。若夫守之而未化，行之而未成，均之不可以凝道也。所謂待其人而後行者，蓋如此。此中庸所以不可能者，而子思子不敢易言之也。有以夫！蓋嘗疑之：道爲人之所必有，則爲人之所必能，何以曰「中庸其至矣乎！民鮮能久矣」？蓋聖賢非言難以阻人之進也。以德不至於聖神，化不臻乎位育，則學問之功猶有歉焉。聖賢固不以小成望吾人也。君子從事於存心致知之學，積而至於能化，則所謂下學而上達者，亦一理而已矣。此又不可不知。

translation_en:
…thereby fully realizing its greatness, leaving nothing unfulfilled. Only when its patterned principles are closely discerned, and one responds to things with immediate comprehension, can the Way’s great functioning attain the utmost refinement without disorder. Yet if one is obscured by what is near and petty, one’s cultivation of true purity remains insufficient; if one is constrained by what one sees and hears, spiritual illumination does not arise from within. Then one’s virtue falls short, and the subtle truth that substance and function have a single source cannot be united in one’s own person. The Way has not yet been fully realized, and the principle that the manifest and the hidden admit no separation is inevitably divided into two things. Why is this? Accomplishing silently and inspiring trust without words depend upon virtuous conduct. As for holding fast to it without attaining transformation, or practicing it without attaining fulfillment, neither suffices to bring the Way to full realization. This is what is meant by saying that it awaits the right person before it can be put into practice. This is why the Mean is so difficult to attain, and why Master Zisi did not dare speak lightly of it. There is good reason for this!

I have sometimes wondered: if the Way is something that human beings necessarily possess, then it must be something they are necessarily capable of practicing. Why, then, is it said, “How consummate is the Mean! Rare indeed have been those among the people capable of it for a long time”? The sages and worthies did not speak of difficulty in order to impede people’s progress. Rather, unless virtue reaches the level of sageliness and spiritual efficacy, and transforming influence reaches the point where Heaven and Earth take their proper places and the myriad things are nurtured, the work of learning still falls short. The sages and worthies certainly do not expect us to content ourselves with minor accomplishments. If the gentleman applies himself to preserving the mind and extending knowledge, accumulating effort until he can bring about transformation, then what is called “learning below and reaching understanding above” is simply the working of a single principle. This, too, must be understood.

Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: 〔No other essay matches this one in closely appreciating Confucius’s words explaining the poem and Mencius’s intention in quoting them; it is neither vague nor cursory.〕
Associate Examiner Ai, Instructor, comments: 〔It grasps the purport of tracing feelings to their source and discerning human nature.〕

The great worthy cites verses approved by the sage in order to show the goodness of human nature. The goodness of human nature is something that cannot be artificially contrived. Looking at the poem’s words and Confucius’s praise of them, one can recognize that human nature is originally good. It was fitting, then, that Mencius quoted these words to resolve Gongduzi’s doubts. His meaning was this: human nature is one, yet those who depart from it regard their own doctrines as correct and thereby mislead others. Have you not heard that, when conflicting assertions cause confusion, one should settle the matter by reference to the sage? Confucius once expressed his approval of the poem “The Multitude of the People” in the Greater Odes. The poem says: “Heaven gives birth to the multitude of the people; wherever there are things, there are their governing principles. The people possess a constant nature and love this excellent virtue.” The author of this poem perceived the shared process whereby goodness is continued and human nature is formed. Those who recite it, however, do not necessarily attain the subtle understanding in which its sounds enter and its meaning penetrates the heart. Confucius embodied this nature innately. He once read this poem and praised it, saying: “Surely the author of this poem understood the Way!” Why was this? When Heaven gives birth to human beings, wherever there is a thing, there must be its governing principle. Material force gives them form, and principle is also endowed upon them. In truth, this is Heaven and Earth’s [two illegible characters; ?]…

易
punctuated:
也。有是則，必屬是人，若于其性而罔或悖焉，殆非須臾所可離也。夫惟秉彛之性無不同，故於好德之情無或異。天機所觸，自見夫理義之悅我心，而善善之公達之天下而無間；德性所知，自覺其非道之拂吾欲，而樂善之誠通乎物我而皆然。是蓋不學而知，其良知也；不慮而能，其良能也。謂作詩者之知道也，豈其然乎？夫好德者，情之善也；而所以好德者，性之本善也。聖人以詩之言爲然，子乃不以聖人之言爲然乎？嗚呼！以孟氏之門，而公都子不悟性善之說，乃以世俗之論質而辨之，其信道不篤，可慨也已！孟子慮其終弗悟也，而以聖人之說折之，蓋以徵諸孔子，則群疑釋而浮論息矣。何其好辨之目猶未免焉？其殆溺於流俗而不能振拔者乎？雖然，聖賢衛道之心，盡其在我，而天下後世之性其性者，皆倡明性學之力也。故曰：「孟子有功於聖門。」

易
translation_en:
…indeed. Wherever such a principle exists, it must belong to the person concerned, accord with that person’s nature without any contradiction [?], and surely cannot be departed from even for an instant. Since the nature endowed with constant moral norms is the same in everyone, the feeling of loving virtue likewise differs in no one. When their innate impulses are stirred, people see for themselves that principle and righteousness delight their hearts; the impartial disposition to approve goodness extends throughout the world without interruption. Through the awareness of their virtuous nature, they recognize for themselves that what is contrary to the Way offends their desires; the sincerity of their delight in goodness pervades both self and others, alike in all. This is knowing without learning—their innate moral knowledge; it is being able without deliberation—their innate moral capacity. Was this not why the poet was said to understand the Way? Loving virtue is the goodness of the feelings; that which makes one love virtue is the original goodness of human nature. The sage accepted the poem’s words as true. Do you, then, refuse to accept the sage’s words as true?

Alas! Though a disciple of Mengzi, Gongduzi failed to grasp the teaching that human nature is good, and instead questioned and disputed it with commonplace arguments. His lack of firm faith in the Way is truly lamentable! Mengzi feared that he would never understand, and therefore settled the matter with the sage’s teaching. By appealing to Kongzi, he would dispel the many doubts and silence groundless arguments. Why, then, did he still fail to escape the charge of being fond of disputation? Was this perhaps because those who made the charge were mired in prevailing vulgar opinions and unable to raise themselves above them? Even so, in their resolve to defend the Way, sages and worthies fully discharge what lies within their own power. That people throughout the world and in later generations realize their own nature is entirely owing to the work of those who proclaimed and clarified the learning of human nature. Thus it is said: “Mengzi rendered meritorious service to the school of the sages.”

Book of Changes

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
文言曰元者善之長也亨者嘉之會也利
者義之和也貞者事之幹也君子體仁
足以長人嘉會足以合禮利物足以和
義貞固足以幹事君子行此四德者故
曰乾元亨利貞
王纘宗
同考試官教諭王　批〔天德備於人而體於君子之健此作剖析評盡眞究心於理學者〕
同考試官教諭張　批得聖人發象象之藴
===
考試官教諭李　批〔純正〕
考試官學正周　批〔得旨〕
文言論天德在人而體於君子必申其所以體
之之也蓋德備於人非至健無以體之也君子之
所不可及者其惟是歟夫子發乾之藴以申象
傳之意蓋謂道原於一本而命之為四德其趨
則同也探乾之藴可識矣何則乾天也元亨利
貞天之德也元以統之成性存矣而道義之門
出焉亨以萃之美在中矣而人文之賁煥焉利
punctuated:
文言曰：「元者，善之長也；亨者，嘉之會也；利者，義之和也；貞者，事之幹也。君子體仁，足以長人；嘉會，足以合禮；利物，足以和義；貞固，足以幹事。君子行此四德者，故曰：『乾，元亨利貞。』」
王纘宗
同考試官教諭王，批〔天德備於人而體於君子之健，此作剖析評盡，眞究心於理學者。〕
同考試官教諭張，批：得聖人發象象之藴。
考試官教諭李，批〔純正。〕
考試官學正周，批〔得旨。〕
文言論天德在人，而體於君子，必申其所以體之之也。蓋德備於人，非至健無以體之也。君子之所不可及者，其惟是歟！夫子發乾之藴，以申象傳之意，蓋謂道原於一本，而命之為四德，其趨則同也。探乾之藴，可識矣。何則？乾，天也；元亨利貞，天之德也。元以統之，成性存矣，而道義之門出焉；亨以萃之，美在中矣，而人文之賁煥焉；利
translation_en:
The Commentary on the Words of the Text (Wenyan) says: “Origination is the foremost of goodness; flourishing is the gathering of excellence; benefit is the harmony of righteousness; constancy is the supporting trunk of affairs. By embodying benevolence, the gentleman is able to lead others; by bringing excellence together, he is able to accord with ritual propriety; by benefiting things, he is able to harmonize righteousness; by remaining constant and firm, he is able to sustain affairs. The gentleman practices these four virtues. Hence it is said: ‘Qian: origination, flourishing, benefit, and constancy.’”
Wang Zuanzong 王纘宗.
Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: 〔“Heaven’s virtues are fully present in human beings and embodied through the gentleman’s vigor. This composition analyzes and evaluates them exhaustively [?]: its author has truly devoted his mind to the learning of principle.”〕
Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “It grasps the underlying meaning of the sage’s exposition of the images [?].”
Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: 〔“Pure and correct.”〕
Examiner Zhou, Instructor, comments: 〔“Grasps the essential meaning.”〕
The Commentary on the Words of the Text discusses how Heaven’s virtues reside in human beings and are embodied by the gentleman; it must therefore explain how he embodies them [?]. For although these virtues are fully present in human beings, without the utmost vigor one cannot embody them. Is this not precisely what makes the gentleman beyond others’ reach? The Master reveals the inner meaning of Qian to amplify the meaning of the Commentary on the Images. His point is that the Way originates in a single root: although its manifestations are named the four virtues, their tendency is the same. By exploring Qian’s inner meaning, one can understand this. Why is this so? Qian is Heaven; origination, flourishing, benefit, and constancy are Heaven’s virtues. Origination unifies them: the fully constituted nature is preserved, and from it emerges the gateway to the Way and righteousness. Flourishing gathers them together: beauty resides within, and the adornment of human culture shines forth. Benefit…

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
以定天下之分而其處之也當貞以一天下之
動而其察之也深在天者未始不在於人焉然
賦賦惟均而存焉者寡惟君子以仁爲體而於
愛無不周其儀不忒而於禮無不合宜焉以昭
執物於此而得其分矣哲焉以寧志事由此而
有所依矣在人者未始不爲天焉夫君子之所
以體德而異於人者夫豈可以襲而取之也哉
亦惟至健而已矣盍觀諸乾乎乾惟健也故能
統乎四德而無間君子惟健也而後能行此四
===
德而無遺熟於仁而精於義實本於必爲之勇
節於禮而成於智實由夫自勝之强不然則欲
然而餒猶夫人爾其何以法乾之健而妙元亨
利貞之德乎是則健也者天德之剛也自强不
息者君子法天之功也聖人闡乾之藴以開示
後學者蓋如此抑剛健中正純粹而精誠之謂
也中庸曰誠者天之道也誠之者人之道也即
君子法乾之健以求合一者也命之所以不已
教之所以無窮其惟是乎健也者聖學之全功
punctuated: 以定天下之分，而其處之也當；貞以一天下之動，而其察之也深。在天者未始不在於人焉。然賦賦惟均，而存焉者寡。惟君子以仁爲體，而於愛無不周；其儀不忒，而於禮無不合。宜焉以昭，執物於此而得其分矣；哲焉以寧，志事由此而有所依矣。在人者未始不爲天焉。夫君子之所以體德而異於人者，夫豈可以襲而取之也哉？亦惟至健而已矣。盍觀諸乾乎？乾惟健也，故能統乎四德而無間；君子惟健也，而後能行此四德而無遺。熟於仁而精於義，實本於必爲之勇；節於禮而成於智，實由夫自勝之强。不然，則欲然而餒，猶夫人爾，其何以法乾之健而妙元亨利貞之德乎？是則健也者，天德之剛也；自强不息者，君子法天之功也。聖人闡乾之藴以開示後學者，蓋如此。抑剛健中正、純粹而精，誠之謂也。《中庸》曰：「誠者，天之道也；誠之者，人之道也。」即君子法乾之健以求合一者也。命之所以不已，教之所以無窮，其惟是乎？健也者，聖學之全功
translation_en: …by settling the proper divisions throughout the world, and its disposition of them is fitting; steadfastness unifies the movements of the world, and its discernment of them is profound. What resides in Heaven has never been absent from human beings. Yet although the endowment is equally bestowed [?], few preserve it. Only the gentleman takes benevolence as his substance, so that his love embraces all; his deportment is without error, so that everything accords with ritual propriety. Through fittingness he achieves clarity, and in handling things thereby assigns each its proper place; through wisdom he achieves tranquillity, and his aspirations and undertakings thereby find something on which to rely. What resides in human beings has never been other than Heaven. Can the gentleman’s embodiment of virtue, which distinguishes him from others, possibly be acquired through mere imitation? It rests solely upon the utmost vigor. Why not consider Qian, the Creative? Because Qian is vigorous, it encompasses the four virtues without interruption; only through vigor can the gentleman practice these four virtues without omission. His maturity in benevolence and refinement in righteousness are truly rooted in the courage to act resolutely; his discipline in ritual propriety and fulfillment in wisdom truly arise from the strength to overcome himself. Otherwise, he may wish to achieve these things but lose heart, remaining just like anyone else. How could he then emulate Qian’s vigor and bring to perfection the virtues of origination, flourishing, benefit, and steadfastness? Vigor, then, is the firmness of Heaven’s virtue; unceasing self-strengthening is the gentleman’s work of emulating Heaven. Such is the sage’s purpose in elucidating Qian’s hidden meaning to instruct later learners. Moreover, to be firm and vigorous, centered and correct, pure and unmixed, and refined—this is what sincerity means. The Doctrine of the Mean says: “Sincerity is the Way of Heaven; making oneself sincere is the Way of human beings.” This is precisely how the gentleman emulates Qian’s vigor and seeks unity with Heaven. Is this not why Heaven’s mandate never ceases and why its teaching is inexhaustible? Vigor is the complete accomplishment of learning to become a sage…

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
而彌綸參贊本於此矣未至於健者當何如亦
曰知恥近乎勇
聖人南面而聽天下嚮明而治蓋取諸此
也
劉念
同考試官教諭王　批〔文辭縝密不襲故常非精於易者不能也宜取以冠多士〕
同考試官教諭張　批〔融會聖人取易之義可嘉〕
考試官教諭李　批〔潔凈精微此作得之矣〕
===
考試官學正周　批〔純粹典雅〕
大傳舉王者居正以閈明而有取於後天之卦
位焉甚矣聖人大居正而貴明德也觀於後天
離卦之位而聖人之用易可見矣夫子闡後天
圖學之秘至此蓋謂聖人之治法諸天天下之
理備於易吾觀後天南離之位不獨可以見造
化之理也蓋亦有用於王道之大焉何則昔者
聖人之王天下也居正體元端冕以式夫百辟
者恭已南面也而大觀仰顒若之容正位凝命
punctuated:
而彌綸參贊本於此矣。未至於健者當何如？亦曰：「知恥近乎勇。」
聖人南面而聽天下，嚮明而治，蓋取諸此也。
劉念
同考試官教諭王　批〔文辭縝密，不襲故常，非精於易者不能也。宜取以冠多士。〕
同考試官教諭張　批〔融會聖人取易之義，可嘉。〕
考試官教諭李　批〔潔凈精微，此作得之矣。〕
考試官學正周　批〔純粹典雅。〕
大傳舉王者居正以閈明，而有取於後天之卦位焉。甚矣，聖人大居正而貴明德也！觀於後天離卦之位，而聖人之用易可見矣。夫子闡後天圖學之秘，至此蓋謂聖人之治法諸天，天下之理備於易。吾觀後天南離之位，不獨可以見造化之理也，蓋亦有用於王道之大焉。何則？昔者聖人之王天下也，居正體元，端冕以式夫百辟者，恭已南面也，而大觀仰顒若之容；正位凝命，
translation_en:
…and comprehensively ordering the world and assisting the transforming and nourishing work of Heaven and Earth are rooted in this. What should those who have not yet attained such vigor do? It is simply said: “To know shame is to approach courage.”
“The sage faces south and gives audience to all under Heaven; he faces the light and governs. This was surely taken from this.”
Liu Nian
Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: “The composition is closely reasoned and does not follow conventional precedents. Only someone thoroughly versed in the Book of Changes could achieve this. It should be selected to rank first among the candidates.”
Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “Its integrated understanding of how the sages drew upon the Book of Changes is commendable.”
Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “Purity and subtle precision: this composition has attained them.”
Examiner Zhou, School Director, comments: “Pure, refined, and classically elegant.”
The Great Commentary describes the king occupying the correct position so as to attain illumination [?], drawing upon the positions of the trigrams in the Later Heaven arrangement. How greatly the sage esteems occupying the correct position and values luminous virtue! By observing the position of the trigram Li in the Later Heaven arrangement, one can see how the sage employs the Book of Changes. At this point in his exposition of the mysteries of the Later Heaven diagram, the Master means that the sage models his governance on Heaven, and that the principles of all under Heaven are fully contained in the Book of Changes. When I consider the southern position of Li in the Later Heaven arrangement, I see not only the principles of creation and transformation: it also has applications to the great enterprise of the kingly Way. Why is this? In ancient times, when sages ruled all under Heaven, they occupied the correct position and embodied the originating principle. Wearing ceremonial robes and caps to serve as models for the many lords, they held themselves reverently and faced south, and those beholding their majestic presence looked up to their dignified bearing. They made their position correct and secured Heaven’s mandate…

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
垂衣以涖夫萬國者端拱南面也而臨下者有
赫之盛繼明以照於四方幽隱於是乎畢達文
明以化成天下陽德於是乎昭宣制禮作樂以
辯上下焉以和神人焉而因天則地之規何顯
設也明法勅罰以一民行焉以防民忒焉而昭
德塞違之典何章明也夫南面以宅明而用明
以圖治聖人御世之道得矣而果何所取哉蓋
亦取於後天之離而已夫離南方也天地之正
位也其德天地之明德也易卦陳圖以示範則
===
貞明之體列而默成之象已具聖人辯方以象
德則顯比之道著而效法之能已成表正萬邦
其治辨矣庶績咸熙其道光矣聖人之有取於
離也蓋如此是可以見易道爲用之大而聖人
法易之功斯其至矣抑聖人純乎易者也故曰
天地設位聖人成能又曰天地設位而易行乎
其中矣成性存存道義之門夫子旣以萬物之
隨帝出入者闡其秘而復推之於王道以著其
盛則易之所以彌綸天地經紀人事者益以明
punctuated: 垂衣以涖夫萬國者，端拱南面也，而臨下者有赫之盛。繼明以照於四方，幽隱於是乎畢達；文明以化成天下，陽德於是乎昭宣。制禮作樂，以辯上下焉，以和神人焉，而因天則地之規何顯設也！明法勅罰，以一民行焉，以防民忒焉，而昭德塞違之典何章明也！夫南面以宅明，而用明以圖治，聖人御世之道得矣，而果何所取哉？蓋亦取於後天之離而已。夫離，南方也，天地之正位也；其德，天地之明德也。易卦陳圖以示範，則貞明之體列，而默成之象已具；聖人辯方以象德，則顯比之道著，而效法之能已成。表正萬邦，其治辨矣；庶績咸熙，其道光矣。聖人之有取於離也，蓋如此。是可以見易道爲用之大，而聖人法易之功，斯其至矣。抑聖人純乎易者也，故曰：「天地設位，聖人成能。」又曰：「天地設位，而易行乎其中矣。成性存存，道義之門。」夫子旣以萬物之隨帝出入者闡其秘，而復推之於王道以著其盛，則易之所以彌綸天地、經紀人事者益以明。
translation_en:
…Letting his robes hang down as he presides over the myriad states, he sits upright with hands folded, facing south; thus his rule over those below possesses radiant majesty. Continuing the light to illuminate the four quarters, he brings all that is hidden and obscure into view. Through cultural brilliance he transforms and perfects all under Heaven, and thus the virtue of yang is gloriously displayed. He establishes ritual and creates music to distinguish those above from those below and to bring spirits and human beings into harmony: how manifestly established are these standards that accord with Heaven and take Earth as their model! He clarifies laws and enjoins punishments to unify the people’s conduct and guard against their transgressions: how resplendent are these institutions that make virtue manifest and prevent wrongdoing!

By facing south to dwell in brightness, and employing brightness to seek good government, the sage attains the way of governing the world. From what, then, does he take his model? Simply from Li in the Later Heaven arrangement. Li occupies the south, a cardinal position of Heaven and Earth; its virtue is the luminous virtue of Heaven and Earth. When the trigrams of the Changes are arrayed in a diagram to provide a model, the configuration of steadfast brightness is set forth, and the image of silent accomplishment is already complete. When the sage distinguishes the directions to embody their virtues, the way of manifest union becomes apparent, and his capacity to emulate them is fully realized. Setting an upright example for the myriad states, he brings order to his government; with all undertakings flourishing, his way shines forth. Such is the sage’s adoption of Li as his model.

Here we can see the greatness of the Way of the Changes in its application, and the sage’s achievement in taking the Changes as his model reaches its utmost extent. Indeed, the sage is wholly at one with the Changes. Thus it says: “Heaven and Earth establish their positions, and the sage fulfills their capacities.” It also says: “Heaven and Earth establish their positions, and change operates between them. Preserving continually the nature that has been formed is the gateway to the Way and righteousness.” The Master has already disclosed its mysteries through the myriad things that follow the Supreme Lord in coming forth and withdrawing; he further extends this to the kingly Way to reveal its grandeur. Thus it becomes still clearer how the Changes encompasses and orders Heaven and Earth and regulates human affairs…

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
聖人之所以參賛化育佐佑斯民者益以大何
也惟其體與之一故其用與之符蓋非有心取
之者也善觀易與聖人者盍於無言之妙求之
書
羅頊
水火金木土穀惟修正德利用厚生惟和
考試官教諭李　批〔虞廷保治氣象千載讀之猶可想見〕
考試官學正周　批〔典雅〕
===
大臣啓君之養民惟克治乎府事而已蓋六府
三事養道備矣苟能有以治之則於保治何有
哉昔禹推益儆戒之旨以告舜如此其意若曰
天之立君以爲民也君之立政以爲養也失養
則病政失政則病德帝之所深念者當何如耶
蓋養之原於府者其道有六曰水曰火曰金曰
木曰土曰穀皆天之所由以生物者也然天能
生於其所及不能生於其所不及則所以成天
之能者帝也帝惟裁成其道輔相其宜盈則泄
punctuated:
聖人之所以參賛化育、佐佑斯民者益以大。何也？惟其體與之一，故其用與之符，蓋非有心取之者也。善觀易與聖人者，盍於無言之妙求之？

書
羅頊
「水火金木土穀惟修，正德利用厚生惟和。」
考試官教諭李　批〔虞廷保治氣象，千載讀之猶可想見。〕
考試官學正周　批〔典雅。〕

大臣啓君之養民，惟克治乎府事而已。蓋六府三事，養道備矣。苟能有以治之，則於保治何有哉？昔禹推益儆戒之旨以告舜，如此。其意若曰：天之立君以爲民也，君之立政以爲養也。失養則病政，失政則病德。帝之所深念者，當何如耶？蓋養之原於府者，其道有六，曰水、曰火、曰金、曰木、曰土、曰穀，皆天之所由以生物者也。然天能生於其所及，不能生於其所不及，則所以成天之能者，帝也。帝惟裁成其道，輔相其宜，盈則泄
translation_en:
…and the means by which the sage participates in and assists transformation and nurture, supporting and aiding the people, become still greater. Why is this? Only because his substance is one with that of the Changes does his functioning accord with it; he does not deliberately seek to draw upon it. Those who would fully understand the Changes and the sage—why not seek this in the wonder that lies beyond words?

Book of Documents
Luo Xu 羅頊
“Water, fire, metal, wood, earth, and grain are to be duly regulated; rectifying virtue, facilitating use, and enriching livelihood are to be harmonized.”
Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: 〔Even after a thousand years, reading this still enables one to envision the atmosphere of preserving good government at Shun’s court.〕
Examiner Zhou, Instructor, comments: 〔Classical and elegant.〕

A great minister’s instruction to his ruler concerning the nourishment of the people consists simply in effectively managing the six resources and the three affairs. For these six resources and three affairs encompass the entire way of nourishing the people. If one can manage them properly, what difficulty can there be in preserving good government? Long ago, Yu elaborated the purport of Yi’s admonitions and addressed Shun in these terms. His meaning was as follows: Heaven establishes rulers for the sake of the people; rulers establish government for the sake of nourishing them. Failure to nourish the people impairs government; failure in government impairs virtue. How deeply, then, should the emperor ponder this?

As for nourishment originating in resources, there are six means: water, fire, metal, wood, earth, and grain. These are all things through which Heaven brings living things into being. Yet Heaven can generate life within its reach, but cannot do so beyond its reach. It is therefore the emperor who brings Heaven’s capacity to completion. The emperor shapes and completes its way and assists what is fitting to it; when there is excess, he drains…

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
之範圍而不過也虛則相之曲成而不遺也必
使行於天者其氣順也具於地者其質遂也成
於人者其工訖也則五行時若氣化默成於休
徵百穀用登育物咸熙於茂對所謂天地設位
聖人成能者此也而民焉有不得其養者乎養
之寓於事者其道有三曰正德曰利用曰厚生
民之所由以與能者也然民能與於其所能不
能與於其所不能則所以作民之則者帝也帝
惟神以盡能化以盡利大觀在上懋建惟皇之
===
極通變在下益章不倦之神必使迪其經也其
典敘也制其用也其利溥也阜其俗也其風洽
也則教思無窮自承式於軌物容保無疆咸胥
慶於平康所謂聖人成能百姓與能者此也而
民焉有不得其養者乎是則府以修之養之始
也事以和之養之終也萬世永賴養之極也此
有虞所以不可及也抑聖人之憂民如此其詳
且切也宜天下無不得其所者然竟不能援當
時之阻饑者何蓋聖人之心固欲盡夫人而怙
punctuated: 之，範圍而不過也；虛則相之，曲成而不遺也。必使行於天者，其氣順也；具於地者，其質遂也；成於人者，其工訖也。則五行時若，氣化默成於休徵；百穀用登，育物咸熙於茂對。所謂「天地設位，聖人成能」者，此也。而民焉有不得其養者乎？養之寓於事者，其道有三：曰正德，曰利用，曰厚生，民之所由以與能者也。然民能與於其所能，不能與於其所不能，則所以作民之則者，帝也。帝惟神以盡能，化以盡利，大觀在上，懋建惟皇之極；通變在下，益章不倦之神。必使迪其經也，其典敘也；制其用也，其利溥也；阜其俗也，其風洽也。則教思無窮，自承式於軌物；容保無疆，咸胥慶於平康。所謂「聖人成能，百姓與能」者，此也。而民焉有不得其養者乎？是則府以修之，養之始也；事以和之，養之終也；萬世永賴，養之極也。此有虞所以不可及也。抑聖人之憂民如此其詳且切也，宜天下無不得其所者，然竟不能援當時之阻饑者，何？蓋聖人之心固欲盡夫人而怙
translation_en:
…it, encompassing and regulating it without excess; where there is deficiency, he assists it, bringing everything to fulfillment in all its particulars without omission. He must ensure that what moves in Heaven has its vital forces flow harmoniously; that what is furnished by Earth fully develops its material qualities; and that what is accomplished by human beings reaches completion in their labors. Then the Five Phases follow their proper seasons, and the transformations of vital forces silently produce auspicious signs; the hundred grains ripen, and the nurture of all things flourishes in full accord with Heaven and Earth. This is what is meant by “Heaven and Earth establish their positions, and the sage brings their capacities to fulfillment.” How, then, could any of the people fail to receive their sustenance?

As for sustenance embodied in affairs, its ways are three: rectifying virtue, facilitating use, and enriching livelihood. These are the means by which the people participate in this accomplishment.
