Yet the people can participate in what lies within their capacities, but cannot participate in what lies beyond them. It is therefore the emperor who establishes the standard for the people. Through his spiritual efficacy, the emperor fully realizes these capacities; through transformation, he fully realizes their benefits. As a magnificent example on high, he diligently establishes the sovereign’s supreme standard; adapting to change below, he further manifests his untiring spiritual efficacy. He must guide the people along the constant ways, so that their norms are properly ordered; regulate their use of things, so that benefits extend widely; and enrich their customs, so that his transforming influence pervades them. Then, with his concern for instruction inexhaustible, they naturally receive their models from established rules and standards; with his embrace and protection boundless, all rejoice together in peace and well-being. This is what is meant by “The sage brings these capacities to fulfillment, and the common people participate in their accomplishment.” How, then, could any of the people fail to receive their sustenance?

Thus, putting the six resources in order is the beginning of providing sustenance; harmonizing the three affairs is its completion; and ensuring that ten thousand generations may depend upon it forever is its highest realization. This is why the ruler of Youyu, Shun, cannot be equaled. Yet the sage’s concern for the people was so detailed and so urgent that everyone under Heaven ought to have found a fitting place. Why, then, was he ultimately unable to rescue those who suffered hunger in his time? For the sage’s heart surely desired that every person should find support…

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
□之然而勢有不能則聖人病矣是聖人之仁
民其所能者心也其所不能者勢也雖然聖人
不病也天之大也人猶有所憾甚矣聖人之似
天也
惟助成王德顯越尹人祗辟
高躍
考試官教諭李　批〔內服外服之心言之殆盡是可錄也〕
考試官學正周　批〔明暢〕
===
商之羣臣惟期弼成乎君相而已蓋君相之責
重矣羣臣所以共弼其成者此耳其尚敢以自
逸也哉昔武王告康叔之意豈不曰昔殷哲王
越厥御事罔敢暇逸則然矣至于內服外服諸
臣亦循是也抑何爲也哉蓋天下有君道焉人
心所視以爲安危者也今日經哲之謨則既聖
矣似若無事於匡弼者然責難之心諸臣其能
一日已耶所以不敢暇逸者正欲爲之先後爲
之疏附因其經而導之以綏猷也因其哲而通
punctuated:
□之，然而勢有不能，則聖人病矣。是聖人之仁民，其所能者心也，其所不能者勢也。雖然，聖人不病也。天之大也，人猶有所憾。甚矣，聖人之似天也！

惟助成王德顯，越尹人祗辟。
高躍
考試官教諭李　批〔內服外服之心，言之殆盡，是可錄也。〕
考試官學正周　批〔明暢。〕

商之羣臣，惟期弼成乎君相而已。蓋君相之責重矣，羣臣所以共弼其成者，此耳。其尚敢以自逸也哉？昔武王告康叔之意，豈不曰：「昔殷哲王，越厥御事，罔敢暇逸。」則然矣。至于內服外服諸臣，亦循是也，抑何爲也哉？蓋天下有君道焉，人心所視以爲安危者也。今日經哲之謨，則既聖矣，似若無事於匡弼者。然責難之心，諸臣其能一日已耶？所以不敢暇逸者，正欲爲之先後，爲之疏附，因其經而導之以綏猷也，因其哲而通
translation_en:
…[illegible] them [?]. Yet where circumstances make this impossible, the sage is distressed. Thus, in the sage’s benevolence toward the people, what lies within his power is his heart; what lies beyond his power is circumstance. Even so, this is no failing of the sage. Great as Heaven is, people still find cause for regret. How closely the sage resembles Heaven!

“Only assist in bringing the king’s virtue to illustrious perfection, and assist the chief minister in reverently serving the sovereign.”
Gao Yue
Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: 〔The intentions of those serving within and outside the court are expressed almost exhaustively. This merits selection.〕
Examiner Zhou, Instructor, comments: 〔Clear and fluent.〕

The assembled ministers of Shang sought only to assist the ruler and chief minister in accomplishing their work. The responsibilities of ruler and chief minister were indeed weighty; this alone was what the ministers jointly helped them fulfill. How could they then dare indulge in ease? Was this not the meaning of King Wu’s admonition to Kang Shu: “Formerly, the wise kings of Yin and those who served them dared not indulge in leisure or ease”? So indeed it was. The ministers serving within and outside the court likewise followed this practice. Why did they do so?

There is a ruler’s Way in the world, to which the people’s hearts look for their security or peril. The present ruler’s plans, grounded in ordering affairs and in wisdom, are already sagely, so that there seems to be no need to correct or assist him. Yet could the ministers cease for even a single day to demand difficult achievements of him? Their refusal to indulge in leisure or ease arose precisely from their desire to guide and support him, to draw him close and attach themselves to him: building upon his ordering of affairs, they would guide him toward bringing his plans to fruition; building upon his wisdom, they would lead him onward …

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
之以迪忱也務使一人成不顯之休而四海有
無窮之聞然後吾心始慰耳夫諸臣與君其分
遠矣而其休戚同也是故以君之心爲心而不
能自已如此也不然則君德有關於天下而乃
遏佚其光也寧不有負於君乎天下有相道焉
君德所恃以爲隆替者也今日篤棐之忱則既
賢矣似若無待於夾持者然交脩之益諸臣其
敢一息忘耶所以罔敢暇逸者正欲爲之和衷
爲之寅恭左右贊襄以成能也朝夕交儆以崇
===
德也務使宰臣益加祗辟之道而國家長蒙顯
德之休然後吾心始安耳夫羣臣與相其禮絶
矣而其安危同也是故以相之心爲心而不能
自已如此也不然則相道有關於君德而乃怠
逸其敬也寧不有負於相乎吁羣臣獨成之心
懇切至此則亦不暇於酒矣康叔之國其尚念
哉抑讀酒誥至此而考見三代有道之盛焉蓋
君臣本一體也上下本一心也使内外大小御
事之臣能助其君則君德之顯猶吾德也能獨□
punctuated: 之以迪忱也。務使一人成不顯之休，而四海有無窮之聞，然後吾心始慰耳。夫諸臣與君，其分遠矣，而其休戚同也。是故以君之心爲心，而不能自已如此也。不然，則君德有關於天下，而乃遏佚其光也，寧不有負於君乎？天下有相道焉，君德所恃以爲隆替者也。今日篤棐之忱，則既賢矣，似若無待於夾持者。然交脩之益，諸臣其敢一息忘耶？所以罔敢暇逸者，正欲爲之和衷，爲之寅恭，左右贊襄以成能也，朝夕交儆以崇德也。務使宰臣益加祗辟之道，而國家長蒙顯德之休，然後吾心始安耳。夫羣臣與相，其禮絶矣，而其安危同也。是故以相之心爲心，而不能自已如此也。不然，則相道有關於君德，而乃怠逸其敬也，寧不有負於相乎？吁！羣臣獨成之心，懇切至此，則亦不暇於酒矣。康叔之國，其尚念哉！抑讀《酒誥》至此，而考見三代有道之盛焉。蓋君臣本一體也，上下本一心也。使内外大小御事之臣能助其君，則君德之顯猶吾德也；能獨□
translation_en:
…by leading him toward sincerity. They strive to ensure that the One Man—the sovereign—achieves manifest glory, and that his renown endures without end throughout the Four Seas; only then are their hearts consoled. Although the ministers and their ruler are far apart in rank, they share prosperity and adversity. Thus they take the ruler’s concerns as their own and cannot cease their efforts. Otherwise, since the ruler’s virtue bears upon all under Heaven, would they not fail him by obscuring and neglecting its radiance [?]?

There is also the way of the chief minister, upon which the flourishing or decline of the ruler’s virtue depends. His sincere commitment to steadfast assistance today is already worthy, seemingly requiring no further support. Yet dare the other ministers forget, even for a moment, the benefits of mutual cultivation? Their refusal to indulge in leisure is precisely intended to bring him wholehearted cooperation and reverent service: assisting him on every side to perfect his capacities, and exchanging admonitions morning and evening to elevate virtue. They strive to ensure that the chief minister increasingly follows the way of reverence for his sovereign, and that the state long enjoys the blessings of manifest virtue; only then are their hearts at ease. Although the ministers and the chief minister are sharply distinguished in ceremonial standing, they share security and peril. Thus they take the chief minister’s concerns as their own and cannot cease their efforts. Otherwise, since the chief minister’s conduct bears upon the ruler’s virtue, would they not fail him by allowing their reverence to lapse into indolence?

Ah! With the ministers’ resolve to bring matters to fulfillment [?] so earnest, they would likewise have no leisure for wine. As Kang Shu goes to his fief, may he bear this in mind! Moreover, reading the Announcement on Wine to this point, one can discern the flourishing of the Way under the Three Dynasties. Ruler and ministers are fundamentally one body; those above and below are fundamentally of one mind. If the officials charged with affairs, within and without the court, great and small, can assist their ruler, then the manifestation of his virtue is as their own virtue. If they can [doubtful text: 獨□] …

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
其相則相業之隆猶吾業也此一德一心之治
也故曰人主聯屬天下以成其身意正如此以
此爲坊而後世猶有自獨俾臧自有肺腸俾民
卒狂者何哉
詩
允矣君子展也大成
李詩
同考試官教諭吳　批〔大蒐之禮載在月令郊特牲穀梁傳此作能言之可錄以式〕
===
同考試官教諭翟　批〔溫柔敦厚可與言詩矣〕
考試官教諭李　批〔中興氣象宛然在目〕
考試官學正周　批〔雅健〕
詩人紀周王之于田而深美其復古之盛焉蓋
田以嚴終則復古之業盛矣詩人深美之也宜
哉車攻之詩紀宣王之復古也至此則總敘其
始終而深美之若曰我周昔在中葉大蒐廢而
不講今觀甫草諸侯會而載興一時復古之盛
當何如哉夫田獵之典所以觀君道也使其或
punctuated:
其相，則相業之隆猶吾業也。此一德一心之治也。故曰：「人主聯屬天下以成其身。」意正如此。以此爲坊，而後世猶有自獨俾臧、自有肺腸、俾民卒狂者，何哉？
詩
允矣君子，展也大成。
李詩
同考試官教諭吳批〔大蒐之禮，載在《月令》《郊特牲》《穀梁傳》。此作能言之，可錄以式。〕
同考試官教諭翟批〔溫柔敦厚，可與言詩矣。〕
考試官教諭李批〔中興氣象，宛然在目。〕
考試官學正周批〔雅健。〕
詩人紀周王之于田，而深美其復古之盛焉。蓋田以嚴終，則復古之業盛矣。詩人深美之也，宜哉！《車攻》之詩，紀宣王之復古也。至此，則總敘其始終而深美之。若曰：我周昔在中葉，大蒐廢而不講。今觀甫草，諸侯會而載興，一時復古之盛，當何如哉！夫田獵之典，所以觀君道也。使其或
translation_en:
…his chief minister, then the flourishing of the minister’s achievements is like that of our own. This is government united in virtue and purpose. Thus it is said, “The ruler joins all under Heaven together to complete his own person.” This is precisely the meaning. With this as a barrier against wrongdoing, why were there still those in later ages who deemed themselves alone good, followed their own private inclinations, and brought the people at last to frenzy?
Book of Odes
“Truly a noble man; indeed, a great accomplishment.”
Li Shi
Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: 〔The rites of the great hunt are recorded in “Monthly Ordinances,” “The Single Victim at the Border Sacrifice,” and the Guliang Commentary. This composition succeeds in explaining them and may be included as a model.〕
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhai, Instructor: 〔Gentle and kind, sincere and generous: one may discuss the Odes with this author.〕
Comment by Examiner Li, Instructor: 〔The atmosphere of dynastic resurgence stands vividly before one’s eyes.〕
Comment by Examiner Zhou, Instructor: 〔Elegant and vigorous.〕
The poet records the king of Zhou going hunting and deeply praises the grandeur of his restoration of ancient practices. For when the hunt is conducted with rigor through its conclusion, the work of restoring ancient practices flourishes. How fitting that the poet should praise it so deeply! The ode “Our Chariots Were Stout” records King Xuan’s restoration of ancient practices. At this point it sums up the undertaking from beginning to end and praises it profoundly. It is as though it said: In the middle period of our Zhou dynasty, the great hunt had been abandoned and its rites were no longer practiced. Now, looking upon the grasslands of Fu, we see the feudal lords assemble and the hunt revived. How splendid must this restoration of ancient practices be! The institution of hunting is a means of observing the ruler’s Way. If he should perchance…

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
戒之始而終則怠焉循弗田也可以爲君子乎
吾王今日之田蓋愼終以惟始者司徒以搢扑
主祠以祭禽而七騶駕焉誓社以觀變流禽以
艷利而五戎習焉貴賤明而等列辨王度之昭
宣煥乎如玉如金矣少長順而威儀彰王猷之
允塞赫然有嚴有翼矣以觀文王之耿光以揚
武王之大烈不於此重可見乎謂之君子信乎
其君子也哉田獵之禮所以明王業也使其或
肅之終而始則略焉循弗田也可以爲大成乎
===
今日甫草之田蓋謹始以永終者班馬以同力
授車以別級而整設於屛外艾蘭以爲防置旃
以爲門而厲飾於敎中軍實充而王賦復人心
攸同無弗納於軌物者矣綜理周而上下洽王
靈丕震無弗爭乎權輿者矣以發舒華夏之氣
以掃清戎狄之氛不於此重可見乎謂之大成
誠哉其大成也已吁宣王復古之盛有如此者
可以觀中興矣抑是禮也見于月令于郊特牲
四時行之亦以率先王之舊章云耳詩人乃若
punctuated: 戒之始而終則怠焉，循弗田也，可以爲君子乎？吾王今日之田，蓋愼終以惟始者。司徒以搢扑，主祠以祭禽，而七騶駕焉；誓社以觀變，流禽以艷利，而五戎習焉。貴賤明而等列辨，王度之昭宣，煥乎如玉如金矣；少長順而威儀彰，王猷之允塞，赫然有嚴有翼矣。以觀文王之耿光，以揚武王之大烈，不於此重可見乎？謂之君子，信乎其君子也哉！田獵之禮，所以明王業也。使其或肅之終而始則略焉，循弗田也，可以爲大成乎？今日甫草之田，蓋謹始以永終者。班馬以同力，授車以別級，而整設於屛外；艾蘭以爲防，置旃以爲門，而厲飾於敎中。軍實充而王賦復，人心攸同，無弗納於軌物者矣；綜理周而上下洽，王靈丕震，無弗爭乎權輿者矣。以發舒華夏之氣，以掃清戎狄之氛，不於此重可見乎？謂之大成，誠哉其大成也已！吁！宣王復古之盛，有如此者，可以觀中興矣。抑是禮也，見于《月令》，于《郊特牲》，四時行之，亦以率先王之舊章云耳。詩人乃若
translation_en:
…careful at the beginning but negligent at the end—following this would be no true hunt [?]; could he be called a gentleman? Our king’s hunt today indeed shows one who takes as much care at the end as at the beginning. The Minister of Education tucks the rod of punishment into his sash; the officer presiding over sacrifices offers game; and the seven equerries harness the teams [?]. Oaths are sworn at the altar of the soil to observe responses to changing circumstances, and game is let loose to entice men with the prospect of gain; thus the five kinds of troops are trained. Noble and humble are clearly distinguished, and ranks are differentiated: the king’s institutions shine forth, splendid as jade and gold. Younger and older take their proper places, and dignified bearing is manifest: the king’s guiding principles fully prevail, glorious in their solemnity and reverence. Are not the means of displaying King Wen’s brilliant light and exalting King Wu’s great achievements once more visible here [?]? He is called a gentleman: truly a gentleman he is!

The rites of hunting serve to make manifest the royal enterprise. If one were solemn at the end but careless at the beginning—following this would be no true hunt [?]—could it be called a great accomplishment? Today’s hunt at the grasslands of Fu indeed shows one who attends carefully to the beginning so as to carry the undertaking through to its end. Horses are distributed to equalize the strength of the teams, and chariots assigned according to rank, all arrayed in good order outside the screen. Fragrant grasses are cut to form an enclosure, and banners set up to mark its entrance; preparations are made with rigorous care amid the training [?]. Military supplies are abundant and the royal military levies restored. The people’s hearts are united, and all are brought within established norms. Overall arrangements are complete, and superiors and inferiors are in harmony. The king’s awe-inspiring power resounds mightily, and all vie to be foremost at the outset. Are not the means of releasing the vital spirit of Huaxia and sweeping away the threatening presence of the Rong and Di once more visible here [?]? It is called a great accomplishment: truly a great accomplishment it is!

Ah! Such was the magnificence of King Xuan’s restoration of ancient practices: here one can behold the revival of the dynasty. Yet these rites appear in the Monthly Ordinances and the Single Victim at the Suburban Sacrifice. Their performance in all four seasons was merely adherence to the established regulations of the former kings. Yet the poet seems as though…

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
創見而侈言之何耶蓋宣王以復古也以明文
武之功業也此車攻吉日所爲作也南征北伐
以戰則克其機蓋出於此則今日之舉夫豈好
田之云哉吁以此爲防而大蒐于昌間大蒐于
比蒲猶有若昭定之世者詩人之言至是其荒
矣
商之先后受命不殆在武丁孫子武丁孫
子武王靡不勝龍旂十乘大糦是承邦
畿千里維民所止肇域彼四海四海來
假來假祁祁景員維河殷受命咸宜百
祿是何
羅緯
===
同考試官敎諭吳　批〔葩經無慮千卷求其辭理精到〕
〔者無踰此作〕
同考試官敎諭翟　批〔結用武字最是〕
考試官敎諭李　批〔明盡〕
考試官學正周　批〔得頌德之意〕
商人之祀先必述前王垂統之澤而及後王繼
punctuated:
創見而侈言之，何耶？蓋宣王以復古也，以明文武之功業也。此《車攻》《吉日》所爲作也。南征北伐，以戰則克，其機蓋出於此，則今日之舉，夫豈好田之云哉！吁！以此爲防，而大蒐于昌間，大蒐于比蒲，猶有若昭定之世者，詩人之言至是其荒矣。
商之先后，受命不殆，在武丁孫子。武丁孫子，武王靡不勝。龍旂十乘，大糦是承。邦畿千里，維民所止。肇域彼四海，四海來假。來假祁祁，景員維河。殷受命咸宜，百祿是何。
羅緯
同考試官敎諭吳　批〔葩經無慮千卷，求其辭理精到者，無踰此作。〕
同考試官敎諭翟　批〔結用武字最是。〕
考試官敎諭李　批〔明盡。〕
考試官學正周　批〔得頌德之意。〕
商人之祀先，必述前王垂統之澤，而及後王繼
translation_en:
…as though seeing it for the first time, and speak of it so lavishly—why? It was because King Xuan restored ancient practices and made manifest the achievements of Kings Wen and Wu. This was why “Chariots Are Strong” (Che gong) and “Auspicious Day” (Ji ri) were composed. His southern expeditions and northern campaigns brought victory whenever he fought; the means of achieving this surely arose here. Could the undertaking on this occasion, then, possibly have been merely a matter of delighting in hunting? Alas! Even with this as a safeguard, there were still such events as the great hunts at Changjian [?] and Bipu in the reigns of Dukes Zhao and Ding. By then, the poet’s words had fallen into neglect.

“The former sovereigns of Shang received Heaven’s mandate without peril; it rested with Wuding’s descendants. Wuding’s descendants, those martial kings, were victorious in all things. Ten chariots bearing dragon banners attend upon the great sacrificial feast. The royal domain extends a thousand li: there the people dwell. They first marked out the realm within the Four Seas, and all within the Four Seas came to pay homage. They came to pay homage in multitudes; the vast territory was bounded by the Yellow River [?]. Yin received the mandate in full accord with what was fitting and bore its hundred blessings.”

Luo Wei

Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor, comments: “Of the thousand or so examination scripts on the Classic of Poetry, none surpasses this piece in the refinement and precision of its language and reasoning.”

Associate Examiner Zhai, Instructor, comments: “The use of the word ‘martial’ (wu) in the conclusion is especially apt.”

Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “Clear and exhaustive.”

Examiner Zhou, School Instructor, comments: “It captures the intent of praising virtue.”

When the people of Shang sacrificed to their ancestors, they invariably recounted the blessings bestowed by earlier kings in handing down the dynastic succession, and then proceeded to the later kings’ continuation…

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
統之休焉蓋君子之垂統顧所繼何如耳有商
之前後相承如此其一代世德之盛乎此亦祭
祀宗廟之樂其登歌之意則曰我商一代之盛
所以相承於今日者亦惟世德之先後相望焉
耳自昔成湯智勇錫而九圍式聖武昭而羣后
朝由七十里而克享乎天心其受命則不殆矣
傳六七君而施及于武丁其孫子有攸賴矣今
日承其澤以有位也襲其號以有爲也視之成
湯殆無有弗似者語其智可與幾也語其武可
===
與成也推之天下又何所弗勝耶故宗廟之中
龍旂有來乎十乘大糦共承乎四時其志同矣
邦畿之內民居雖限於千里肇域則極乎四海
其馭廣矣商邑四方之極也羣后畢朝祈祈然
其殆一人之慶乎景山殷命之始也大河四周
泱泱然其殆萬世之宗乎夫人心與天命相爲
表裏者也於此而見我殷之命武湯宜也武丁
亦宜也所謂百祿之遒者此耳不然則天本難
忱而何爲其有是哉天命與國脉相爲去留者
punctuated: 統之休焉。蓋君子之垂統，顧所繼何如耳。有商之前後相承如此，其一代世德之盛乎！此亦祭祀宗廟之樂，其登歌之意則曰：我商一代之盛，所以相承於今日者，亦惟世德之先後相望焉耳。自昔成湯，智勇錫而九圍式，聖武昭而羣后朝。由七十里而克享乎天心，其受命則不殆矣。傳六七君而施及于武丁，其孫子有攸賴矣。今日承其澤以有位也，襲其號以有爲也，視之成湯，殆無有弗似者。語其智，可與幾也；語其武，可與成也。推之天下，又何所弗勝耶？故宗廟之中，龍旂有來乎十乘，大糦共承乎四時，其志同矣。邦畿之內，民居雖限於千里，肇域則極乎四海，其馭廣矣。商邑，四方之極也，羣后畢朝，祈祈然，其殆一人之慶乎！景山，殷命之始也，大河四周，泱泱然，其殆萬世之宗乎！夫人心與天命相爲表裏者也。於此而見我殷之命，武湯宜也，武丁亦宜也。所謂百祿之遒者，此耳。不然，則天本難忱，而何爲其有是哉？天命與國脉相爲去留者
translation_en:
…the glory of continuing the dynastic succession. For when a noble ruler establishes a line of succession, what matters is how those who follow carry it on. With successive rulers of Shang sustaining one another in this way, how flourishing was the virtue transmitted through that dynasty’s generations! This too is music for sacrifices in the ancestral temple. The meaning of its song, sung as the musicians ascend the hall, is as follows: The flourishing achievement of our Shang dynasty has been handed down to this day solely because successive generations have matched one another in inherited virtue.

Long ago, Cheng Tang was endowed with wisdom and courage, and the nine regions took him as their model; his sagely martial prowess shone forth, and the assembled lords came to court. Beginning with a territory of seventy li, he succeeded in winning Heaven’s favor, and his receipt of the Mandate was secure. Passed down through six or seven rulers, its benefits reached Wu Ding, giving Tang’s descendants something upon which to rely. Now Wu Ding inherits Tang’s blessings and occupies the throne; he succeeds to Tang’s title and accomplishes great deeds. Compared with Cheng Tang, there is scarcely anything in which he does not resemble him. In wisdom, he can share Tang’s discernment of the first stirrings of events; in martial prowess, he can share his accomplishments. Extending these qualities throughout the realm, what could he not master?

Thus, at the ancestral temple, ten chariots arrive with dragon banners, and abundant sacrificial grain is reverently presented through the four seasons: their purpose is united. Within the royal domain, although the people’s dwellings are confined to a thousand li, the boundaries established extend to the Four Seas: his dominion is vast. The city of Shang is the focal point of the four quarters. All the lords attend court in dignified procession: is this not the felicity of the One Man, the sovereign? Mount Jing is where Yin’s Mandate began. The great river surrounds it, vast and flowing: is this not the ancestral seat for ten thousand generations?

The people’s hearts and Heaven’s Mandate are the outward and inward aspects of one another. Here we see that our Yin’s Mandate fittingly belonged to the martial Tang, and fittingly belonged to Wu Ding as well. This is precisely what is meant by ‘the hundred blessings gathering.’ Otherwise, since Heaven is inherently difficult to trust, how could such blessings have come about? Heaven’s Mandate and the lifeblood of the state depart or remain together…

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
也於此而見有商之命武丁宜也孫子亦宜也
所謂百祿是何者此耳不然則命本靡常而何
爲其若此哉吁有商其盛矣乎抑人君受命之
道詩書所載詳矣詩人獨拳拳於武之一字何
耶蓋前乎湯牽割甚矣非武則不可得而定也
後乎武丁若德鮮矣非武則不可得而興也此
宗廟升歌之意也故曰七世之廟可以觀德不
然則周公之克詰戎兵召公之張皇六師者非
耶
===
春秋
楚人使宜申來獻捷　十有二月癸丑公
會諸侯盟于薄釋宋公〔俱僖公二十有一年〕
陳宗虞
考試官學正周　批〔發明爲魯諱意親切簡嚴殆深於〕
〔春秋者〕
考試官教諭李　批〔思致精深筆力雄健麟經義〕
〔無踰此作〕
punctuated:
也。於此而見有商之命，武丁宜也，孫子亦宜也。所謂「百祿是何」者，此耳。不然，則命本靡常，而何爲其若此哉？吁！有商其盛矣乎！抑人君受命之道，詩書所載詳矣，詩人獨拳拳於武之一字，何耶？蓋前乎湯，牽割甚矣，非武則不可得而定也；後乎武丁，若德鮮矣，非武則不可得而興也。此宗廟升歌之意也。故曰：「七世之廟，可以觀德。」不然，則周公之克詰戎兵、召公之張皇六師者，非耶？

春秋

楚人使宜申來獻捷。十有二月癸丑，公會諸侯盟于薄，釋宋公。〔俱僖公二十有一年〕

陳宗虞

考試官學正周，批〔發明爲魯諱意，親切簡嚴，殆深於〕〔春秋者。〕

考試官教諭李，批〔思致精深，筆力雄健，麟經義〕〔無踰此作。〕
translation_en:
… Thus we see that the mandate of Shang was fittingly held by Wu Ding, and fittingly held by his descendants as well. This is precisely what is meant by “bearing the hundred blessings.” Otherwise, since the mandate is inherently inconstant, how could things have been thus? Ah, how flourishing Shang was! Yet the way in which rulers receive the mandate is recorded in detail in the Book of Odes and the Book of Documents. Why, then, does the poet dwell so insistently on the single word “martial”? Before Tang, oppression and mutilation were extreme; without martial power, order could not have been established. After Wu Ding, those who followed virtue were few [?]; without martial power, renewal could not have been achieved. This is the meaning of the song sung in the ancestral temple. Hence the saying: “In the temples of seven generations, one can observe virtue.” Otherwise, were the Duke of Zhou’s ordering of arms and troops, and the Duke of Shao’s grand deployment of the Six Armies, wrong?

Spring and Autumn Annals

“The men of Chu sent Yishen to present the spoils of victory.” “In the twelfth month, on the guichou day, the duke met the feudal lords and covenanted at Bo. They released the Duke of Song.” 〔Both passages are from the twenty-first year of Duke Xi.〕

Chen Zongyu

Examiner Zhou, School Instructor, comments: 〔The exposition of the intention to conceal matters on Lu’s behalf is apt, concise, and rigorous. The author appears to have a profound understanding of〕〔the Spring and Autumn Annals.〕

Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: 〔The thought is refined and profound, and the writing vigorous and forceful. Among essays interpreting the Classic of the Unicorn—the Spring and Autumn Annals—〕〔none surpasses this work.〕

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
春秋以義責望國有因受脅于外者有因求成
于外者此捷之獻薄之盟魯之于楚弗申於義
矣宜春秋以諱爲貶歟且宜申爲爲來獻捷耶
伐宋而魯獨不與故爲是以脅魯也則是捷也
捷之宋也諱不言宋者蓋曰宋非楚可捷也捷
且不可而奚急魯之獻迹其驕矜以逞乘廣之
焰熾矣馳辭以却其使聲罪以致其辟楚不靡
然戢乎而乃因其獻也俯焉以受之其弗競孰
甚焉夫諸侯所務以靖區夏尊攘焉爾魯也怵
===
楚之威忘其已之爲夏也義舉弗宣而薦辭禮
使以德宋捷之及則尊攘之職魯自隳之矣王
室之藩屏將復誰望哉經於其來其獻而不書
宋使若非宋捷然爲魯諱以貶之也諸侯曷爲
盟于薄耶襄執而猶未歸焉故假此以釋襄也
則是釋也釋之楚也諱不言楚者蓋曰襄非楚
可執也執既不可而奚自楚之釋迹其憑陵莫
禦天下之變大矣陳旅以問其故請命以解其
圍楚不惴然屈乎而乃與之盟也俛焉以求之
punctuated:
春秋以義責望國，有因受脅于外者，有因求成于外者。此捷之獻、薄之盟，魯之于楚弗申於義矣，宜春秋以諱爲貶歟！且宜申爲爲來獻捷耶？伐宋而魯獨不與，故爲是以脅魯也。則是捷也，捷之宋也。諱不言宋者，蓋曰宋非楚可捷也。捷且不可，而奚急魯之獻？迹其驕矜以逞，乘廣之焰熾矣。馳辭以却其使，聲罪以致其辟，楚不靡然戢乎？而乃因其獻也，俯焉以受之，其弗競孰甚焉！夫諸侯所務以靖區夏，尊攘焉爾。魯也怵楚之威，忘其已之爲夏也，義舉弗宣，而薦辭禮使，以德宋捷之及，則尊攘之職，魯自隳之矣。王室之藩屏，將復誰望哉？經於其來其獻而不書宋，使若非宋捷然，爲魯諱以貶之也。

諸侯曷爲盟于薄耶？襄執而猶未歸焉，故假此以釋襄也。則是釋也，釋之楚也。諱不言楚者，蓋曰襄非楚可執也。執既不可，而奚自楚之釋？迹其憑陵莫禦，天下之變大矣。陳旅以問其故，請命以解其圍，楚不惴然屈乎？而乃與之盟也，俛焉以求之。
translation_en:
The Spring and Autumn Annals holds leading states accountable to righteousness: in some cases they submit to coercion from outside; in others they seek an accommodation with outside powers. In this presentation of the spoils of victory and the covenant at Bo, Lu failed to uphold righteousness in its dealings with Chu. Was it not fitting that the Annals should censure it through concealment? Now, why did Yishen come to present the spoils of victory [?]? Lu alone had not participated in the attack on Song, so Chu did this to intimidate Lu. This victory was a victory over Song. In concealing this and not naming Song, the text in effect declares that Chu had no right to conquer Song. If even the victory was impermissible, why press to present its spoils to Lu? Examining Chu’s conduct, we see its pride indulged without restraint and the blazing arrogance of its war chariots [?]. Had Lu dispatched a declaration rejecting its envoy and proclaimed its crimes to bring it to punishment, would Chu not have submissively restrained itself? Instead, when Chu presented its spoils, Lu bowed down and accepted them. What greater weakness could there be! The duty of the feudal lords in bringing peace to the Chinese realm consists simply in honoring the king and repelling the barbarians. Yet Lu, frightened by Chu’s might, forgot that it itself belonged to the civilized Chinese states. It failed to make righteousness manifest through action, but offered courteous words and treated the envoy with ceremony, expressing gratitude for receiving the spoils of victory over Song. Thus Lu itself abandoned its duty to honor the king and repel the barbarians. To whom, then, could one look as a bulwark of the royal house? In recording the envoy’s arrival and his presentation, the Classic does not name Song, making it appear that these were not the spoils of a victory over Song. It conceals the matter for Lu’s sake, thereby censuring Lu.

Why did the feudal lords covenant at Bo? Duke Xiang had been seized and had still not returned, so they used this occasion to secure his release. This release was a release by Chu. In concealing this and not naming Chu, the text in effect declares that Chu had no right to seize Xiang. Since the seizure itself was impermissible, why should his release depend upon Chu? Examining Chu’s unchecked aggression, we see a grave upheaval in the order of the world. Had they arrayed their troops to demand an explanation and requested the king’s command to deliver him from his predicament, would Chu not have yielded in fear? Instead, they entered into a covenant with Chu, bowing low to seek his release…

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
其事已傎甚矣夫王者所執以厲庶邦操縱焉
爾魯也爲宋之圖忘其楚之爲夷也義聲弗振
而貿神致約以徼宋釋之惠則操縱之權楚得
制之矣中國之綱紀將焉攸賴耶經於其盟其
釋而不書楚使若非楚釋然爲魯諱以深貶之
也是則宋揵諱之惡其弱於夷也以正防也楚
釋諱之嫌其近於王也以謹分也聖人經世之
慮其深矣哉抑因是而徵宋襄之咎焉楚夷國
也裂防以會之不虞兵車之詐公子目夷之忠
===
謀擯不見庸其及也宜矣向非社稷神靈之對
宋之厄當不止傷股官殲已也然則自貽伊慼
者襄乎宋之幸不爲楚者賴有目夷也用賢圖
理國其可緩乎哉
六月公會單子晉侯宋公衛侯鄭伯莒子
邾子齊世子光已未同盟于雞澤〔襄公〕
三年
李之珍
考試官學正周　批〔士子類以病楚瀆分並看殊失本〕
punctuated:
其事已傎甚矣！夫王者所執以厲庶邦，操縱焉爾。魯也爲宋之圖，忘其楚之爲夷也，義聲弗振，而貿神致約，以徼宋釋之惠，則操縱之權，楚得制之矣。中國之綱紀，將焉攸賴耶？經於其盟其釋而不書楚，使若非楚釋然，爲魯諱以深貶之也。是則宋揵諱之，惡其弱於夷也，以正防也；楚釋諱之，嫌其近於王也，以謹分也。聖人經世之慮，其深矣哉！抑因是而徵宋襄之咎焉。楚，夷國也，裂防以會之，不虞兵車之詐，公子目夷之忠謀，擯不見庸，其及也宜矣。向非社稷神靈之對，宋之厄當不止傷股官殲已也。然則自貽伊慼者，襄乎！宋之幸不爲楚者，賴有目夷也。用賢圖理，國其可緩乎哉？
六月，公會單子、晉侯、宋公、衛侯、鄭伯、莒子、邾子、齊世子光，已未，同盟于雞澤。〔襄公〕三年。
李之珍
考試官學正周，批〔士子類以病楚瀆分並看，殊失本〕
translation_en:
…The affair was already profoundly perverse! What a true king holds in order to discipline the many states is simply the power to restrain and release. Yet Lu, in devising plans for Song, forgot that Chu was a barbarian state. Instead of raising its voice for righteousness, it invoked the spirits to conclude a compact [?], hoping to obtain the favor of Song’s release. Thus Chu gained control of the power to restrain and release. On what, then, could the order of the central states depend? In recording the covenant and the release, the Classic does not name Chu, making it appear that the release was not Chu’s doing. It conceals the matter for Lu’s sake, thereby censuring Lu all the more severely. Thus, by concealing Song’s victory [?], it condemns submission to the barbarians and maintains the proper barrier; by concealing Chu’s release of the captive, it guards against Chu’s approaching the authority of a king and carefully preserves distinctions of rank. How profound was the sage’s concern for ordering the world!
We may also use this affair to establish the culpability of Duke Xiang of Song. Chu was a barbarian state, yet he broke down the barrier to meet with it, failing to anticipate its deceit involving war chariots. The loyal counsel of Prince Muyi was rejected and left unused: it was fitting that disaster should overtake him. Had it not been for the reply concerning the divine powers of the altars of soil and grain, Song’s calamity would not have stopped at a wounded thigh and the slaughter of its officers [?]. Was it not Xiang, then, who brought this grief upon himself? That Song fortunately did not become Chu’s possession was due to Muyi. Can a state afford to delay employing the worthy and seeking good government?
“In the sixth month, the duke met with the Viscount of Shan, the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, and Guang, heir apparent of Qi. On the yiwei day [?], they jointly entered into a covenant at Jize.” Third year of 〔Duke Xiang〕.
Li Zhizhen.
Examiner Zhou, School Director, comments: 〔“Candidates generally treat censuring Chu and violating distinctions of rank together, seriously missing the fundamental…”〕

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
旨此篇融會傳意不瑣不遺可以式矣錄之
考試官教諭李　批　辭嚴義正
春秋紀上下之盟而著其懼外之失焉甚矣盟
不足恃也懼楚以盟諸侯之謀失矣故春秋譏
之如此昔晉因鄭服且欲脩吳好也乃即雞澤
盟焉春秋于此特書曰同者蓋是役也繁陽之
師猶在而獻子懷憂令尹之侵無紀而袁僑來
成楚爲中國患也亦甚迫矣于是晉倡之列國
從之而王臣若單頃公者亦預焉出三物以要
===
言志載書以辭是凡以爲楚也君子謂諸侯之
病楚深矣夫楚之可憂者勢也而其可恃以無
恐者不有安攘之策乎使能耀德懷貳而協義
以奠邦開誠布公而矢謀以禦侮則人心之衛
固於城郭忠信之字堅於甲冑荊楚雖强何畏
焉而乃約誓徒煩訂謨罔協在王臣旣不恩悖
信明義以表四方在列辟又不知尊主奉法以
保社稷先事弗備空懷知時之嗟卒使陳於繁
陽莫敢誰何則我之所以病楚者果何爲哉是
punctuated:
旨。此篇融會傳意，不瑣不遺，可以式矣，錄之。
考試官教諭李，批：辭嚴義正。
春秋紀上下之盟，而著其懼外之失焉。甚矣，盟不足恃也！懼楚以盟，諸侯之謀失矣，故春秋譏之如此。昔晉因鄭服，且欲脩吳好也，乃即雞澤盟焉。春秋于此特書曰「同」者，蓋是役也，繁陽之師猶在，而獻子懷憂；令尹之侵無紀，而袁僑來成。楚爲中國患也，亦甚迫矣。于是晉倡之，列國從之，而王臣若單頃公者亦預焉。出三物以要言，志載書以辭，是凡以爲楚也。君子謂諸侯之病楚深矣。夫楚之可憂者，勢也；而其可恃以無恐者，不有安攘之策乎？使能耀德懷貳，而協義以奠邦；開誠布公，而矢謀以禦侮，則人心之衛固於城郭，忠信之字堅於甲冑。荊楚雖强，何畏焉？而乃約誓徒煩，訂謨罔協。在王臣，旣不恩悖信明義以表四方；在列辟，又不知尊主奉法以保社稷。先事弗備，空懷知時之嗟，卒使陳於繁陽，莫敢誰何，則我之所以病楚者，果何爲哉？是
translation_en:
…the purport. This essay integrates the meaning of the commentary, neither becoming petty nor leaving anything out. It can serve as a model; let it be recorded.
Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: The language is stern and the principles correct.
The Spring and Autumn Annals records the covenant between superiors and inferiors and exposes their error in fearing an outside power. How utterly unreliable covenants are! In forming a covenant out of fear of Chu, the feudal lords erred in their planning; hence the Annals censures them in this way. Formerly, Jin, taking advantage of Zheng’s submission and also wishing to renew friendly relations with Wu, concluded a covenant at Jize. The Annals specifically writes “jointly” here because, at the time of this undertaking, the army at Fanyang was still present and Xianzi harbored anxieties; the chief minister’s incursions knew no restraint, and Yuan Qiao came to seek an accord. The threat Chu posed to the central states was indeed pressing. Thus Jin took the initiative, the other states followed, and royal ministers such as Duke Qing of Shan also participated. They brought out the three sacrificial objects to bind their pledged words and set their intentions down in the covenant document [?]. All this was directed against Chu. The gentleman observes that the feudal lords were deeply troubled by Chu.
What made Chu a source of anxiety was its power. Yet were there not policies for securing peace within and repelling threats from without on which they could rely to dispel their fear? Had they displayed their virtue to win over the wavering and united in righteousness to settle their states; had they acted with sincerity and impartiality and pledged themselves to plans for resisting aggression, then the protection afforded by the people’s hearts would have been stronger than city walls, and the care afforded by loyalty and trustworthiness firmer than armor and helmets. Though Jing-Chu was strong, what would there have been to fear? Instead, they merely multiplied agreements and oaths, while failing to agree in their deliberations. The royal ministers failed to uphold trustworthiness and make righteousness manifest as an example to the four quarters [preceding wording garbled: 恩悖信, ?]; the rulers of the states, for their part, did not know to honor their sovereign and observe established laws so as to preserve their altars of soil and grain. They made no preparations beforehand, merely nursing the lament of one who understood the times [?]. In the end, they allowed troops to be arrayed at Fanyang, with none daring to challenge them. What, then, had our efforts to counter the trouble posed by Chu actually accomplished? This …

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
雖上屢元老祇以修瀆分之惡耳思患不防馴
成棄陳之計卒使結言袁僑竟屬虛約恐楚之
所以病我者殆未艾也是雖八國同欲適以滋
反覆之習耳吾於天保而見其治內焉於釆薇
而見其治外焉先王之經理天下固自有令圖
也寧有惴惴焉徒懼如兹盟者乎諸侯之務亦
末矣故春秋特書曰同著同欲也蓋譏之也夫
豈以單子預盟故哉雖然晉悼賢侯也兹盟蓋
其召諸侯共謀不協之始乃所見亦若而人焉
===
且畀盟大夫以肇失政之端通吳於上國及向
之役始欲數不德以退之君子謂其規摹欲速
而諸侯失政悼實爲之惜也悼有君子之資而
未聞道也使加學問之功則樹建豈其謬拂至
此惜當時魏絳諸人無有以是語之者
禮記
是故樂在宗廟之中君臣上下同聽之則
莫不和敬
任有齡
punctuated:
雖上屢元老，祇以修瀆分之惡耳。思患不防，馴成棄陳之計，卒使結言袁僑，竟屬虛約，恐楚之所以病我者殆未艾也。是雖八國同欲，適以滋反覆之習耳。吾於《天保》而見其治內焉，於《釆薇》而見其治外焉。先王之經理天下，固自有令圖也，寧有惴惴焉徒懼如兹盟者乎？諸侯之務亦末矣！故《春秋》特書曰「同」，著同欲也，蓋譏之也。夫豈以單子預盟故哉？雖然，晉悼賢侯也，兹盟蓋其召諸侯共謀不協之始，乃所見亦若而人焉。且畀盟大夫，以肇失政之端；通吳於上國，及向之役，始欲數不德以退之。君子謂其規摹欲速，而諸侯失政，悼實爲之，惜也！悼有君子之資，而未聞道也。使加學問之功，則樹建豈其謬拂至此？惜當時魏絳諸人無有以是語之者。

禮記
是故樂在宗廟之中，君臣上下同聽之，則莫不和敬。
任有齡
translation_en:
…even though senior statesmen repeatedly participated [?], this merely perpetuated the evil of violating distinctions of rank. They considered dangers but took no precautions, gradually arriving at a plan to abandon Chen. In the end, the pledges made with Yuan Qiao proved empty agreements. I fear that Chu’s affliction of us was scarcely at an end. Thus, although the eight states shared a common desire, this merely fostered their habit of vacillation. In “Heaven Protects” (Tian bao), I see how they governed internal affairs; in “Gathering Bracken” (Cai wei), I see how they managed external affairs. The former kings certainly had excellent plans for ordering the world. Would they ever have trembled in mere apprehension, as those at this covenant did? The concerns of the feudal lords were indeed superficial!

Thus the Spring and Autumn Annals specifically records the word “together,” making their common desire explicit; its purpose is to criticize them. How could it have been because the Viscount of Shan participated in the covenant? Nevertheless, Duke Dao of Jin was a worthy lord. This covenant marked the beginning of his summoning the feudal lords to deliberate jointly on those who would not cooperate, yet his discernment proved no better than that of such men. Moreover, he entrusted covenant-making to the grandees, initiating the loss of governing authority. He brought Wu into relations with the states of the central realm, but only at the expedition to Xiang did he seek to enumerate its failings in virtue and send it away. The gentleman judges that his plans sought results too quickly, and that Duke Dao himself brought about the feudal lords’ loss of governing authority. What a pity! Duke Dao had the qualities of a gentleman, but had not heard the Way. Had he devoted himself further to study, could his undertakings have gone so far astray? It is regrettable that none of the men of that time, such as Wei Jiang, spoke to him about this.

Record of Rites
“Thus, when music is performed within the ancestral temple and ruler and ministers, high and low, listen to it together, none fails to become harmonious and reverent.”
Ren Youling

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭苂　批〔理趣充足辭氣悠揚誦之亦如聽和平之音不覺令人暢然悅豫非但致心之生而已〕
考試官教諭李　批〔題目冠冕此作亦能稱之〕
考試官學正周　批〔上下只就助祭諸臣說良是〕
樂作於廟而聽者皆感焉蓋君臣上下皆有事
於廟者也聽樂而莫不和敬焉則樂之所感者
深矣昔先王因人情之樂而欲道之正故制雅
頌之聲而一本之和聲音文理旣足樂而足論
始終節奏又盡善而盡美則其用也豈不極其
===
感乎是故宗廟者揭虔妥靈之地祖考在焉報
本反始之所昭穆列焉或特祭而掌礿之有行
則是樂必在所作洋洋乎旣和且平也或大祭
而禘祫之當舉則是樂必在所奏渢渢乎和正
以廣也斯時也以其分而言之有爲君爲臣者
焉而莫不樂聲之是聽以其位而言之有在上
在下者焉而罔不樂音之是聞夫天尊地卑而
君臣之分定固以敬爲主者况在宗廟之中乎
是故不患其不敬而惟患其不和也山高澤平
punctuated:
同考試官教諭苂批〔理趣充足，辭氣悠揚，誦之亦如聽和平之音，不覺令人暢然悅豫，非但致心之生而已。〕
考試官教諭李批〔題目冠冕，此作亦能稱之。〕
考試官學正周批〔上下只就助祭諸臣說，良是。〕
樂作於廟，而聽者皆感焉。蓋君臣上下，皆有事於廟者也。聽樂而莫不和敬焉，則樂之所感者深矣。昔先王因人情之樂而欲道之正，故制雅頌之聲，而一本之和。聲音文理旣足樂而足論，始終節奏又盡善而盡美，則其用也，豈不極其感乎？是故宗廟者，揭虔妥靈之地，祖考在焉；報本反始之所，昭穆列焉。或特祭而掌礿之有行，則是樂必在所作，洋洋乎旣和且平也；或大祭而禘祫之當舉，則是樂必在所奏，渢渢乎和正以廣也。斯時也，以其分而言之，有爲君爲臣者焉，而莫不樂聲之是聽；以其位而言之，有在上在下者焉，而罔不樂音之是聞。夫天尊地卑，而君臣之分定，固以敬爲主者，况在宗廟之中乎？是故不患其不敬，而惟患其不和也。山高澤平
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner Yin [?] (苂), Instructor: 〔Rich in principled insight, with a flowing and resonant expression. Reciting it is itself like hearing harmonious, peaceful music: it unwittingly makes one feel expansive and delighted, doing more than merely bringing the heart to life [?].〕
Comment by Examiner Li, Instructor: 〔The topic is dignified and imposing, and this composition measures up to it.〕
Comment by Examiner Zhou, School Instructor: 〔It is quite right to explain “those above and below” solely in terms of the ministers assisting at the sacrifice.〕
Music is performed in the ancestral temple, and all who hear it are moved. For ruler and ministers, those above and below, all have duties in the temple. When they hear the music, none fails to become harmonious and reverent: profound indeed is music’s influence upon them. In antiquity, the former kings drew upon the joy inherent in human feelings and sought to guide it toward what was right. They therefore established the music of the Court Hymns and Eulogies, grounding it entirely in harmony. Its sounds and patterned arrangements suffice both to delight and to warrant discussion; its rhythms and measures, from beginning to end, are perfectly good and perfectly beautiful. How, then, could its effect in performance fail to reach the utmost depth?
Thus the ancestral temple is a place for displaying devotion and settling the spirits, where one’s forebears are present; it is a place for repaying one’s origins and returning to one’s beginnings, where the ancestors are arrayed in the alternating zhao and mu ranks. When an individual sacrifice is held and the yue sacrifice is conducted [?], this music must be performed, flowing abundantly, harmonious and peaceful. When a great sacrifice is due and the di and xia rites must be celebrated, this music must be played, rich and full, harmonious, correct, and expansive. At such a time, considered in terms of their allotted roles, some are ruler and others ministers, yet all listen to the music’s sounds. Considered in terms of their positions, some are above and others below, yet all hear its tones.
Heaven is exalted and earth is lowly, and the distinction between ruler and ministers is fixed. Reverence is naturally their governing principle; how much more so within the ancestral temple! Thus the concern is not that they will lack reverence, but only that they will lack harmony. Mountains are high and marshes level …

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
而上下之位列亦以敬爲先者況在祭祀之所
乎是故非敬之艱而惟和之艱也今惟在廟而
與乎祭行禮而奏其樂吾知君臣之間一聞其
既和且平而天機爲之自動懽然相接而齋莊
以飾貌者自得乎安舒之美矣上下之際一聞
其和正以廣而天衷爲之自啓油然相與而恭
肅以檢外者自獲乎從容之常矣分雖嚴而心
則孚不以等威之辨而至於杆格焉猶之天地
定位而未甞不許合也君臣有不和敬者乎位
===
雖殊而情則洽不以勢分之懸而至於乖違焉
猶之山澤異形而未甞不通氣也上下有不和
敬者乎是則先王之作樂明而感人者既皆和
敬則幽而感神者昭格可知矣抑論之瓠巴鼓
瑟而游魚出聽伯牙鼓琴而六馬仰秣彼二子
特以琴瑟之音而且能感物如此況先王大成
之樂乎是故動天地感鬼神和上下育萬物而
致禎祥皆有不期然而然者觀之虞書及此經
所云斯可識矣蓋樂必本之性情稽之度數制
punctuated: 而上下之位列，亦以敬爲先者，況在祭祀之所乎？是故非敬之艱，而惟和之艱也。今惟在廟而與乎祭，行禮而奏其樂，吾知君臣之間，一聞其既和且平，而天機爲之自動，懽然相接，而齋莊以飾貌者，自得乎安舒之美矣。上下之際，一聞其和正以廣，而天衷爲之自啓，油然相與，而恭肅以檢外者，自獲乎從容之常矣。分雖嚴而心則孚，不以等威之辨而至於杆格焉，猶之天地定位而未甞不許合也。君臣有不和敬者乎？位雖殊而情則洽，不以勢分之懸而至於乖違焉，猶之山澤異形而未甞不通氣也。上下有不和敬者乎？是則先王之作樂，明而感人者既皆和敬，則幽而感神者昭格可知矣。抑論之，瓠巴鼓瑟而游魚出聽，伯牙鼓琴而六馬仰秣，彼二子特以琴瑟之音，而且能感物如此，況先王大成之樂乎？是故動天地，感鬼神，和上下，育萬物，而致禎祥，皆有不期然而然者。觀之《虞書》及此經所云，斯可識矣。蓋樂必本之性情，稽之度數，制
translation_en:
…and the positions of those above and below are arrayed in order, with reverence likewise taking precedence. How much more so at the place of sacrifice! Thus reverence is not what is difficult; harmony alone is difficult. Now, when they participate in sacrifices in the ancestral temple, performing the rites and playing the music, I know that, between ruler and ministers, as soon as they hear its harmony and balance, their innate impulses stir spontaneously. They meet one another joyfully, and those whose demeanor is marked by solemn dignity naturally attain the beauty of ease and composure. Between superiors and inferiors, as soon as they hear its harmony, correctness, and breadth, their Heaven-endowed hearts open spontaneously. They associate with one another freely, and those who restrain their outward conduct with respectful solemnity naturally attain lasting poise. Although their distinctions are strict, their hearts trust one another; distinctions of rank and dignity do not lead to obstruction and estrangement. It is like Heaven and Earth: their positions are fixed, yet they never fail to unite [?]. Could ruler and ministers fail to be harmonious and reverent? Although their positions differ, their feelings accord; the disparity in their power and station does not lead to discord. It is like mountains and marshes: their forms differ, yet their vital energies never fail to communicate. Could superiors and inferiors fail to be harmonious and reverent?

Thus, in the music made by the former kings, its manifest influence upon human beings brings all to harmony and reverence; we may therefore understand how its hidden influence upon the spirits brings them to manifest their presence. Consider further: when Hu Ba played the se zither, swimming fish emerged to listen; when Bo Ya played the qin zither, the six horses raised their heads from their fodder. Those two men could move other creatures in this way merely through the sounds of zithers. How much more could the fully perfected music of the former kings do so! Hence it moves Heaven and Earth, stirs ghosts and spirits, harmonizes superiors and inferiors, nurtures the myriad beings, and brings auspicious signs—all occurring spontaneously, without being deliberately sought. This can be understood by considering what is said in the Documents of Yu and in this Classic. For music must be rooted in human nature and feelings, examined against measures and numbers, and regulated…

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
之禮義極至和之妙而爲至德之音此其感召
之大所以至於如此也後世代變新聲祇足以
導欲而增悲者視先王之樂何如哉
民以君爲心君以民爲體
舒九齡
同考試官教諭艾　批〔講爲心爲體處親切有味其措〕
〔於體認而善於發揮者歟〕
考試官教諭李　批〔所以不可溺於民之意說得分曉〕
考試官學正周　批〔據理遣辭非稗筆可及〕
===
觀聖人之設喻而上下相須之義可見矣夫心
體通乎一身而倡之衛之者常相須也聖人近
取諸身以喻乎上下則人君之不可溺於民也
不亦可見乎夫子之意若謂君民之分雖殊相
須之義則一是故心在內而役乎四體者好惡
之由出也君雖非民之心而民則心之何也君
有所好民則從其好以爲已之好無有作好者
焉猶之目視而耳聽非耳目也由此心役之爾
君有所惡民則從其惡以爲已之惡無有作惡
punctuated:
之禮義，極至和之妙，而爲至德之音。此其感召之大，所以至於如此也。後世代變新聲，祇足以導欲而增悲者，視先王之樂何如哉？

民以君爲心，君以民爲體。
舒九齡
同考試官教諭艾　批〔講爲心爲體處，親切有味。其措〕〔於體認而善於發揮者歟？〕
考試官教諭李　批〔所以不可溺於民之意，說得分曉。〕
考試官學正周　批〔據理遣辭，非稗筆可及。〕

觀聖人之設喻，而上下相須之義可見矣。夫心體通乎一身，而倡之衛之者常相須也。聖人近取諸身以喻乎上下，則人君之不可溺於民也，不亦可見乎？夫子之意若謂：君民之分雖殊，相須之義則一。是故心在內而役乎四體者，好惡之由出也。君雖非民之心，而民則心之，何也？君有所好，民則從其好，以爲已之好，無有作好者焉。猶之目視而耳聽，非耳目也，由此心役之爾。君有所惡，民則從其惡，以爲已之惡，無有作惡
translation_en:
…regulated by ritual and rightness, it brings the subtle workings of supreme harmony to their utmost and becomes the music of consummate virtue. This is why its power to evoke responses reaches such greatness. In later ages, each era introduced new sounds that served only to arouse desire and deepen sorrow. How do these compare with the music of the former kings?

“The people take the ruler as their heart; the ruler takes the people as his body.”
By Shu Jiuling.
Associate Examiner Ai, Instructor, comments: 〔The explanation of serving as heart and body is immediate and meaningful. Is this someone grounded in personal apprehension [?] and skilled at elaborating its implications?〕
Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: 〔The reason the ruler must not allow himself to be submerged among the people is explained clearly.〕
Examiner Zhou, School Instructor, comments: 〔The wording rests on principle; no trifling writer could match it.〕

By considering the analogy established by the sage, we can see the principle of mutual dependence between those above and those below. Heart and body are interconnected within a single person: that which directs and that which protects always depend on one another. The sage drew an analogy close at hand, from the human person, to illustrate the relationship between those above and those below. Does this not also show that the ruler must not allow himself to be submerged among the people? The Master's meaning seems to be this: although ruler and people occupy different stations, the principle of mutual dependence is the same.

Thus the heart, situated within and directing the four limbs, is the source of likes and dislikes. Although the ruler is not the people's actual heart, the people nevertheless treat him as their heart. Why? When the ruler likes something, the people follow his liking and make it their own; none independently establishes a liking. This resembles the eyes seeing and the ears hearing: it is not the ears and eyes themselves that act, but this heart that directs them. When the ruler dislikes something, the people follow his dislike and make it their own; none independently establishes a dislike…

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
者焉猶之手持而足行非手足也由此心令之
爾過惡揚善而君之好惡正歟雖欲在民者之
不正不可得矣蓋心一斂而嚴威儼恪之容必
著也舉枉錯直而君之好惡僻歟雖欲在民者
之不僻亦不可得矣蓋心一縱而惰慢邪僻之
氣必見也所謂民以君爲心者如此若夫體在
外而衛乎一心者存亡之相關也民雖非君之
體而君則體之何也得衆則可以得國而至於
致治不循膚革充盈而中心悅豫乎非衆則罔
===
與守邦而難以圖存不循手足痿痺而憂心孔
疚乎耕食鑿飲而民皆安於樂利者非民之休
即君身之安富也饑寒疾苦而民不免於愁嘆
者非民之戚即君身之恫瘝也所謂君以民爲
體者如此由此觀之則倡之者必當盡其道而
使衛之者不至於失其職也又豈可以溺于民
哉考之書曰民心罔中惟爾之中是即民以君
爲心之意又曰恫瘝乃身是即君以民爲體之
意也古之人君深知乎此故必謹其心之好惡
punctuated: 者焉。猶之手持而足行，非手足也，由此心令之爾。過惡揚善，而君之好惡正歟？雖欲在民者之不正，不可得矣。蓋心一斂，而嚴威儼恪之容必著也。舉枉錯直，而君之好惡僻歟？雖欲在民者之不僻，亦不可得矣。蓋心一縱，而惰慢邪僻之氣必見也。所謂民以君爲心者如此。若夫體在外而衛乎一心者，存亡之相關也。民雖非君之體，而君則體之，何也？得衆則可以得國，而至於致治，不循膚革充盈而中心悅豫乎？非衆則罔與守邦，而難以圖存，不循手足痿痺而憂心孔疚乎？耕食鑿飲，而民皆安於樂利者，非民之休，即君身之安富也。饑寒疾苦，而民不免於愁嘆者，非民之戚，即君身之恫瘝也。所謂君以民爲體者如此。由此觀之，則倡之者必當盡其道，而使衛之者不至於失其職也。又豈可以溺于民哉？考之《書》曰：「民心罔中，惟爾之中。」是即民以君爲心之意。又曰：「恫瘝乃身。」是即君以民爲體之意也。古之人君深知乎此，故必謹其心之好惡
translation_en:
…none who originate dislikes of their own. It is like the hands grasping and the feet walking: it is not the hands and feet themselves that act, but the heart that commands them. If the ruler censures evil and commends goodness, so that his likes and dislikes are correct, could the people's fail to be correct, even if one wished it? Once the heart is disciplined, an appearance of solemn dignity and reverence necessarily manifests itself. If he promotes the crooked and sets them above the upright, so that his likes and dislikes are perverse, could the people's fail to be perverse, even if one wished it? Once the heart is unrestrained, an air of indolence, arrogance, and perversity necessarily appears. This is what is meant by saying that the people take the ruler as their heart.

As for the body's being outside and protecting the single heart within, their survival and destruction are bound together. Although the people are not literally the ruler's body, he treats them as his body. Why? By gaining the multitude, he can gain the state and ultimately bring about good government. Is this not like [?] the flesh being full and healthy and the heart within being joyful? Without the multitude, there is no one with whom to defend the realm, and its survival is difficult to secure. Is this not like [?] the hands and feet being withered and numb and the anxious heart being deeply distressed? When the people till the soil for food and dig wells for drink, all living contentedly in happiness and material benefit, their well-being is not theirs alone: it is the ruler's own security and prosperity. When they suffer hunger, cold, illness, and hardship, unable to escape sorrow and lamentation, their distress is not theirs alone: it is the ruler's own pain and suffering. This is what is meant by saying that the ruler takes the people as his body.

Viewed in this light, the one who leads must fully fulfill the Way proper to him, so that those who protect him do not fail in their duties. How, then, could he allow himself to be submerged among the people? Examining the Documents, we find: “The people's hearts have no constant mean; they take your mean as their own.” This expresses precisely the idea that the people take the ruler as their heart. It also says: “Pain and suffering in your own person.” This expresses precisely the idea that the ruler takes the people as his body. The rulers of antiquity understood this deeply; therefore, they invariably exercised care over the likes and dislikes in their hearts…

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
者非獨爲己而謹所以遏民之邪也厚其政之
教養者非特爲民而厚所以保吾之體也嗚呼
此其所以上下一德而久安長治也歟
第貳塲
論
至誠贊天地之化育
王纘宗
同考試官教諭吳　批〔根據義理而規模氣象正大光明〕
〔至誠參贊之功可想見矣〕
===
考試官教諭李　批〔豐贍高古可嘉可嘉〕
考試官學正周　批〔得至誠功用自然之妙〕
論曰天地萬物之性一也聖人能盡其性而天
地之用自我出矣蓋天地者誠之原也性之所
由出也化生萬物而誠斯立焉誠立而性具矣
聖人者人之至者也其性與天地萬物一也一
者誠也惟聖人之性與天地萬物一也故能盡
其性而天地萬物之性可一以貫之而無遺矣
人見天地定位萬物化醇若於聖人無與也而
punctuated:
者，非獨爲己而謹，所以遏民之邪也；厚其政之教養者，非特爲民而厚，所以保吾之體也。嗚呼！此其所以上下一德而久安長治也歟！

第貳塲

論

至誠贊天地之化育

王纘宗

同考試官教諭吳，批〔根據義理，而規模氣象正大光明。〕〔至誠參贊之功可想見矣。〕

考試官教諭李，批〔豐贍高古，可嘉，可嘉。〕

考試官學正周，批〔得至誠功用自然之妙。〕

論曰：天地萬物之性，一也。聖人能盡其性，而天地之用自我出矣。蓋天地者，誠之原也，性之所由出也。化生萬物，而誠斯立焉；誠立而性具矣。聖人者，人之至者也。其性與天地萬物一也。一者，誠也。惟聖人之性與天地萬物一也，故能盡其性，而天地萬物之性可一以貫之而無遺矣。人見天地定位，萬物化醇，若於聖人無與也，而
translation_en:
…they exercise this care not solely for their own sake, but to check wickedness among the people. They generously provide instruction and nourishment through their government not merely for the people’s sake, but to preserve their own body. Ah! Is this not how those above and below become one in virtue, securing lasting peace and enduring good government?

Second Session

Discourse

Utmost Sincerity Assists the Transforming and Nourishing Work of Heaven and Earth

Wang Zuanzong

Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor, comments: 〔Grounded in moral principle, its scope and spirit are upright, expansive, and luminous.〕〔One can envision the achievement of utmost sincerity in participating in and assisting this work.〕

Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: 〔Rich and ample, lofty and antique in style. Commendable, commendable!〕

Examiner Zhou, School Instructor, comments: 〔It captures the subtlety of the spontaneous efficacy of utmost sincerity.〕

The discourse states: The nature of Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things is one. The sage can fully realize his nature, and thus the workings of Heaven and Earth issue from his own self. Heaven and Earth are the source of sincerity and that from which nature proceeds. They transform and generate the myriad things, and sincerity is thereby established; with sincerity established, nature is fully endowed. The sage is the highest realization of humanity. His nature is one with that of Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things. This oneness is sincerity. Precisely because the sage’s nature is one with that of Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things, he can fully realize his nature; a single principle can thus run through the nature of Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things, leaving nothing out. People see Heaven and Earth occupying their appointed places and the myriad things undergoing transformation and maturation, as though the sage had no part in this, yet …

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
不知萬物皆備於我聖人所以參贊之道亦惟
取足於我而無待於外以成其能焉耳有待於
外則不可以語誠不可以語誠則不可以語聖
矣子思子論至誠之參贊而首以盡性言之其
至矣乎嘗讀中庸首篇而知夫天命之性矣而
知夫喜怒哀樂未發之中發皆中節之和矣而
知夫致中和而天地位萬物育矣夫天地位焉
萬物育焉其道大矣中和何與焉曰誠也中者
天下之大本也性也和者天下之達道也性而
===
情者也天地萬物之性亦由是而已故吾心正
而天地之心亦正吾氣順而天地之氣亦順非
有待於外也今夫乾父也坤母也民吾同胞也
物吾與也其夫父母兄弟其氣一也其疲癃殘疾惸獨鰥寡皆吾兄弟之
顛連而無告也夫父母兄弟其氣一也其氣一
則其性一知父母兄弟之性之一也又何獨於
天地萬物而疑之故聖人者天地之塞其體也
萬物之體一也天地之帥其性也萬物之性一
也故其所以裁成天地之道輔相天地之宜以
punctuated: 不知萬物皆備於我，聖人所以參贊之道，亦惟取足於我，而無待於外，以成其能焉耳。有待於外，則不可以語誠；不可以語誠，則不可以語聖矣。子思子論至誠之參贊，而首以盡性言之，其至矣乎！嘗讀《中庸》首篇，而知夫天命之性矣，而知夫喜怒哀樂未發之中、發皆中節之和矣，而知夫致中和而天地位、萬物育矣。夫天地位焉，萬物育焉，其道大矣，中和何與焉？曰：誠也。中者，天下之大本也，性也；和者，天下之達道也，性而情者也。天地萬物之性，亦由是而已。故吾心正，而天地之心亦正；吾氣順，而天地之氣亦順，非有待於外也。今夫乾，父也；坤，母也；民，吾同胞也；物，吾與也。其夫父母兄弟，其氣一也；其疲癃殘疾、惸獨鰥寡，皆吾兄弟之顛連而無告也。夫父母兄弟，其氣一也；其氣一，則其性一。知父母兄弟之性之一也，又何獨於天地萬物而疑之？故聖人者，天地之塞，其體也，萬物之體一也；天地之帥，其性也，萬物之性一也。故其所以裁成天地之道、輔相天地之宜，以
translation_en:
…not knowing that the myriad things are all complete within oneself. The way by which the sage participates in and assists the transforming and nourishing work of Heaven and Earth likewise consists solely in finding sufficiency within himself, without depending on anything external, thereby fully realizing his capacity. If there is dependence on anything external, one cannot speak of sincerity; if one cannot speak of sincerity, one cannot speak of sagehood. When Master Zisi discussed how perfect sincerity participates in and assists this work, he began by speaking of fully realizing one’s nature. How consummate his account is!

I have read the opening chapter of the Doctrine of the Mean and thereby understood the nature conferred by Heaven; understood the equilibrium before pleasure, anger, sorrow, and joy arise, and the harmony when their expression invariably accords with due measure; and understood that, when equilibrium and harmony are brought to their fullest realization, Heaven and Earth take their proper places and the myriad things are nourished. Heaven and Earth taking their places and the myriad things being nourished—great indeed is this Way! What part do equilibrium and harmony play in it? The answer is sincerity. Equilibrium is the great foundation of all under Heaven: it is nature. Harmony is the universally prevailing Way of all under Heaven: it is nature manifesting as feelings. The nature of Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things likewise proceeds from this alone. Thus, when my heart is upright, the heart of Heaven and Earth is also upright; when my vital force is in accord, the vital force of Heaven and Earth is also in accord. This does not depend on anything external.

Now Qian is father, and Kun is mother; the people are my siblings, and the other creatures are my companions. As for fathers, mothers, and siblings [?], their vital force is one; the infirm, disabled, orphaned, solitary, widowed men and widowed women among them are all my siblings in distress, with no one to whom they can appeal. Fathers, mothers, and siblings share one vital force; since their vital force is one, their nature is one. Once we recognize the unity of the nature of parents and siblings, why should we doubt it only in the case of Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things? Thus, for the sage, that which fills Heaven and Earth constitutes his body: the bodies of the myriad things are one. That which directs Heaven and Earth constitutes his nature: the natures of the myriad things are one. Thus, the means by which he shapes and completes the Way of Heaven and Earth and assists what is fitting to Heaven and Earth, in order to…

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
左右民者於已取之而已矣於已取之而皇極
由是建焉皇極建而天地萬物皆有以範圍而
不過曲成而不遺矣由今觀之始之以五行也
敬之以五事也厚之以八政也恊之以五紀也
乂之以三德也明之以稽疑也驗之以庶徵也
勸懲之以福極也皆聖人參贊之迹也皆吾之
性也亦皆天地萬物之性也聖人特因其所固
有而先之耳因其所固有而先之而尤恐其未
至故王省惟歲卿士惟月師尹惟日者非他也
===
所以考乎失得之故以驗吾性何如也故仰觀
乎天陰陽相摩天地相蕩鼓之以雷霆奮之以
風雨動之以四時煖之以日月而百化興焉而
天道官矣俯觀乎地草木茂區萌達羽翼奮角
觡生蟄蟲昭蘇羽者嫗伏毛者孕鬻胎生不殰
卵生不殈而地道察矣中觀於人君君臣臣父
父子子夫夫婦婦長長幼幼以等貴賤以辨尊
卑以和上下以别内外以明遠邇而人道立矣
故聖人能以天下爲一家以中國爲一人者非
punctuated: 左右民者，於已取之而已矣。於已取之，而皇極由是建焉。皇極建，而天地萬物皆有以範圍而不過，曲成而不遺矣。由今觀之，始之以五行也，敬之以五事也，厚之以八政也，恊之以五紀也，乂之以三德也，明之以稽疑也，驗之以庶徵也，勸懲之以福極也，皆聖人參贊之迹也，皆吾之性也，亦皆天地萬物之性也。聖人特因其所固有而先之耳。因其所固有而先之，而尤恐其未至，故「王省惟歲，卿士惟月，師尹惟日」者，非他也，所以考乎失得之故，以驗吾性何如也。故仰觀乎天，陰陽相摩，天地相蕩，鼓之以雷霆，奮之以風雨，動之以四時，煖之以日月，而百化興焉，而天道官矣。俯觀乎地，草木茂，區萌達，羽翼奮，角觡生，蟄蟲昭蘇，羽者嫗伏，毛者孕鬻，胎生不殰，卵生不殈，而地道察矣。中觀於人，君君，臣臣，父父，子子，夫夫，婦婦，長長，幼幼，以等貴賤，以辨尊卑，以和上下，以别内外，以明遠邇，而人道立矣。故聖人能以天下爲一家，以中國爲一人者，非
translation_en:
…in order to assist the people, they draw only upon themselves. By drawing upon themselves, they thereby establish the August Standard. Once the August Standard is established, Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things are all encompassed without exceeding their bounds, and each is brought to fulfillment in its particular circumstances without omission. Viewed from this perspective, beginning with the Five Phases, cultivating reverence through the Five Activities, enriching life through the Eight Affairs of Government, bringing harmony through the Five Regulators of Time, establishing order through the Three Virtues, attaining clarity through the Examination of Doubts, testing through the Various Signs, and encouraging and admonishing through Blessings and Calamities—all these are manifestations of the sage’s participation in and assistance to the transforming work of Heaven and Earth. All belong to my nature, and all likewise belong to the nature of Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things. The sage merely draws upon what is inherently present in them and takes the lead. Yet even while doing so, he fears that his efforts may fall short. Thus the statement, “The king examines the year, the high ministers the month, and the officials the day,” has no other purpose than to investigate the causes of failure and success, thereby testing the condition of my own nature.

Thus, looking upward at Heaven, we see yin and yang interacting and Heaven and Earth stirring one another. Thunder rouses things; wind and rain set them in motion; the four seasons impel them; and the sun and moon warm them. The hundred transformations arise, and the Way of Heaven fulfills its office [?]. Looking downward at Earth, we see plants and trees flourishing, shoots emerging, wings spreading, and horns and antlers growing. Hibernating creatures awaken and revive; feathered creatures brood over their eggs, and furry creatures conceive and give birth. Live-born young do not perish in the womb, and eggs do not spoil before hatching. Thus the Way of Earth becomes manifest. Looking between them at humankind, we see rulers acting as rulers, ministers as ministers, fathers as fathers, sons as sons, husbands as husbands, wives as wives, elders as elders, and juniors as juniors. Through this, the noble and lowly are ranked, the honored and humble distinguished, superiors and inferiors brought into harmony, inner and outer differentiated, and relations with those distant and near clarified. Thus the human Way is established. Therefore, that the sage can regard all under Heaven as one family and the Central Kingdom as one person is not…

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
意之也必知其情辟於其義明於其利達於其
患然後能爲之故曰誠之不可掩如此昔者堯
舜禹稷伊尹數聖人者之憂民也若己溺之也
若己饑之也若己推而納之溝中也汲汲然斷
以爲己任而莫之辭也其心何心哉蓋誠見乎
天地萬物莫非我也故斯民有一未得其所則
吾性猶有未盡也吾性未盡則吾任未副其如天
地萬物何哉故曰萬物皆備於我也反身而誠
樂莫大焉反身而誠則能盡其性能盡萬物之
===
性而後化育行天地參而後聖人之心始樂抑
天地之常以其心普萬物而無心聖人之常以
其情順萬事而無情天地聖人一而已矣故曰
誠者天之道也君子之學所以求至乎天也求
至乎天者求盡其性而已求盡其性者求定其
性而已曰廓然而大公物來而順應也曰無將
迎無內外也以無爲爲應迹以明覺爲自然也
此皆定性之說也故君子必先定性而後可以
語盡性
punctuated:
意之也，必知其情，辟於其義，明於其利，達於其患，然後能爲之。故曰：「誠之不可掩如此。」昔者堯、舜、禹、稷、伊尹，數聖人者之憂民也，若己溺之也，若己饑之也，若己推而納之溝中也，汲汲然斷以爲己任而莫之辭也。其心何心哉？蓋誠見乎天地萬物莫非我也。故斯民有一未得其所，則吾性猶有未盡也；吾性未盡，則吾任未副，其如天地萬物何哉？故曰：「萬物皆備於我也。反身而誠，樂莫大焉。」反身而誠，則能盡其性，能盡萬物之性，而後化育行，天地參，而後聖人之心始樂。
抑天地之常，以其心普萬物而無心；聖人之常，以其情順萬事而無情。天地、聖人，一而已矣。故曰：「誠者，天之道也。」君子之學，所以求至乎天也。求至乎天者，求盡其性而已；求盡其性者，求定其性而已。曰：「廓然而大公，物來而順應也。」曰：「無將迎，無內外也。」以無爲爲應迹，以明覺爲自然也。此皆定性之說也。故君子必先定性，而後可以語盡性。
translation_en:
…merely by imagining it. He must understand their circumstances, comprehend what is right for them, discern what benefits them, and grasp what troubles them; only then can he accomplish this. Thus it is said: “Such is the impossibility of concealing sincerity.” In antiquity, the sages Yao, Shun, Yu, Ji, and Yi Yin were concerned for the people as though they themselves had drowned them, starved them, or pushed them into a ditch. Anxiously and resolutely, they took this as their own responsibility, and none declined it. What sort of heart was theirs? They truly perceived that Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things were all part of themselves. Thus, if even one person among the people has not found their proper place, my own nature remains incompletely fulfilled. If my nature remains unfulfilled, I have not discharged my responsibility: how, then, can I answer to Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things? Thus it is said: “The myriad things are all complete within me. To turn back upon oneself and find sincerity—there is no greater joy.” By turning back upon oneself and achieving sincerity, one can fully realize one’s own nature and the nature of the myriad things. Only then do transformation and nurture proceed, and one joins Heaven and Earth as a third; only then does the sage’s heart begin to rejoice.
Moreover, the constant way of Heaven and Earth is to extend their heart throughout the myriad things while having no deliberate intention; the constant way of the sage is to respond through his feelings to the myriad affairs while having no private emotional attachments. Heaven, Earth, and the sage are simply one. Thus it is said: “Sincerity is the Way of Heaven.” The learning of the noble man is the means by which he seeks to attain Heaven. Seeking to attain Heaven is simply seeking to realize his nature fully; seeking to realize his nature fully is simply seeking to stabilize it. It is said: “Be expansively and wholly impartial, responding fittingly to things as they come.” It is also said: “Neither anticipate nor seek to welcome things; make no distinction between inner and outer.” Take action without contrivance as the outward expression of response, and lucid awareness as what is natural. These are all explanations of stabilizing one’s nature. Thus the noble man must first stabilize his nature before one can speak of fully realizing it.

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
同前　　　　　　　　于鶴
同考試官教諭翟　批〔渾金璞玉精華自在宜弁録〕
以式
考試官教諭李　批〔理明辭到〕
考試官學正周　批〔古雅〕
聖人所以成天地之能而與之參者亦惟盡性
而已矣夫天地之道大矣聖人一身混然中處
而有以參之何哉蓋人物之生莫不有性而化
===
育流行莫非天地之所性也天地能與人物以
性而不能使之各盡其性是故必有待于聖人
聖人之性與人同而踐形盡性則與人異是以
會人物於一身而以其盡諸已者盡諸人與物
而無不得其所之憾則天地之所不及者聖人
有以贊而成之聖人之化育一天地也天地無
心而成化聖人有心而無爲夫豈可以形器囿
哉於乎斯道也其惟天下之至誠乎至誠贊天
地之化育子思之言非自子思始也嘗觀諸易
punctuated:
同前，于鶴。
同考試官教諭翟批〔渾金璞玉，精華自在，宜弁録〕以式。
考試官教諭李批〔理明辭到〕。
考試官學正周批〔古雅〕。
聖人所以成天地之能而與之參者，亦惟盡性而已矣。夫天地之道大矣，聖人一身混然中處，而有以參之，何哉？蓋人物之生，莫不有性，而化育流行，莫非天地之所性也。天地能與人物以性，而不能使之各盡其性，是故必有待于聖人。聖人之性與人同，而踐形盡性則與人異。是以會人物於一身，而以其盡諸已者盡諸人與物，而無不得其所之憾，則天地之所不及者，聖人有以贊而成之。聖人之化育，一天地也。天地無心而成化，聖人有心而無爲，夫豈可以形器囿哉？於乎！斯道也，其惟天下之至誠乎！至誠贊天地之化育，子思之言，非自子思始也。嘗觀諸《易》
translation_en:
On the same topic as above. By Yu He 于鶴.
Associate Examiner Zhai, Instructor, comments: “Unrefined gold and uncarved jade: their essential brilliance is inherent. This should head the record to serve as a model.”
Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “The principles are clear and the expression apt.”
Examiner Zhou, School Instructor, comments: “Classical and elegant.”
The means by which the sage brings Heaven and Earth’s capacities to fulfillment and stands alongside them as a third is simply the full realization of his nature. The Way of Heaven and Earth is vast. How can the sage, a single person dwelling harmoniously between them, stand alongside them? All people and things possess a nature from birth, and the ceaseless flow of transformation and nurture is wholly an expression of the nature of Heaven and Earth. Heaven and Earth can endow people and things with their natures, but cannot make each fully realize its nature. Thus they must depend upon the sage. The sage’s nature is the same as that of other people, but he differs from them in fulfilling his bodily form and fully realizing his nature. Thus he brings people and things together within his own person; through fully realizing his own nature, he enables people and things to realize theirs, leaving none with the regret of failing to find its proper place. What Heaven and Earth cannot accomplish, the sage assists and brings to completion. In his transforming and nurturing activity, the sage is himself a Heaven and Earth. Heaven and Earth accomplish transformation without conscious intention; the sage possesses conscious intention yet acts without contrivance. How could he be confined by physical forms and vessels?
Ah! Is this Way not attainable only through the utmost sincerity under Heaven? That utmost sincerity assists the transforming and nurturing activity of Heaven and Earth—these words of Zisi did not originate with Zisi himself. I have examined this in the Book of Changes …

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
矣曰后以裁成天地之道輔相天地之宜以左
右民又曰易與天地準故能彌綸天地之道又
曰天地設位聖人成能聖人之心根諸誠聖人
之誠盡諸易易也者聖人之化育也是故言之
不一而裁成而輔相而彌綸以成能則固未甞
與天地異也天地非至誠則道幾乎息曷成其
化育之盛聖人非至誠則道亦幾乎息曷成其
贊化育之能故天地有聖人則造化有全功聖
人惟盡性則天地無餘事而人物之責成於我
===
者不孤矣今夫化育流行性命各正得其正且
通者爲人得其偏且塞者爲物聖人亦人爾性
天地之帥體天地之塞未始不與人同而其異
於物者亦幾希也然形得以圍之見得以梏之
分得以拘之而人之性不能自盡也非惟人之
性不能自盡也而物之性亦不能自盡也人物
之不能自盡天地不能盡之也於是聖人者作
心爲太極道爲太極靜虛動直明通公溥一誠
之極而無所矯焉其天下之至誠乎夫語誠而
punctuated:
矣。曰：「后以裁成天地之道，輔相天地之宜，以左右民。」又曰：「易與天地準，故能彌綸天地之道。」又曰：「天地設位，聖人成能。」聖人之心根諸誠，聖人之誠盡諸易。易也者，聖人之化育也。是故言之不一，而裁成，而輔相，而彌綸以成能，則固未甞與天地異也。天地非至誠，則道幾乎息，曷成其化育之盛？聖人非至誠，則道亦幾乎息，曷成其贊化育之能？故天地有聖人，則造化有全功；聖人惟盡性，則天地無餘事，而人物之責成於我者不孤矣。
今夫化育流行，性命各正，得其正且通者爲人，得其偏且塞者爲物。聖人亦人爾，性天地之帥，體天地之塞，未始不與人同，而其異於物者亦幾希也。然形得以圍之，見得以梏之，分得以拘之，而人之性不能自盡也。非惟人之性不能自盡也，而物之性亦不能自盡也。人物之不能自盡，天地不能盡之也。於是聖人者作，心爲太極，道爲太極，靜虛動直，明通公溥，一誠之極，而無所矯焉。其天下之至誠乎！夫語誠而
translation_en:
…It says: “The ruler thereby shapes and completes the Way of Heaven and Earth, assists what is fitting in Heaven and Earth, and thus guides the people.” It also says: “The Changes accords with Heaven and Earth, and therefore can encompass and weave together the Way of Heaven and Earth.” Again it says: “Heaven and Earth establish their positions, and the sage brings their capacities to completion.” The sage’s mind is rooted in sincerity; the sage’s sincerity finds its fullest realization in the Changes. The Changes is the sage’s work of transformation and nurture. Thus, although the expressions differ—shaping and completing, assisting, encompassing and weaving together to bring capacities to completion—these activities have never differed from those of Heaven and Earth. Without utmost sincerity, the Way of Heaven and Earth would all but cease: how could they accomplish their abundant transformation and nurture? Without utmost sincerity, the sage’s Way would likewise all but cease: how could he fulfill his capacity to assist transformation and nurture? Thus, when Heaven and Earth have a sage, the work of creation is complete. Only when the sage fully realizes the nature of things does the work of Heaven and Earth leave nothing undone; then the trust that people and things place in me to bring them to fulfillment is not betrayed.
Now, as transformation and nurture flow onward, each being receives its proper nature and allotted endowment. Those receiving what is balanced and unobstructed become human beings; those receiving what is partial and obstructed become other creatures. The sage, too, is merely human. He takes as his nature the commanding principle of Heaven and Earth, and as his body that which fills Heaven and Earth. In this he has never differed from other people, and what distinguishes him from other creatures is likewise very slight. Yet bodily form can hem people in, their views can shackle them, and their allotted circumstances can constrain them, so that human nature cannot reach fulfillment on its own. Nor is it only human nature that cannot fulfill itself: the natures of other creatures likewise cannot fulfill themselves. Where people and things cannot fulfill themselves, Heaven and Earth cannot bring them to fulfillment. Thereupon the sage arises. His mind is the Supreme Ultimate, and his Way is the Supreme Ultimate: empty in stillness, upright in activity, lucid and penetrating, impartial and all-embracing. All is the culmination of a single sincerity, without anything forced. Is this not the utmost sincerity under Heaven? Now, in speaking of sincerity and…

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
至於天下之至誠則性之在我者無不盡矣吾
盡吾性而視人物之所不盡者不自我以盡之
豈天地萬物一體之仁乎如是則非所以爲聖
人聖人之心亦隘矣而又何以贊天地之化育
哉何則有盛德必有大業蓋兼天地而成其仁
知必周知而知之無不明立必俱立而處之無
不當其施之天下國家也治之而爭奪息教之
而倫理明導之而生養遂所以盡人之性焉因
其材質之宜以致其用制其撙節之方以遂其
===
生所以盡物之性焉布之而爲九經建之而爲
三重散之而爲三千三百錯之而爲容爲執爲
敬爲別極之而經綸大經建立大本以至篤恭
而天下平則百姓太和萬物咸若化之極也何
莫而非所以盡人物之性焉夫舉人物之性範
圍之而不過曲成之而不遺而聖人之心始遂
矣然非分我所有以益之也取諸彼而自足聖
人又何事焉其功用至是則口代天言身代天
工心代天意化育之功不在天地而在聖人矣
punctuated: 至於天下之至誠，則性之在我者無不盡矣。吾盡吾性，而視人物之所不盡者，不自我以盡之，豈天地萬物一體之仁乎？如是，則非所以爲聖人，聖人之心亦隘矣，而又何以贊天地之化育哉？何則？有盛德，必有大業，蓋兼天地而成其仁。知必周知，而知之無不明；立必俱立，而處之無不當。其施之天下國家也，治之而爭奪息，教之而倫理明，導之而生養遂，所以盡人之性焉。因其材質之宜以致其用，制其撙節之方以遂其生，所以盡物之性焉。布之而爲九經，建之而爲三重，散之而爲三千三百，錯之而爲容、爲執、爲敬、爲別，極之而經綸大經、建立大本，以至篤恭而天下平，則百姓太和，萬物咸若，化之極也。何莫而非所以盡人物之性焉？夫舉人物之性，範圍之而不過，曲成之而不遺，而聖人之心始遂矣。然非分我所有以益之也，取諸彼而自足，聖人又何事焉？其功用至是，則口代天言，身代天工，心代天意，化育之功不在天地而在聖人矣。
translation_en:
…when it reaches the utmost sincerity under Heaven, nothing of the nature within oneself remains unfulfilled. If I fulfill my own nature, yet, seeing what remains unfulfilled in the natures of people and things, do not myself bring it to fulfillment, can this be the benevolence that forms one body with Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things? Such conduct would not constitute sagehood; the sage’s heart would itself be narrow. How, then, could he assist the transforming and nourishing work of Heaven and Earth? Why is this so? Abundant virtue must issue in great achievements: his benevolence achieves fulfillment by embracing Heaven and Earth. His knowing must extend comprehensively to all, leaving nothing obscure in his understanding; in establishing himself, he must establish all together, leaving nothing improperly placed. Applied to the world and its states and families, this means governing people so that contention and strife cease, teaching them so that human relationships become clear, and guiding them so that their livelihood and nurture are secured. These are the means of fulfilling human nature. Bringing things into use according to the suitability of their material qualities, and establishing methods of restraint and moderation so that their life may flourish: these are the means of fulfilling the nature of things.

Set forth, this becomes the nine guiding principles; instituted, it becomes the three weighty matters; elaborated, it becomes the three thousand and three hundred rules of ritual. Applied in their various settings, these govern demeanor, the holding of objects, reverence, and distinctions. Carried to their utmost, they order the great enduring relationships and establish the great foundation, until, through profound reverence, all under Heaven is at peace. Then the people enjoy supreme harmony and the myriad things all follow their proper course: this is transformation at its utmost. Which of these is not a means of fulfilling the natures of people and things? Only when the sage embraces all these natures, encompassing them without overstepping and bringing each to fulfillment in its particular circumstances without omission, is his heart’s purpose realized. Yet he does not divide up what he himself possesses to supplement them. What is drawn from them is sufficient in itself; what further undertaking, then, is required of the sage? When his efficacy reaches this point, his mouth speaks on Heaven’s behalf, his person performs Heaven’s work, and his heart acts for Heaven’s intent. The achievement of transformation and nurture then rests with the sage, rather than with Heaven and Earth.

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
謂之曰贊天地之化育與天地參不其然乎是
可以見體信達順之道誠感神應之機矣先天
而天弗違後天而奉天時所過者化所存者神
上下與天地同流即至誠贊化育之謂也向使
聖人之心或有毫髮未盡則機滯而化塞感淺
而應微施諸一事一物或未得其理而欲使天
地位萬物育有是理哉粤稽諸古恊和時雍惠
疇咸熙堯舜之化育也庶績其凝兆民允懷遵
化垂拱裒時對命禹湯文武之化育也立之斯
===
立道之斯行綏之斯來動之斯和孔子之化育
也皆有以贊天地而成其能殆不可以窮達言
也非至誠之盡性其孰能之雖然誠一也何聖
人至誠盡性而吾人弗若也蓋有生之後不攻
於雜揉則蕩於嗜慾莫之振拔而聖凡逈矣故
立教者使之由致曲之功積而至於能化則立
誠以立人之極亦不異於聖人矣故曰誠者聖
功之本
叔
punctuated:
謂之曰贊天地之化育、與天地參，不其然乎？是可以見體信達順之道、誠感神應之機矣。先天而天弗違，後天而奉天時；所過者化，所存者神；上下與天地同流，即至誠贊化育之謂也。向使聖人之心或有毫髮未盡，則機滯而化塞，感淺而應微；施諸一事一物，或未得其理，而欲使天地位、萬物育，有是理哉？粤稽諸古，恊和時雍，惠疇咸熙，堯舜之化育也；庶績其凝，兆民允懷，遵化垂拱，裒時對命，禹湯文武之化育也；立之斯立，道之斯行，綏之斯來，動之斯和，孔子之化育也。皆有以贊天地而成其能，殆不可以窮達言也。非至誠之盡性，其孰能之？雖然，誠一也，何聖人至誠盡性，而吾人弗若也？蓋有生之後，不攻於雜揉，則蕩於嗜慾，莫之振拔，而聖凡逈矣。故立教者使之由致曲之功，積而至於能化，則立誠以立人之極，亦不異於聖人矣。故曰：「誠者，聖功之本。」

叔
translation_en:
…To call this “assisting Heaven and Earth in their transforming and nourishing work, and forming a triad with Heaven and Earth”—is this not indeed fitting? Here we can perceive the Way of embodying trustworthiness and attaining harmony, and the workings by which sincerity moves and the spiritual responds. When the sage acts before Heaven, Heaven does not oppose him; when he acts after Heaven, he follows Heaven’s seasons. Wherever he passes, transformation occurs; wherever he abides, his influence is spiritual. Above and below, he flows together with Heaven and Earth. This is precisely what is meant by utmost sincerity assisting their transforming and nourishing work.

If the sage’s heart had left even the slightest part unrealized, these workings would be impeded and transformation obstructed; his power to move would be shallow and the response slight. If, in dealing with a single affair or thing, he had perhaps failed to grasp its principle, yet wished Heaven and Earth to take their proper places and the myriad things to flourish, could this be possible? Examining antiquity, we find harmonious concord and universal peace, favorable ordering and general flourishing [?]: these were the transforming and nourishing achievements of Yao and Shun. The consolidation of all accomplishments, the sincere allegiance of the countless people, transformation followed while the ruler sat with folded hands, and the ample fulfillment of Heaven’s mandate: these were the transforming and nourishing achievements of Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu. “When he establishes them, they stand; when he guides them, they proceed; when he comforts them, they come; when he stirs them, they attain harmony”: these were the transforming and nourishing achievements of Confucius. All possessed the means to assist Heaven and Earth and bring their capacities to fulfillment. This can hardly be judged in terms of whether they lacked or attained public office. Who could accomplish it without fully realizing their nature through utmost sincerity?

Nevertheless, sincerity is one and the same. Why, then, do sages fully realize their nature through utmost sincerity, while we fall short? After birth, unless we are assailed by mixed and impure influences, we are swept away by appetites and desires. With nothing to rouse us and lift us free, sages and ordinary people become far apart. Thus those who establish the teaching have people begin with the work of bringing sincerity to fulfillment in particular aspects of their nature, accumulating effort until they become capable of transforming others. By establishing sincerity, they establish the highest standard of humanity, and in this they are no different from sages. Thus it is said: “Sincerity is the foundation of the work of sagehood.”

Shu [?; isolated character].

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
擬翰林學士承旨兼吏部尚書詹同等
進

張國珎
同考試官教諭朱　批〔揄揚〕

punctuated:

translation_en:
Memorial submitting the Daily Calendar of the Great Ming, composed in the person of Zhan Tong, Hanlin Academician Recipient of Edicts and concurrently Minister of Personnel, and his colleagues. Seventh year of Hongwu [1374].
By Zhang Guozhen.
Associate Examiner Zhu, Instructor, comments: “Extols the magnificence of the sagely founder’s achievements. The final couplet especially reveals loyalty and affection. Even had the ministers of that time spoken for themselves, they could have said no more than this.”
Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: “He has fashioned an essay by distilling the main purport of the Daily Calendar: truly an accomplished writer.”
Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “Elegant parallel prose, dignified and correct. Include it.”
Examiner Zhou, School Director, comments: “The composition is worthy of attention.”
On a certain day of a certain month in the seventh year of Hongwu, your servants, so-and-so and others, holding the specified offices, state: Having now completed the compilation of the Daily Calendar of the Great Ming, we have respectfully made a fair copy and bound it into volumes, which we submit with this memorial.
We humbly consider: Having first received the great Mandate, Your Majesty gloriously unites the Chinese and the peoples beyond for ten thousand generations; now completed, this great compilation records the events and makes manifest the abundance of the Son of Heaven’s virtue and achievements. Founded upon facts, it records them without distortion, so that evidence may be consulted and a trustworthy account transmitted. We have therefore compiled this Daily Calendar and venture to submit it to…

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
天聰臣等懽忭懽忭頓首頓首上言自昔明君
必有左右史以書其舉後世人主乃設起
居注以擬其官重其事則以台輔監修取
其才盛以中丞兼領禁林之彥固係專門
別署之英亦資秉筆名銜雖則有異責任
未嘗不同珥管操觚務取見聞之實更番
遞直互求言動之詳金匱石室之所藏蘭
臺芸閣之所貯雖越宇宙爲遼今稽簡帙
猶存世道之治亂興衰可以視諸掌上史
筆之是非曲直舉莫逃於目前相古皆然
===
惟
今爲盛時方向乎偃武衆咸樂于修文恭惟
皇帝陛下
藉世累仁
荷
天眷命神武不殺而無敵
剛柔相濟以有爲粤自
提義旅而奮起臨濠以至驅胡元之遁還朔
punctuated:
天聰。臣等懽忭懽忭，頓首頓首，上言：自昔明君，必有左右史以書其舉；後世人主，乃設起居注以擬其官。重其事，則以台輔監修；取其才，盛以中丞兼領。禁林之彥，固係專門；別署之英，亦資秉筆。名銜雖則有異，責任未嘗不同。珥管操觚，務取見聞之實；更番遞直，互求言動之詳。金匱石室之所藏，蘭臺芸閣之所貯，雖越宇宙爲遼，今稽簡帙猶存。世道之治亂興衰，可以視諸掌上；史筆之是非曲直，舉莫逃於目前。相古皆然，惟今爲盛。
時方向乎偃武，衆咸樂于修文。恭惟皇帝陛下，藉世累仁，荷天眷命，神武不殺而無敵，剛柔相濟以有爲。粤自提義旅而奮起臨濠，以至驅胡元之遁還朔
translation_en:
…to Your Majesty’s hearing. We, your servants, rejoice, rejoice; we knock our heads upon the ground, twice, and submit: Since antiquity, enlightened rulers have always had Scribes of the Left and Right to record their actions. Rulers of later ages established posts for recording the Diaries of Activity, modeling them on those earlier offices. Because they regarded this work as important, they appointed chief ministers to supervise its compilation; to secure men of talent, they also placed Vice Censors-in-Chief concurrently in charge [?]. The distinguished scholars of the Hanlin Academy were certainly specialists, but talented men from other offices were also called upon to wield the brush. Although their titles differed, their responsibilities were always the same. With writing brushes tucked beside their ears and writing tablets in hand, they sought truthful accounts of what was seen and heard; serving on duty in rotation, they worked together to obtain detailed records of words and actions. What was preserved in golden coffers and stone chambers, what was stored in the Orchid Terrace and the book repositories, survives today for consultation in its volumes, despite vast distances in space and time. Order and disorder, rise and decline in the affairs of the world can be seen as plainly as something held in the palm; the rights and wrongs, distortions and rectitude recorded by the historian’s brush all lie exposed before our eyes. Such was the practice throughout antiquity, but only now has it attained its greatest flourishing.
The times were turning toward laying down arms, and all delighted in cultivating civil accomplishments. We reverently consider that Your Imperial Majesty, drawing upon benevolence accumulated over generations and receiving Heaven’s favor and mandate, possessed divine martial prowess, invincible without killing, and accomplished great deeds by balancing firmness with gentleness. From the time you raised a righteous army and rose at Linhao, until you drove the Mongol Yuan into retreat back to the northern…

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
漢東征西討壺漿簞食紛迎
天與人歸訟獄謳歌畢至僭亂旣平而
戎衣遂釋豈論歸馬之三千臣民上請而
黼扆斯登允應
飛龍於九五霈普天之霖雨洗滌腥羶轟奮
地之雷霆震驚聾聵
聖人作而萬物覩胥有快于乘時
天地革而四時成孰不忻于改命遡自乙未之
夏至於癸丑之冬凡戒諭之諄嚴及征誅
===
之次第禮樂制度之沿革刑威爵賞之重
輕酌古準今皆
精神心術之運用興衰撥亂一
仁義道德之敷宣仰觀
聖人之大有所爲固詳陳之不足比諸
天地之一言而盡亦條列之可該語
功烈之高迥出百王之上得
國統之正同符兩漢之興
堯神湯智而獨禀維全謨略匪臣工所能贊
punctuated: 漢，東征西討，壺漿簞食紛迎，天與人歸，訟獄謳歌畢至。僭亂旣平，而戎衣遂釋，豈論歸馬之三千？臣民上請，而黼扆斯登，允應飛龍於九五。霈普天之霖雨，洗滌腥羶；轟奮地之雷霆，震驚聾聵。聖人作而萬物覩，胥有快于乘時；天地革而四時成，孰不忻于改命？遡自乙未之夏，至於癸丑之冬，凡戒諭之諄嚴，及征誅之次第，禮樂制度之沿革，刑威爵賞之重輕，酌古準今，皆精神心術之運用；興衰撥亂，一仁義道德之敷宣。仰觀聖人之大有所爲，固詳陳之不足；比諸天地之一言而盡，亦條列之可該。語功烈之高，迥出百王之上；得國統之正，同符兩漢之興。堯神湯智，而獨禀維全，謨略匪臣工所能贊
translation_en:
…to the northern regions [?]. On campaigns east and west, crowds welcomed you with pitchers of drink and baskets of food. Heaven bestowed its favor, and the people gave their allegiance; those seeking judgment in lawsuits and those singing praises all came to you. Once usurpation and rebellion had been quelled, you laid aside your military dress. What need to speak of the three thousand horses turned out to pasture? Your officials and people petitioned you to ascend the throne, and you took your seat before the embroidered screen, truly answering to the flying dragon in the fifth, yang position of the Changes. You poured down timely rain throughout the realm, washing away the rank and fetid taint; you unleashed thunder that stirred the earth, startling even the deaf and unhearing. The sage arose, and all things beheld him: all rejoiced that you had seized the proper moment. Heaven and earth underwent transformation, and the four seasons attained their order: who did not rejoice in the change of mandate?

Looking back from the summer of yiwei to the winter of guichou, your earnest and stern admonitions, the sequence of your punitive campaigns, the preservation and revision of rites, music, institutions, and regulations, and the relative severity or generosity of punishments, ranks, and rewards—all weighed antiquity against the needs of the present and expressed the workings of your spirit, mind, and judgment. Reviving what had declined and restoring order from chaos were wholly an unfolding of benevolence, righteousness, moral principle, and virtue. Reverently contemplating the sage’s great accomplishments, even a detailed account would surely be inadequate; yet, just as heaven and earth may be encompassed in a single saying, an orderly enumeration can also convey their scope. In the loftiness of your achievements, you far surpass the hundred kings; in the legitimacy of your acquisition of imperial succession, you match the founding of the two Han dynasties. With Yao’s sagacity and Tang’s wisdom, you alone possess their fullness; your plans and strategies are beyond the ability of your officials to assist…

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
助
敬
天勤民而兼極其致精誠與上下相爲感通
家法甚嚴飭
內庭勿干外政兵權有制役大將不啻小兒
