是惟約而可數有此六條所以推而行之
至成一統〔臣等素慚〕〔𧦅質日侍〕
燕閒皐陶見而知之何幸
明良之遇宰我阿非所好豈云智識之汚夫覆
===
大君之烈而會歸簡牘則史職所宜苟失纂修
冒綿區固
曷逃尸素况
創造甫成而致治復盛可容緩于丕揚俟
統臨愈久而積美更多則亦易於再舉爰開
史局精簡儒紳目染耳濡聞見共據其舊
討論潤色編摩各盡其長凡例攸分大書
特書而屢書不已後先以次一日一日而
靡日或遺用漢儒之文字以爲膺第慚未
punctuated:
助。敬天勤民，而兼極其致，精誠與上下相爲感通。家法甚嚴，飭內庭勿干外政；兵權有制，役大將不啻小兒。是惟約而可數，有此六條，所以推而行之，至成一統。
〔臣等素慚〕〔𧦅質日侍〕燕閒，皐陶見而知之，何幸明良之遇！宰我阿非所好，豈云智識之汚？夫覆大君之烈，而會歸簡牘，則史職所宜。苟失纂修，冒綿區固，曷逃尸素？况創造甫成，而致治復盛，可容緩于丕揚？俟統臨愈久，而積美更多，則亦易於再舉。爰開史局，精簡儒紳，目染耳濡，聞見共據其舊；討論潤色，編摩各盡其長。凡例攸分，大書特書，而屢書不已；後先以次，一日一日，而靡日或遺。用漢儒之文字，以爲膺第，慚未
translation_en:
…assist. In revering Heaven and attending diligently to the people, he carried both to their fullest extent; his utter sincerity brought those above and below into sympathetic communion. His household rules were exceedingly strict: he enjoined the inner court not to interfere in external government. Military authority was regulated, and he commanded great generals as readily as little children. These are the six points that can be briefly enumerated; by extending them and putting them into practice, he ultimately achieved unification.
〔We, your servants, have always been ashamed〕〔of our dull capacities [?]; daily we attend〕you in your leisure. Like Gao Yao, we know through direct observation: how fortunate we are to witness the meeting of an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers! Like Zai Wo, we have no fondness for flattery [?]; how could our understanding be called debased? To encompass the great sovereign’s achievements and gather them into written records is the proper duty of the historiographers. If we failed to compile them, while presumptuously occupying our positions [?], how could we escape the charge of drawing salaries without performing our duties? Moreover, the founding has only just been accomplished, yet good government already flourishes anew: how could we delay its magnificent proclamation? When your reign has lasted still longer and more excellent deeds have accumulated, it will also be easy to undertake this work again.
Accordingly, a Historiography Office was established, and learned gentlemen were carefully selected. Drawing on what their eyes and ears had absorbed, they jointly relied on their prior observations and knowledge; in discussion, refinement, compilation, and composition, each exercised his particular strengths. The editorial principles distinguish the categories: matters deserving prominent and special recording are recorded repeatedly without cease. Events are arranged in chronological order, day after day, with not a single day omitted. We employ the literary language of Han scholars, considering it worthy of recognition [?], yet are ashamed that we have not…

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
傅託蒼頡之籀書以爲秉所冀增華仁者
謂之仁智者謂之智孰窺大造之全行帝
道而帝行王道而王曷紀
至神之化臣等計所逾之日則二百有餘舉
同事之臣則一十有四茲覩汗青之就幸
逃頭白之譏雖記事有徵可備後來之採
擇顧立言無法莫追古史之分毫蓋旣乏
乎知幾之所謂長者三而尤困于袁松之
所謂難者五也彙成百卷上進
===
九重
帝德罔愆夫豈自觀之不可
孫謀詒翼國將垂訓於無窮伏願念
創業之惟艱恒存儆惕觀生靈之甫息益切
綏懷多
哲嗣而宜君宜王介
聖壽而時萬時億歲每雨暘時若戶皆弦誦聲
聞麟出鳳遊應
治邁虞廷之瑞梯山航海來
punctuated:
傅。託蒼頡之籀書以爲秉，所冀增華。仁者謂之仁，智者謂之智，孰窺大造之全？行帝道而帝，行王道而王，曷紀至神之化？臣等計所逾之日，則二百有餘；舉同事之臣，則一十有四。茲覩汗青之就，幸逃頭白之譏。雖記事有徵，可備後來之採擇，顧立言無法，莫追古史之分毫。蓋旣乏乎知幾之所謂長者三，而尤困于袁松之所謂難者五也。彙成百卷，上進九重。帝德罔愆，夫豈自觀之不可？孫謀詒翼，國將垂訓於無窮。
伏願念創業之惟艱，恒存儆惕；觀生靈之甫息，益切綏懷。多哲嗣而宜君宜王，介聖壽而時萬時億。歲每雨暘時若，戶皆弦誦聲聞。麟出鳳遊，應治邁虞廷之瑞；梯山航海，來
translation_en:
…transmitted [?]. Drawing upon Cangjie’s seal-script writing as our support [?], we hoped to add lustre. The benevolent call it benevolence, and the wise call it wisdom: who can glimpse the entirety of Your Majesty’s great creative work? Practising the Way of the ancient emperors, you are an emperor; practising the Way of the ancient kings, you are a king. How could we record your supremely wondrous transforming influence?
We, your servants, reckon that more than two hundred days have elapsed, and that fourteen officials have worked together on this undertaking. Now that we see the historical compilation completed, we are fortunate to escape the reproach of having grown white-haired over it. Although the events recorded are supported by evidence and may furnish material for later selection, our writing lacks proper method and cannot approach even a fraction of the achievement of the ancient historians. We lack the three strengths of which Liu Zhiji spoke, and are especially beset by the five difficulties described by Yuan Song. We have assembled the work in one hundred juan and respectfully submit it to the imperial throne. Your imperial virtue is without fault: how could it be improper for you to examine this record yourself? Providing plans and assistance for your descendants, the dynasty will transmit instruction without end.
We humbly pray that you remember the difficulty of founding the enterprise and remain ever vigilant; that, seeing the people have only just gained respite, you take still greater care to bring them peace and comfort. May you have many wise descendants, fit to be lords and kings; may your sacred longevity be blessed with ten thousand years, a hundred million years. May rain and sunshine arrive in season every year, and the sounds of stringed accompaniment and recitation be heard in every household. May qilin appear and phoenixes roam, auspicious responses to a reign surpassing the court of Shun; may those who scale mountains and cross the seas come …

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
王輸絶域之琛〔臣無任瞻〕
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹以所編
大明日曆隨
表上
進以
聞
第叄場
策五道
第一問
王纘宗
===
同考試官教諭張　批
〔聖學心法實具與〕
〔敬一箴相表裏皆千聖傳心之樞要也子能揄揚殆盡其涵濡而有得者耶〕
考試官教諭李　批〔末以誠之一字爲〕
〔今日緝熙之助忠愛之心藹然見矣〕
考試官學正周　批〔敷答明暢宜録以式〕
帝王之治天下有至要之道有不易之□
punctuated:
王，輸絶域之琛。〔臣無任瞻〕天仰聖，激切屏營之至，謹以所編《大明日曆》隨表上進以聞。

第叄場
策五道
第一問
王纘宗

同考試官教諭張，批：〔聖學心法實具，與〕〔敬一箴相表裏，皆千聖傳心之樞要也。子能揄揚殆盡，其涵濡而有得者耶？〕

考試官教諭李，批：〔末以誠之一字爲〕〔今日緝熙之助，忠愛之心藹然見矣。〕

考試官學正周，批：〔敷答明暢，宜録以式。〕

帝王之治天下，有至要之道，有不易之□
translation_en:
…in allegiance, presenting treasures from distant lands. Your servant, gazing toward Heaven and looking up to Your Majesty, is overcome with fervent emotion and profound trepidation. I respectfully submit the compiled Daily Record of the Great Ming (Da Ming rili) together with this memorial for Your Majesty’s consideration.

Third Session
Five Policy Questions
First Question
Wang Zuanzong

Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “The essential teachings of the sages’ learning are fully embodied here [?] and complement the Admonition on Reverent Unity (Jingyi zhen); both are central to the transmission of the mind’s teaching through all the sages. You have expounded them almost exhaustively. Might you have gained this understanding through sustained immersion in them?”

Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “At the close, you offer the single word ‘sincerity’ as an aid to the continued cultivation of luminous virtue today. Your loyal devotion is abundantly apparent.”

Examiner Zhou, Instructor, comments: “The answer is clear and fluent in its exposition. It should be recorded as a model.”

In governing all under Heaven, emperors and kings have a Way of utmost importance and an unchanging [illegible]…

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
所以行之者一也一者何也曰心也道也
者心之用也法也者道之推也道有要焉
執其要可以達之天下而無間法有則焉
善其則可以傳之萬世而不易故曰帝王
之治本於道帝王之道出於心此之謂也
此我
太祖高皇帝
成祖文皇帝曁我
皇上所以紹千聖傳心之秘貽萬世致治之規
===
而蕩蕩難名也與請因執事明問而敬陳
之嘗稽尚書之中古昔已往之治而有以
見聖王相傳之法蓋至微矣唐虞御極道
化翔洽德澤所加浸濡無外聖智協于朝
百姓驩于野庶物和于兩間當此之時咸
池大韶之音感通靈瑞民萌丕丕忘其帝
力蓋極盛矣史臣莫能殫述惟稱贊二后
之德曰欽明文思安安允恭克讓光被四
表格于上下曰重華協于帝濬哲文明溫
punctuated:
所以行之者一也。一者何也？曰心也。道也者，心之用也；法也者，道之推也。道有要焉，執其要，可以達之天下而無間；法有則焉，善其則，可以傳之萬世而不易。故曰：「帝王之治本於道，帝王之道出於心。」此之謂也。此我太祖高皇帝、成祖文皇帝曁我皇上所以紹千聖傳心之秘，貽萬世致治之規，而蕩蕩難名也與？請因執事明問而敬陳之。
嘗稽《尚書》之中古昔已往之治，而有以見聖王相傳之法，蓋至微矣。唐虞御極，道化翔洽，德澤所加，浸濡無外。聖智協于朝，百姓驩于野，庶物和于兩間。當此之時，《咸池》《大韶》之音感通靈瑞，民萌丕丕，忘其帝力，蓋極盛矣。史臣莫能殫述，惟稱贊二后之德曰：「欽明文思安安，允恭克讓，光被四表，格于上下。」曰：「重華協于帝，濬哲文明，溫
translation_en:
…That by which these are put into practice is one. What is this one thing? It is the mind. The Way is the functioning of the mind; governing methods are the extension of the Way. The Way has its essentials: grasp them, and it can reach throughout the realm without obstruction. Governing methods have their standards: perfect them, and they can be transmitted through ten thousand generations without alteration. Thus it is said: “The government of emperors and kings is rooted in the Way; the Way of emperors and kings issues from the mind.” This is what those words mean. Is this not how our Emperor Taizu Gao, Emperor Chengzu Wen, and our reigning emperor have continued the secret of the transmission of the mind through a thousand sages and bequeathed standards for achieving good government to ten thousand generations—so vast that words cannot describe it? Allow me respectfully to set this forth in response to your discerning question.
I have examined the government of bygone antiquity in the Book of Documents (Shangshu), and have thereby discerned the methods transmitted from one sage king to another: they are indeed supremely subtle. When the rulers of Tang and Yu occupied the throne, the transforming influence of the Way spread everywhere, and the beneficence of their virtue reached and permeated all without exception. Sages and wise men worked in harmony at court; the common people rejoiced in the countryside; and all things were in accord between Heaven and Earth. At that time, the music of Xianchi and Dashao called forth numinous auspicious signs. The people flourished in great numbers, oblivious to the emperor’s power: this was surely the height of prosperity. The court historians could not recount it exhaustively, but simply praised the virtues of the two sovereigns, saying: “Reverent and discerning, accomplished and thoughtful, naturally at ease; truly respectful and capable of yielding, his radiance extended to the four quarters and reached above and below.” And: “Chonghua accorded with the emperor; profound in wisdom, accomplished and discerning, mild …

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
恭允塞巳耳此萬世心學之所繇啓也皆
及夏商周之君應運迭興以王天下皆循
二后之訓闡其精奥莫可改易若射者求
的遠近不同而矢道一也由漢唐宋以還
此道或幾乎息矣
皇天眷命肇啓
聖人我
太祖高皇帝繼天立極統攝三五肅祗百禮上
下欽若功烈振于古初德教溢乎四海嘗
===
諭禮部侍郎曾魯曰人君一心治化之本存於
中者無堯舜之心欲施於政者有堯舜之
治决不可得也又嘗謂學士宋濂曰人心
虚靈乘氣機出入操而存之爲難此精一
之學蓋與唐虞相周旋矣
文皇繼承特製
聖學心法一書分别條貫述六籍所稱垂鑒
後世愚嘗莊誦伏讀而竊窺一二矣言乎
君臣也者相須以成務者也言乎父子也
punctuated:
恭允塞」巳耳。此萬世心學之所繇啓也。皆及夏商周之君，應運迭興，以王天下，皆循二后之訓，闡其精奥，莫可改易。若射者求的，遠近不同，而矢道一也。由漢唐宋以還，此道或幾乎息矣。
皇天眷命，肇啓聖人。我太祖高皇帝繼天立極，統攝三五，肅祗百禮，上下欽若，功烈振于古初，德教溢乎四海。嘗諭禮部侍郎曾魯曰：「人君一心，治化之本。存於中者無堯舜之心，欲施於政者有堯舜之治，决不可得也。」又嘗謂學士宋濂曰：「人心虚靈，乘氣機出入，操而存之爲難。」此精一之學，蓋與唐虞相周旋矣。
文皇繼承，特製《聖學心法》一書，分别條貫，述六籍所稱，垂鑒後世。愚嘗莊誦伏讀，而竊窺一二矣。言乎君臣也者，相須以成務者也；言乎父子也
translation_en:
…“reverent and truly sincere”—that is all. This is the source from which the learning of the mind for all ages arose. When the rulers of Xia, Shang, and Zhou in turn arose in response to Heaven’s appointed succession to rule all under Heaven [?], they all followed the teachings of the two sovereigns, elucidating their profound essence, which admitted of no alteration. They were like archers aiming at a target: the distances differed, but the path of the arrow was one. From the Han, Tang, and Song onward, this Way at times almost died out.
August Heaven bestowed its favor and mandate, bringing forth a sage. Our Emperor Taizu Gao succeeded Heaven and established the supreme standard, encompassing the achievements of the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors. Solemnly reverent in all rites, he was respectfully followed by those above and below. His glorious achievements rivaled those of high antiquity, and his moral instruction spread throughout the realm. He once instructed Zeng Lu, Vice Minister of Rites: “The ruler’s single mind is the foundation of governance and moral transformation. If what he harbors within is not the mind of Yao and Shun, yet he wishes to achieve in government the good order of Yao and Shun, it is utterly impossible.” He also once told Academician Song Lian: “The human mind is empty and numinous; it comes and goes with the workings of vital force. To grasp and preserve it is difficult.” This learning of refinement and singleness of mind was surely on a par with that of Tang Yao and Yu Shun.
Emperor Wen succeeded him and specially composed a book, The Mind Method of Sagely Learning (Shengxue xinfa). He distinguished its categories and organizing principles, expounded what the Six Classics taught, and bequeathed a mirror for later generations. I, in my ignorance, have solemnly recited and reverently read it, and have ventured to glimpse one or two of its meanings. Where it speaks of ruler and minister, these are those who depend on one another to accomplish their duties; where it speaks of father and son…

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
者相繼以承序者也或統言者極其大而
無餘也或專言者析其精而不亂也曰學
問曰敬天曰法天曰祀神曰法祖曰謹好
惡曰勤勵曰戒謹曰德化曰正內治曰睦
親曰仁政曰育材曰用人曰納諫曰辨邪
正曰脩禮樂曰正名分曰禮臣下曰明賞
罰曰慎刑曰理財曰節儉曰馭夷狄曰征
伐而君道備矣曰忠曰勤曰廉曰謹而臣
道備矣嗟乎道出於心者也出於心則至
===
要而不繁法出於道者也出於道則一定
而不易是故行之天下者傳之後世者也
傳之後世者行之天下者也合而非離也
一而非二也
聖學之蘊如此其精也
聖治之謨如此其大也而尤有取於帝範之十
二篇者豈不曰貞觀之治雖正心誠意尚
未有聞而飭躬闡政不爲無補耶不然帝
王之道亦多術矣
punctuated:
者，相繼以承序者也。或統言者，極其大而無餘也；或專言者，析其精而不亂也。曰學問，曰敬天，曰法天，曰祀神，曰法祖，曰謹好惡，曰勤勵，曰戒謹，曰德化，曰正內治，曰睦親，曰仁政，曰育材，曰用人，曰納諫，曰辨邪正，曰脩禮樂，曰正名分，曰禮臣下，曰明賞罰，曰慎刑，曰理財，曰節儉，曰馭夷狄，曰征伐，而君道備矣。曰忠，曰勤，曰廉，曰謹，而臣道備矣。嗟乎！道出於心者也，出於心則至要而不繁；法出於道者也，出於道則一定而不易。是故行之天下者，傳之後世者也；傳之後世者，行之天下者也。合而非離也，一而非二也。
聖學之蘊如此其精也，聖治之謨如此其大也，而尤有取於《帝範》之十二篇者，豈不曰貞觀之治，雖正心誠意尚未有聞，而飭躬闡政不爲無補耶？不然，帝王之道亦多術矣。
translation_en:
…are those who succeed one another to carry on the line. Some statements treat matters comprehensively, encompassing their full scope and leaving nothing out; others address particular matters, distinguishing their subtleties without confusion. It speaks of learning, revering Heaven, taking Heaven as a model, sacrificing to the spirits, following ancestral models, exercising care in likes and dislikes, diligent exertion, vigilance and caution, transformation through virtue, rectifying the governance of the inner palace, maintaining harmony among kin, benevolent government, nurturing talent, employing people, accepting remonstrance, distinguishing the deviant from the upright, cultivating rites and music, rectifying titles and distinctions of rank, treating ministers with ritual courtesy, making rewards and punishments clear, exercising caution in punishments, managing finances, practicing frugality, controlling the Yi and Di peoples, and conducting punitive campaigns. Thus the Way of the ruler is fully set forth. It speaks of loyalty, diligence, integrity, and circumspection. Thus the Way of the minister is fully set forth. Alas! The Way issues from the heart; issuing from the heart, it is supremely essential and free of complication. Standards issue from the Way; issuing from the Way, they are firmly fixed and unchanging. Therefore, what is put into practice throughout the realm is what is transmitted to later generations, and what is transmitted to later generations is what is put into practice throughout the realm. These are joined, not separate; they are one, not two.
So refined are the inner principles of sagely learning, and so great are the plans for sagely government! Yet he particularly drew upon the twelve chapters of Models for Emperors (Di fan). Was this not because, although rectifying the heart and making the intentions sincere were not yet known in the government of the Zhenguan era, its disciplined personal conduct and development of government were nevertheless of some benefit? Otherwise, the Way of emperors and kings also offers many methods.

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
聖祖何取焉恭惟
皇上天縱聰明道該太始立皇極以錫庶民覲
會通以行典禮彛倫攸敘百度維貞功化
之盛上下同流誠文明之景會也讀書有
得
製爲敬一之箴傳之天下鐫之學宮又嘗莊誦
伏讀而竊窺一二矣曰匪敬弗聚匪一弗
純則允執厥中也曰弗貳以二勿參以三
則惟精惟一也曰畏天勤民不遑寧處則
===
格于上下也曰行顧其言終如其始則身
脩思永也曰省躬察咎儆戒無虞則無怠
無荒也曰靜虛無欲日新不已則帝德廣
運也曰左右輔弼貴乎忠貞則謨明弼諧
也是故以奉天地以假宗廟廣孝也以正
朝廷以御臣庶光化也釐福耀德澤蒙嗣
亂丕緒也宇內嚮風謳歌四應和德也質
之
聖學心法其何異焉故曰先聖後聖其揆一
punctuated: 聖祖何取焉？恭惟皇上，天縱聰明，道該太始，立皇極以錫庶民，覲會通以行典禮，彛倫攸敘，百度維貞，功化之盛，上下同流，誠文明之景會也。讀書有得，製爲敬一之箴，傳之天下，鐫之學宮。又嘗莊誦伏讀，而竊窺一二矣。曰「匪敬弗聚，匪一弗純」，則允執厥中也；曰「弗貳以二，勿參以三」，則惟精惟一也；曰「畏天勤民，不遑寧處」，則格于上下也；曰「行顧其言，終如其始」，則身脩思永也；曰「省躬察咎，儆戒無虞」，則無怠無荒也；曰「靜虛無欲，日新不已」，則帝德廣運也；曰「左右輔弼，貴乎忠貞」，則謨明弼諧也。是故以奉天地，以假宗廟，廣孝也；以正朝廷，以御臣庶，光化也；釐福耀德，澤蒙嗣亂，丕緒也；宇內嚮風，謳歌四應，和德也。質之聖學心法，其何異焉？故曰：「先聖後聖，其揆一
translation_en:
…what would the sagely progenitor have found worthy in it? Reverently considering Your Majesty: Heaven has endowed you with intelligence, and your Way encompasses the primordial beginning. You establish the imperial standard to bestow it upon the common people, and discern [?] the interconnections of principles in order to carry out the established rites. The enduring human relationships are duly ordered, and all institutions are correct. Your achievements and transforming influence flourish, flowing alike through those above and below. This is truly a splendid age of enlightened culture. Having gained insight through reading, you composed the Admonition on Reverence and Oneness, circulated it throughout the realm, and had it engraved in the schools. I too have solemnly recited and reverently read it, and have ventured to glimpse something of its meaning.

It says, “Without reverence there is no concentration; without oneness there is no purity”: this is sincerely holding fast to the Mean. It says, “Do not divide it in two; do not split it into three”: this is being discerning and single-minded. It says, “Revere Heaven and labor for the people, with no leisure to rest at ease”: this is reaching to what is above and below. It says, “Let conduct accord with words; let the end be as the beginning”: this is cultivating oneself and taking thought for the long term. It says, “Examine yourself and scrutinize your faults; remain vigilant when there is no cause for apprehension”: this is being neither indolent nor negligent. It says, “Be still and empty, free from desire; renew yourself daily without cease”: this is imperial virtue extending far and wide. It says, “Among the counselors assisting on either side, loyalty and steadfastness are prized”: this is enlightened counsel and harmonious assistance.

Thus, through it you serve Heaven and Earth and approach the ancestral temples, extending filial piety; through it you set the court in order and govern officials and common people, making your transforming influence shine. Receiving blessings and manifesting virtue, you extend your beneficence to succeeding rulers, magnifying the dynastic inheritance. All within the realm turn toward your influence, and songs of praise respond from every quarter: this is virtue bringing harmony. When tested against the teachings on the mind transmitted in sagely learning, how does it differ? Hence the saying: “The earlier sages and the later sages—their measure is one…

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
也猗與盛哉斯道也始自堯舜至
皇祖而紹其微述自
成祖至
皇上而顯其化闡聖賢之蘊奧會墳典之精深
盡制盡倫爲天下極所謂配二帝考三王
建天地質鬼神上以承
祖宗鴻圖之傳下以衍子孫燕翼之緒不可以
復加矣而執事猶拳拳下問所以爲
今日緝熈之助愚又何言哉蓋嘗莊誦
===
敬一之序有曰虛心寡欲驅除邪逸信任耆
德爲之匡輔敷求善人布列庶位斯可行
純王之道以坐致太平雍熈之至治也於
是有以仰見
皇上體咸之虛而取人以爲善象乾之健而閑
邪以存誠如此也夫誠者天之道也聖功
之本也故曰至誠無息不息則久久則徵
徵則悠遠悠遠則博厚博厚則高明高明
所以配天也博厚所以配地也悠久所以
punctuated: 也。猗與，盛哉！斯道也，始自堯舜，至皇祖而紹其微；述自成祖，至皇上而顯其化。闡聖賢之蘊奧，會墳典之精深，盡制盡倫，爲天下極。所謂配二帝，考三王，建天地，質鬼神，上以承祖宗鴻圖之傳，下以衍子孫燕翼之緒，不可以復加矣。而執事猶拳拳下問，所以爲今日緝熈之助，愚又何言哉？蓋嘗莊誦《敬一》之序，有曰：「虛心寡欲，驅除邪逸，信任耆德，爲之匡輔，敷求善人，布列庶位，斯可行純王之道，以坐致太平雍熈之至治也。」於是有以仰見皇上體咸之虛而取人以爲善，象乾之健而閑邪以存誠，如此也。夫誠者，天之道也，聖功之本也。故曰：「至誠無息，不息則久，久則徵，徵則悠遠，悠遠則博厚，博厚則高明。高明所以配天也，博厚所以配地也，悠久所以
translation_en:
…are one in their guiding principle. Ah, how magnificent! This Way originated with Yao and Shun, and its subtle essentials were carried forward by the Imperial Ancestor; transmitted from Emperor Chengzu, its transforming influence has been made manifest by His Majesty. He elucidates the profound mysteries of the sages and worthies and brings together the deepest insights of the ancient canons, fully realizing institutions and human relationships and serving as the supreme standard for all under Heaven. This is what is meant by matching the Two Emperors, examining the Three Kings, establishing oneself within Heaven and Earth, and submitting oneself to the scrutiny of spirits. Above, he inherits the grand imperial undertaking handed down by his ancestors; below, he extends the legacy that provides security for his descendants. Nothing further could be added. Yet you, honored examiners, still earnestly seek instruction from those below, thereby assisting the continued illumination of virtue today. What more can I, in my ignorance, say?

I have reverently read the preface to Reverence for the One (Jingyi), which says: “Empty the mind and diminish desires; drive out depravity and indolence; trust elders of virtue to provide correction and assistance; seek good men widely and array them in the various offices. Then one may practice the pure Way of the true king and effortlessly bring about the consummate governance of great peace, harmony, and prosperity.” From this we may reverently perceive how His Majesty embodies the receptivity of the hexagram Influence (Xian), drawing upon others to achieve goodness, and emulates the vigor of the hexagram The Creative (Qian), warding off depravity to preserve sincerity. Such is his practice. Sincerity is the Way of Heaven and the foundation of sagely achievement. Thus it is said: “Perfect sincerity never ceases. Never ceasing, it endures; enduring, it becomes manifest; becoming manifest, it extends far into the distance; extending far into the distance, it becomes broad and deep; becoming broad and deep, it becomes lofty and luminous. Through loftiness and luminosity it matches Heaven; through breadth and depth it matches Earth; through its enduring constancy it…”

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
無疆也愚敢以是爲
今日頌
第二問
陳宗虞
同考試官教諭艾　批〔聖賢之學本乎一理此作折衷諸儒之論而以定性約之可以破千古之疑矣豈但冠多士而已乎〕
考試官教諭李　批〔理學精明蓋究心於愽約者〕
考試官學正周　批〔深得諸儒奧旨錄之〕
天下之道散之而不窮合之而無間散之
===
而有窮合之而有間則不可以爲道夫道
也者散一於萬故辨異者其分也命之所
以流行而不已也合萬於一故會同者其
歸也理之所以貞一而不易也自古聖賢
之心學前乎旣往後乎方來所以諄諄然
言之不能已者道之不可窮也然其致則
一而已矣一者無間之謂也無間者其歸
宿也不窮者其散殊也觀此則宋儒之學
亦求以致此而已何必同自此學不講而
punctuated:
無疆也。愚敢以是爲今日頌。

第二問
陳宗虞
同考試官教諭艾，批〔聖賢之學本乎一理，此作折衷諸儒之論，而以定性約之，可以破千古之疑矣，豈但冠多士而已乎！〕
考試官教諭李，批〔理學精明，蓋究心於愽約者。〕
考試官學正周，批〔深得諸儒奧旨，錄之。〕

天下之道，散之而不窮，合之而無間。散之而有窮，合之而有間，則不可以爲道。夫道也者，散一於萬，故辨異者其分也，命之所以流行而不已也；合萬於一，故會同者其歸也，理之所以貞一而不易也。自古聖賢之心學，前乎旣往，後乎方來，所以諄諄然言之不能已者，道之不可窮也。然其致則一而已矣。一者，無間之謂也。無間者，其歸宿也；不窮者，其散殊也。觀此，則宋儒之學亦求以致此而已，何必同？自此學不講而
translation_en:
…is therefore without bounds. I venture to offer this as a tribute to the present reign.

Second Question
Chen Zongyu

Associate Examiner Ai, Instructor, comments: “The learning of the sages and worthies is rooted in a single principle. This essay weighs and reconciles the arguments of the various Confucian scholars, drawing them together through the settling of one’s nature. It can dispel doubts of a thousand ages. How could it merely rank first among the many candidates!”

Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “His understanding of the learning of principle is penetrating and clear. He has evidently devoted himself to breadth of learning and its reduction to essentials.”

Examiner Zhou, School Director, comments: “He has deeply grasped the profound meaning of the various Confucian scholars. Select this for inclusion.”

The Way throughout the world, dispersed, is inexhaustible; gathered together, it is without gaps. If, dispersed, it could be exhausted, or, gathered together, it had gaps, it could not be the Way. The Way disperses the one into the myriad; thus differentiation into distinct things is its division, through which Heaven’s mandate flows without ceasing. It gathers the myriad into the one; thus convergence in unity is its destination, through which principle remains constant, unified, and unchanging. From antiquity, the learning of the mind transmitted by sages and worthies extends backward into the past and forward into what is yet to come. They speak of it earnestly and cannot cease because the Way is inexhaustible. Yet its ultimate purport is simply one. “One” means being without gaps. Being without gaps is its ultimate destination; being inexhaustible is its dispersion into diverse things. Viewed in this light, the learning of the Song Confucians likewise sought only to attain this. Why must they be identical? Since this learning ceased to be expounded, …

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
天下之人始惟異端之趨而莫之或止而
不知聖賢極致之道本如是而已執事發
策以希聖之學覺諸生意甚厚也愚雖不
敏敢不摭拾以對夫道不可尚矣自堯舜
始焉至禹湯文武而極其盛自孔孟繼焉
至周程朱張而析其微間嘗泛觀諸子之
言而求其所以不一之故矣夫易有太極
也在天而言謂之道道生天地者也在人
而言謂之心心統性情者也邵子之言與
===
趙致遠一也夫極建於心則道由此出矣
道始太一也震以肇其端者也一之所由
始也乾以探其本者也一之所由終也邵
子之言與富彥國一也夫一起於乾則震
由此基矣心之虛實本無體也程子之意
特患夫成心之未忘耳志則有主有主則
天理自裕於中而實矣實者我不出也人
欲自絕於外而虛矣虛者物不入也其又
何異焉心之出入本無時也朱子之意特
punctuated:
天下之人始惟異端之趨，而莫之或止，而不知聖賢極致之道本如是而已。執事發策，以希聖之學覺諸生，意甚厚也。愚雖不敏，敢不摭拾以對？
夫道不可尚矣，自堯舜始焉，至禹湯文武而極其盛；自孔孟繼焉，至周程朱張而析其微。間嘗泛觀諸子之言，而求其所以不一之故矣。夫《易》有太極也，在天而言謂之道，道生天地者也；在人而言謂之心，心統性情者也。邵子之言與趙致遠一也。夫極建於心，則道由此出矣。道始太一也，震以肇其端者也，一之所由始也；乾以探其本者也，一之所由終也。邵子之言與富彥國一也。夫一起於乾，則震由此基矣。心之虛實，本無體也。程子之意，特患夫成心之未忘耳。志則有主，有主則天理自裕於中而實矣。實者，我不出也；人欲自絕於外而虛矣。虛者，物不入也。其又何異焉？心之出入，本無時也。朱子之意，特
translation_en:
…the people of the world began to pursue only heterodox teachings, with no one to restrain them, unaware that the Way in its highest realization among the sages and worthies was simply thus. You, honored examiners, have issued a policy question to awaken the students to the learning through which one aspires to sagehood; your intention is most generous. Though I am slow of understanding, how could I dare not gather what I can in reply?
The Way cannot be surpassed. It began with Yao and Shun and reached its fullest flourishing with Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu. Confucius and Mencius carried it forward, and Zhou, Cheng, Zhu, and Zhang analyzed its subtleties. I have at times surveyed the statements of these various masters, seeking the reason for their apparent lack of agreement. The Book of Changes speaks of the Supreme Ultimate. Spoken of in relation to Heaven, it is called the Way: the Way generates Heaven and Earth. Spoken of in relation to human beings, it is called the mind: the mind governs human nature and the emotions. Master Shao's words agree with those of Zhao Zhiyuan. When the Ultimate is established in the mind, the Way proceeds from it. The Way begins in the Great One. Zhen, the Arousing, initiates its unfolding and is where unity begins; Qian, the Creative, fathoms its root and is where unity reaches its completion. Master Shao's words agree with those of Fu Yanguo. Since unity arises in Qian, Zhen takes its foundation from this.
The mind's emptiness and fullness fundamentally have no fixed form. Master Cheng's concern was simply that preconceived notions had not yet been forgotten. With resolve, there is a governing focus; with such a focus, heavenly principle naturally abounds within, and the mind is full. Fullness means that the self does not go out. Human desires naturally cease at the exterior, and the mind is empty. Emptiness means that external things do not enter. What difference, then, is there between these accounts? The mind's going out and coming in fundamentally have no fixed times. Master Zhu's intention was simply …

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
患夫放心之未求耳求則有本有本則在
外而收之入者道心之所由生也在內而
推之出者人心之所由遏也其又何異焉
仁也者人也朱子以爲愛之理矣而尹焞
又以爲公者蓋以公爲心則好惡得其正
所以成其愛也義也者宜也張子以爲仁
之用矣而朱子又以爲質者蓋以義爲質
則裁制有其節所以成其仁也動靜不可
離也周子之動程子之靜一也通書曰靜
===
而無靜動而無動此之謂也使能察識於
未發之前而求所謂中則得之矣或曰動
靜如船之在水非耶知行不可二也尹焞
之行朱子之知一也易曰知至至之知終
終之此之謂也使能踐履於既發之後而
求所謂和則可驗矣或曰知行如車之有
輪非耶人心之虛靈即性也程子以感應
爲定性之常而勉齋又以爲當作心看者
似不一也而不知廓然大公物來順應是
punctuated: 患夫放心之未求耳。求則有本，有本則在外而收之入者，道心之所由生也；在內而推之出者，人心之所由遏也。其又何異焉？仁也者，人也。朱子以爲愛之理矣，而尹焞又以爲公者，蓋以公爲心，則好惡得其正，所以成其愛也。義也者，宜也。張子以爲仁之用矣，而朱子又以爲質者，蓋以義爲質，則裁制有其節，所以成其仁也。動靜不可離也，周子之動、程子之靜，一也。《通書》曰：「靜而無靜，動而無動。」此之謂也。使能察識於未發之前，而求所謂中，則得之矣。或曰：「動靜如船之在水，非耶？」知行不可二也，尹焞之行、朱子之知，一也。《易》曰：「知至至之，知終終之。」此之謂也。使能踐履於既發之後，而求所謂和，則可驗矣。或曰：「知行如車之有輪，非耶？」人心之虛靈，即性也。程子以感應爲定性之常，而勉齋又以爲當作心看者，似不一也。而不知廓然大公，物來順應，是
translation_en: …was concerned only that the strayed mind had not yet been recovered. Seeking it provides a foundation. With this foundation, gathering inward what has strayed outside is how the moral mind arises; pushing outward what is within is how the human mind is restrained. What difference, then, is there between them? Benevolence means being human. Master Zhu regarded it as the principle of love, while Yin Tun regarded it as impartiality. This is because, when impartiality governs the mind, likes and dislikes attain their proper balance, thereby bringing love to fulfillment. Righteousness means appropriateness. Master Zhang regarded it as the functioning of benevolence, while Master Zhu regarded it as one's essential substance. This is because, when righteousness constitutes one's essential substance, judgments and decisions have their proper measure, thereby bringing benevolence to fulfillment. Activity and stillness cannot be separated: Master Zhou's activity and Master Cheng's stillness are one. The Book of Penetration (Tongshu) says: “Still, yet without stillness; active, yet without activity.” This is what it means. If one can discern and recognize before the feelings are aroused, and seek what is called equilibrium, one will attain it. Someone says: “Activity and stillness are like a boat resting on water—is this not so?” Knowledge and action cannot be treated as two: Yin Tun's action and Master Zhu's knowledge are one. The Book of Changes says: “Know where to arrive, and arrive there; know where to end, and end there.” This is what it means. If one can put this into practice after the feelings have been aroused, and seek what is called harmony, one can verify it in experience. Someone says: “Knowledge and action are like a carriage having wheels—is this not so?” The emptiness and numinous awareness of the human mind are precisely its nature. Master Cheng regarded responding to things as the constant operation of a stabilized nature, while Mianzhai held that this should be understood in terms of the mind. These views seem to differ. Yet this overlooks being utterly open and impartial, responding appropriately as things arrive—this …

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
孰爲之耶故曰心者性之郛郭非心之外
而又有所謂性也太和之保合卽性也張
子以形爲氣質之性而程子又以爲二則
不是者非有他也蓋以論性不論氣不備
論氣不論性不明而極言之耳故曰形色
天性也非形色之外而別求所謂性也嗟
乎天高地下萬物散殊其分也萬變而不
可知也流而不息合同而化其理也一本
而不可易也此君子之學所以推之而不
===
窮合之而無間也南軒之學學乎此者也
擴仁義之端彌漫乎六合謹義利之辨剖
析於秋毫至論聖門親切之旨則獨觀其
深矣鶴山之學亦學乎此者也卽物以明
義而究觀乎會通反身以求仁而省察乎
虛滿至論聖門講學之樞要則匪夷所思
也愚聞於師友稽於冊籍敢因明問而上
陳其略如此其究不可得而聞也而執事
尤欲於數言之中而求所謂第一義焉愚
punctuated: 孰爲之耶？故曰：「心者，性之郛郭。」非心之外而又有所謂性也。太和之保合，卽性也。張子以形爲氣質之性，而程子又以爲二則不是者，非有他也，蓋以「論性不論氣，不備；論氣不論性，不明」而極言之耳。故曰：「形色，天性也。」非形色之外而別求所謂性也。嗟乎！天高地下，萬物散殊，其分也，萬變而不可知也；流而不息，合同而化，其理也，一本而不可易也。此君子之學所以推之而不窮，合之而無間也。南軒之學，學乎此者也。擴仁義之端，彌漫乎六合；謹義利之辨，剖析於秋毫。至論聖門親切之旨，則獨觀其深矣。鶴山之學，亦學乎此者也。卽物以明義，而究觀乎會通；反身以求仁，而省察乎虛滿。至論聖門講學之樞要，則匪夷所思也。愚聞於師友，稽於冊籍，敢因明問而上陳其略如此。其究不可得而聞也，而執事尤欲於數言之中而求所謂第一義焉。愚
translation_en:
…who brings this about? Hence it is said: “The mind is the outer wall of human nature.” There is no separate entity called human nature outside the mind. The preservation and union of Supreme Harmony is precisely this nature. Master Zhang regarded bodily form as belonging to the nature constituted by material endowment, whereas Master Cheng said that treating them as two was incorrect. There is no other reason for this: they were simply expressing to the fullest the point that “to discuss nature without discussing material force is incomplete; to discuss material force without discussing nature is unclear.” Hence it is said: “Bodily form and appearance are Heaven-endowed nature.” One should not seek a separate entity called nature outside bodily form and appearance.

Ah! Heaven is high and earth is low; the myriad things are dispersed and distinct. Such is their differentiation, with innumerable transformations that cannot all be known. Flowing without cease, joining together and transforming: such is their principle, rooted in a single source that cannot be altered. This is why the learning of the gentleman can be extended without exhaustion and brought together without a gap. Nanxuan’s learning was directed toward this. He expanded the beginnings of benevolence and righteousness until they filled the six directions, and attended scrupulously to the distinction between righteousness and profit, analyzing it down to the finest hair. When discussing the immediately pertinent purport of the sages’ teaching, he had a singular insight into its depths.

Heshan’s learning was likewise directed toward this. He approached things to clarify righteousness and thoroughly examined their interconnections; he turned back upon himself to seek benevolence and scrutinized whether he was empty or full [?]. When discussing the essential pivot of the exposition of learning in the sages’ tradition, his insights surpassed ordinary understanding.

What I have heard from teachers and friends, I have checked against the written records. In response to your discerning question, I venture respectfully to present this outline. Its ultimate depths are beyond what I have been able to learn; yet you, honored sir, particularly wish to seek within a few words what is called the foremost principle. I…

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
何足以知之嘗聞之孟子曰盡其心者知
其性也知其性則知天矣甚矣知性之難
也故子貢曰性與天道不可得而聞也今
夫人莫不知善之可好而不能如好好色
循不好也莫不知不善之可惡而不能如
惡惡臭循不惡也非天下之眞知故也吾
性之良虛靈全具而乃自欺如此乎此君
子所以必愼其獨而去耳目支離之用全
虛圓不測之神有以也故曰知止而後有
===
定止也者性之謂也知止則知性矣知性
則定矣定則極由我立一由我起無虛實
無出入無動靜無知行而仁義理氣一以
貫之而無餘也易曰乾道變化各正性命
而天地定矣寂然不動感而遂通天下之
故而聖人定矣艮其背不獲其身行其庭
不見其人而君子定矣此愚反覆定性一
書印證於易而未敢以爲然也願因執事
而就正焉惟進而敎之幸甚
punctuated:
何足以知之？嘗聞之，孟子曰：「盡其心者，知其性也；知其性，則知天矣。」甚矣，知性之難也！故子貢曰：「性與天道，不可得而聞也。」今夫人莫不知善之可好，而不能如好好色，循不好也；莫不知不善之可惡，而不能如惡惡臭，循不惡也。非天下之眞知故也。吾性之良，虛靈全具，而乃自欺如此乎？此君子所以必愼其獨，而去耳目支離之用，全虛圓不測之神，有以也。故曰：「知止而後有定。」止也者，性之謂也。知止則知性矣，知性則定矣。定則極由我立，一由我起，無虛實，無出入，無動靜，無知行，而仁義理氣，一以貫之而無餘也。
《易》曰：「乾道變化，各正性命」，而天地定矣；「寂然不動，感而遂通天下之故」，而聖人定矣；「艮其背，不獲其身；行其庭，不見其人」，而君子定矣。此愚反覆《定性》一書，印證於《易》，而未敢以爲然也。願因執事而就正焉，惟進而敎之，幸甚。
translation_en:
… how could I be qualified to understand it? I have heard Mencius say: “One who fully realizes his heart knows his nature; knowing his nature, he knows Heaven.” How very difficult it is to know one's nature! Thus Zigong said: “His teachings on human nature and the Way of Heaven cannot be heard.” Now everyone knows that goodness deserves to be loved, yet cannot love it as one loves beautiful appearances, and goes on failing to love it [?]. Everyone knows that what is not good deserves to be hated, yet cannot hate it as one hates a foul smell, and goes on failing to hate it [?]. This is because theirs is not true knowledge. The goodness of our nature is empty and numinously aware, complete in every respect: can we nevertheless deceive ourselves in this way? There is good reason why the gentleman must be watchful over himself when alone, putting aside the fragmented workings of ears and eyes and preserving whole the empty, all-encompassing, unfathomable spirit. Thus it is said: “Only after knowing where to rest can one become settled.” This resting place means one's nature. Knowing where to rest, one knows one's nature; knowing one's nature, one becomes settled. Once settled, the ultimate standard is established by oneself, and unity arises from oneself. There is no distinction between emptiness and fullness, going out and coming in, movement and stillness, or knowing and acting. Benevolence and righteousness, principle and material force are all threaded together by a single unity, with nothing left out.
The Book of Changes says: “The Way of Qian transforms and changes; each thing attains its proper nature and allotted destiny”—and Heaven and Earth are thereby settled. “Quiescent and unmoving, it responds to stimulation and thereby penetrates the affairs of all under Heaven”—and the sage is thereby settled. “Keeping his back still, he does not apprehend his body; walking in his courtyard, he does not see his people”—and the gentleman is thereby settled. These are the conclusions I have reached by repeatedly studying the Letter on Settling the Nature (Dingxing) and checking it against the Book of Changes, yet I dare not presume that they are correct. I hope to obtain correction through you, honored sir. If you would receive me and instruct me, I would be most fortunate.

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
第三問
李詩
同考試官教諭吳　批〔兵民之憂一體而非二也此篇斟酌古制切中時宜真鑿鑿可行於今日者子其長於經濟矣乎〕
考試官教諭李　批〔救時挽古有用之才可錄可錄〕
考試官學正周　批〔得問者不盡之意可嘉〕
君子之欲有爲於天下必先有以殖其本
而後可以言治不殖其本而言治皆苟道
也故觀國之强弱者不觀之國觀之人而
===
已觀人之向背者不觀之人觀之心而已
人心也者其保國之本乎自古未有不得
其心而能得其人者亦未有不得其人而
能保其國也爲人上者其可不思所以培
殖之哉愚不通於天下之事然亦聞兵民
之爲本矣請因明問而敬陳之天下之生
久矣兵民之弊甚矣昔有周盛時以大司
徒制民以大司馬制軍平居則籍於司徒
征行則屬之司馬故士不待遷卽吾民也
punctuated:
第三問
李詩
同考試官教諭吳批〔兵民之憂一體而非二也。此篇斟酌古制，切中時宜，真鑿鑿可行於今日者。子其長於經濟矣乎！〕
考試官教諭李批〔救時挽古，有用之才，可錄可錄！〕
考試官學正周批〔得問者不盡之意，可嘉。〕
君子之欲有爲於天下，必先有以殖其本，而後可以言治。不殖其本而言治，皆苟道也。故觀國之强弱者，不觀之國，觀之人而已；觀人之向背者，不觀之人，觀之心而已。人心也者，其保國之本乎！自古未有不得其心而能得其人者，亦未有不得其人而能保其國也。爲人上者，其可不思所以培殖之哉！愚不通於天下之事，然亦聞兵民之爲本矣。請因明問而敬陳之。天下之生久矣，兵民之弊甚矣。昔有周盛時，以大司徒制民，以大司馬制軍。平居則籍於司徒，征行則屬之司馬。故士不待遷，卽吾民也。
translation_en:
Third Policy Question
Li Shi

Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: 〔The concerns of soldiers and civilians are one, not two. This essay weighs ancient institutions and precisely meets the needs of the times; its proposals are truly concrete and practicable today. You must be accomplished in statecraft!〕
Comment by Examiner Li, Instructor: 〔A useful talent for remedying the troubles of the times and restoring ancient ways. Worth selecting, worth selecting!〕
Comment by Examiner Zhou, School Director: 〔He grasps the intentions that the questioner did not fully express. Commendable.〕

A gentleman who wishes to accomplish something in the world must first find a way to nurture its foundations; only then can he speak of governing. To speak of governing without nurturing its foundations is merely an expedient course. Thus, to judge a state's strength or weakness, one looks not at the state but at its people; to judge whether the people give or withdraw their allegiance, one looks not at the people but at their hearts. Are not the people's hearts the foundation for preserving the state? From antiquity, no one has ever secured the people without winning their hearts, nor preserved his state without securing its people. How can those who rule over others fail to consider how to cultivate this foundation?

I am unversed in the affairs of the world, yet I too have heard that soldiers and civilians constitute the foundation. Allow me respectfully to set forth my views in response to your illuminating question. Life in the world has endured long, and the afflictions of soldiers and civilians have become severe. In the flourishing days of the Zhou, the Minister of Education administered the people, and the Minister of War administered the army. In ordinary times, people were registered under the Minister of Education; when campaigning, they came under the Minister of War. Thus soldiers did not have to be transferred: they were our own people …

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
將不改置印吾吏也今考其井田溝洫之
法比閭族黨之制伍兩卒旅之規追胥車
馬之數歲時交會之禮養生除害之術凡
所以利安其人而培殖其本者無不至也
周之衰也齊辨四民之業連五家之兵卒
伍整于里軍旅整于郊相地而征山林川
澤各致其時陵阜陸墐各均其宜邑鄉縣
屬各立其正凡所以利安其人而尤知不
失其本也漢唐之間有可言者至于有宋
===
則可慨矣乾道之初蜀人孔棘邊釁起於
貪殘兵籍冒于奸究隱户磬於檢括逋輸
急於期會調度困於誅求經費消於冗濫
吏考當時汪應辰上邊事有三曰舉守臣
曰調土兵曰督軍儲王溚上急務有五曰
嚴戒貪吏之侵漁以杜邊釁曰大攷守兵
之尺籍以責實用曰明絶郡縣之誅求以
開民生曰痛省官吏之冗員以去浮食曰
盡蠲積年之虛額以寬期會皆求所以殖
punctuated:
將不改置，印吾吏也。今考其井田溝洫之法、比閭族黨之制、伍兩卒旅之規、追胥車馬之數、歲時交會之禮、養生除害之術，凡所以利安其人而培殖其本者，無不至也。周之衰也，齊辨四民之業，連五家之兵，卒伍整于里，軍旅整于郊，相地而征，山林川澤各致其時，陵阜陸墐各均其宜，邑鄉縣屬各立其正，凡所以利安其人，而尤知不失其本也。漢唐之間有可言者，至于有宋，則可慨矣。
乾道之初，蜀人孔棘，邊釁起於貪殘，兵籍冒于奸究，隱户磬於檢括，逋輸急於期會，調度困於誅求，經費消於冗濫。吏考當時，汪應辰上邊事有三：曰舉守臣，曰調土兵，曰督軍儲。王溚上急務有五：曰嚴戒貪吏之侵漁以杜邊釁，曰大攷守兵之尺籍以責實用，曰明絶郡縣之誅求以開民生，曰痛省官吏之冗員以去浮食，曰盡蠲積年之虛額以寬期會，皆求所以殖
translation_en:
…Nor did commanders have to be newly appointed: they were our own officials [?]. Now, examining their methods of well-field allocation and irrigation channels; their organization of households into bi, lü, zu, and dang; their military organization into squads, platoons, companies, and battalions; their prescribed numbers of chariots and horses for pursuit and patrol; their rites for seasonal gatherings; and their means of sustaining life and eliminating harm, we find that nothing was left undone to benefit and secure their people and nurture their foundation. When the Zhou declined, Qi distinguished the occupations of the four groups of people and linked the troops supplied by every five households. Squads and companies were organized within the residential wards, and larger military formations in the outskirts. Taxes were assessed according to the land: mountains, forests, rivers, and marshes each supplied their products in season; hills, uplands, and other terrain [?] each bore an appropriate share; and settlements, townships, counties, and larger jurisdictions each had their appointed head. All these arrangements benefited and secured the people, showing particular awareness of the need to preserve the foundation. There were achievements worth recounting under the Han and Tang; by the Song, however, the situation was lamentable.
At the beginning of the Qiandao era, the people of Shu were in dire distress. Frontier conflicts arose from greed and cruelty; military registers were falsified through fraud [?]; unregistered households were utterly depleted by searches and registration; those owing tax arrears were pressed by collection deadlines; the provision of supplies was hampered by extortionate demands; and public funds were consumed by excessive and indiscriminate expenditure. Examining that time [?], Wang Yingchen submitted three proposals concerning frontier affairs: to recommend prefectural administrators, to mobilize local troops, and to oversee military provisions. Wang Da [?] submitted five proposals on urgent affairs: strictly prohibit rapacious officials from exploiting the people, to prevent frontier conflicts; thoroughly investigate the garrison troop registers, to ensure effective service; explicitly end extortionate demands by prefectures and counties, to enable the people to earn their livelihood; drastically reduce superfluous official posts, to eliminate those maintained at public expense without useful service; and remit in full the fictitious assessments accumulated over the years, to ease the pressure of collection deadlines. All sought means to nurture…

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
其本也然其所見者可得而言也其所不
見者不可得而言也則其所遺者宜亦多
矣古之人若李冰文翁孔明李德裕張詠
韓琦趙抃崔與之數人者其所以治蜀何
如也其文其武其寛其猛其張其弛今皆
可得而知也或開導沬江以繼神禹或振
興庠序以希鄒魯或開誠布公以跨荆益
或募兵治賦以城維州或歸屯軍撤守備
而寇不犯或撤劍門平彭益而民以安或
===
清儉帥蜀風俗大變而琴鶴可詠或拊循
將士人心咸悅而仙遊可祠然今皆不可
作矣吾將誰與歸哉夫今日之民猶前日
之民也而其財則盡矣葢賦稅有程而征
科無藝世業有限而横權不已力役已妨
乎樹蓺追呼尤及於鷄豚加之官府賓旅
之擾輿馬徒隷之供皆民實爲之而上莫
之省憂也幾何其不轉而徙也今獨不可
反其政乎或曰正其節目寛其科條停不
punctuated:
其本也。然其所見者，可得而言也；其所不見者，不可得而言也，則其所遺者宜亦多矣。古之人，若李冰、文翁、孔明、李德裕、張詠、韓琦、趙抃、崔與之數人者，其所以治蜀何如也？其文其武，其寛其猛，其張其弛，今皆可得而知也。或開導沬江以繼神禹，或振興庠序以希鄒魯，或開誠布公以跨荆益，或募兵治賦以城維州，或歸屯軍、撤守備而寇不犯，或撤劍門、平彭益而民以安，或清儉帥蜀、風俗大變而琴鶴可詠，或拊循將士、人心咸悅而仙遊可祠。然今皆不可作矣，吾將誰與歸哉？
夫今日之民，猶前日之民也，而其財則盡矣。葢賦稅有程，而征科無藝；世業有限，而横權不已。力役已妨乎樹蓺，追呼尤及於鷄豚。加之官府賓旅之擾、輿馬徒隷之供，皆民實爲之，而上莫之省憂也，幾何其不轉而徙也？今獨不可反其政乎？或曰：「正其節目，寛其科條，停不
translation_en:
…their foundations. Yet what they saw could be spoken of; what they did not see could not be spoken of. Thus, surely, much must also have escaped their attention. How did men of former times such as Li Bing, Wen Weng, Kongming, Li Deyu, Zhang Yong, Han Qi, Zhao Bian, and Cui Yuzhi govern Shu? Their civil and military measures, their leniency and severity, their tightening and relaxation of control—all these can still be known today. One opened and channelled the Mei River, carrying on the work of the divine Yu; another revived the schools, aspiring to the example of Zou and Lu; another dealt openly and impartially with others, extending his authority across Jing and Yi; another recruited troops and managed tax revenues to fortify Weizhou. One sent garrison troops home and withdrew defensive forces, yet raiders did not invade; another dismantled the defenses at Jianmen and pacified Peng and Yi, bringing peace to the people. One governed Shu with integrity and frugality, transforming its customs so greatly that his zither and crane became worthy subjects of verse; another cared for his officers and soldiers, winning everyone’s affection, so that he could be honored at the Xianyou shrine. Yet none of these men can now be brought back. Whom, then, shall I follow?
The people of today are still the people of former days, but their wealth is exhausted. For taxes have prescribed rates, yet additional levies know no bounds; hereditary holdings are limited, yet arbitrary exactions [?] never cease. Corvée labor already interferes with planting and cultivation, while the pursuit of payment reaches even their chickens and pigs. Added to this are the disturbances caused by government offices and visiting travelers, and the provision of carriages, horses, attendants, and runners. All these are in fact supplied by the people, yet those above neither consider nor concern themselves with their plight. How long can it be before they wander away and migrate? Could the present administration not reverse its policies? Someone says: “Set its procedures in order, relax its regulations, and suspend those …

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
急之役省無名之征而又擇守令以滋戶
口勸農桑以殖貨財誅黨比以銷姦萌明
禮制以定風俗旌廉惠以别淑慝懲貪讌
以明賞罰則庶幾有可為者此則又在司
民命者重加之意耳不然則本實先撥其
何以行之哉今日之兵猶前日之兵也而
其力則盡矣蓋尺籍有稽而朘削不已也
田有業而占奪無時加之强力役於私門
老羸充乎行伍凡戈盾弓鞬之備餱糧營
===
壘之具皆兵自為之而上不之省恤也幾
何其不削而弱也今獨不可反其政乎或
曰督之以仁義厲之以勇力嚴其斃放之
罰厚其犒賞之資而又柬將佐以立軍政
比什伍以結衆情考尺籍以禁月錢明屯
堡以銷歲例時簡教以核名實寬力役以
養精銳則庶幾有可為者此特在司兵柄
者重加之意耳不然則其本亂而末治者
否矣昔君子之於天下求必無一人不得
punctuated: 急之役，省無名之征，而又擇守令以滋戶口，勸農桑以殖貨財，誅黨比以銷姦萌，明禮制以定風俗，旌廉惠以别淑慝，懲貪讌以明賞罰，則庶幾有可為者。」此則又在司民命者重加之意耳。不然，則本實先撥，其何以行之哉？今日之兵，猶前日之兵也，而其力則盡矣。蓋尺籍有稽，而朘削不已也；田有業，而占奪無時。加之强力役於私門，老羸充乎行伍，凡戈盾弓鞬之備、餱糧營壘之具，皆兵自為之，而上不之省恤也。幾何其不削而弱也？今獨不可反其政乎？或曰：「督之以仁義，厲之以勇力，嚴其斃放之罰，厚其犒賞之資，而又柬將佐以立軍政，比什伍以結衆情，考尺籍以禁月錢，明屯堡以銷歲例，時簡教以核名實，寬力役以養精銳，則庶幾有可為者。」此特在司兵柄者重加之意耳。不然，則其本亂而末治者，否矣。昔君子之於天下，求必無一人不得
translation_en:
…urgent labor services, eliminate levies imposed without justification, and further select prefects and county magistrates to increase the number of households and inhabitants; encourage farming and sericulture to increase goods and wealth; punish factional collusion to eradicate the beginnings of wrongdoing; clarify ritual institutions to stabilize customs; honor integrity and benevolence to distinguish the good from the wicked; and punish greed and feasting [?] to make rewards and penalties clear. Then perhaps something could be accomplished.” This, in turn, depends upon those responsible for the people’s lives giving the matter serious attention. Otherwise, if the roots have already been undermined, how could these measures be carried out?

Today’s soldiers are still the soldiers of former days, but their strength is exhausted. Although military registers are available for checking, the exactions upon them never cease; although they hold land, its encroachment and seizure occur at any time. Moreover, the strong are put to work in private households, while the old and weak fill the ranks. Soldiers themselves must provide all their equipment—spears, shields, bows, and bow cases—as well as provisions and the materials for camps and fortifications, yet their superiors neither investigate nor show concern. How could they avoid becoming depleted and weak? Can these policies not now be reversed? Some say: “Direct them through benevolence and righteousness, spur them through courage and strength, strictly enforce the penalties of execution and dismissal [?], and provide generously for gifts and rewards. Further, select commanders and their assistants to establish military discipline; organize the men into units of ten and five to bind their loyalties together; examine military registers to prohibit ‘monthly payments’ [?]; clarify the administration of military settlements and forts to eliminate customary annual exactions [?]; conduct inspections and training at proper times to verify that actual conditions match the rolls; and lighten labor services to nurture picked troops. Then perhaps something could be accomplished.” This depends only upon those wielding military authority giving the matter serious attention. Otherwise, for the root to be disordered while the branches are well governed is impossible.

In former times, gentlemen, in their dealings with the world, sought to ensure that not a single person failed to obtain…

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
其分而不相越汲汲然若不能一日安者
凡以此耳夫子思大道爲公之世而不之
逮也冉有季路以政事名者季路曰千乘
之國攝乎大國之間加之以師旅因之以
饑饉由也爲之可使有勇且知方也冉有
曰方六七十如五六十求也爲之可使足
民如其禮樂以俟君子則庶幾乎所謂知
本者矣故夫子許之而不以爲大也然則
夫子之大也如之何曰子貢曰立之斯立
===
道之斯行綏之斯來動之斯和此夫子之
所以不可及如天之不可階而升也謹對
第四問
任有齡
同考試官教諭王　批〔我〕
朝立法之初意本如此子能言之佳士也
考試官教諭李　批〔是知時務者〕
考試官學正周　批〔有議論〕
天下未有不可行之法其所以不能行者
punctuated:
其分，而不相越，汲汲然若不能一日安者，凡以此耳。夫子思大道爲公之世而不之逮也。冉有、季路以政事名者。季路曰：「千乘之國，攝乎大國之間，加之以師旅，因之以饑饉，由也爲之，可使有勇，且知方也。」冉有曰：「方六七十，如五六十，求也爲之，可使足民。如其禮樂，以俟君子。」則庶幾乎所謂知本者矣。故夫子許之，而不以爲大也。然則夫子之大也如之何？曰：子貢曰：「立之斯立，道之斯行，綏之斯來，動之斯和。」此夫子之所以不可及，如天之不可階而升也。謹對。

第四問
任有齡
同考試官教諭王，批：〔我〕朝立法之初意，本如此。子能言之，佳士也。
考試官教諭李，批：〔是知時務者。〕
考試官學正周，批：〔有議論。〕

天下未有不可行之法，其所以不能行者，
translation_en:
…his proper place, without encroaching upon others. Their urgent concern, as though they could not rest easy for even a single day, was entirely for this. Confucius longed for an age when the Great Way prevailed and the world belonged to all, but could not attain it. Ran You and Jilu were renowned for their ability in government. Jilu said: “A state of a thousand chariots, hemmed in between great states, beset by invading armies and then afflicted by famine—if I, You, governed it, I could give its people courage and make them understand the right course.” Ran You said: “A territory sixty or seventy li square, or fifty or sixty—if I, Qiu, governed it, I could provide sufficiently for its people. As for its rites and music, I would await a gentleman.” They thus came close to what is called understanding the fundamentals. Hence Confucius approved of them, yet did not consider their accomplishments great. What, then, constituted Confucius’s greatness? The answer is in Zigong’s words: “If he established them, they would stand; if he guided them, they would proceed; if he brought them peace, they would come to him; if he stirred them, they would live in harmony.” This is why Confucius could not be equaled, just as heaven cannot be reached by climbing steps. Respectfully submitted in reply.

Fourth Question
Ren Youling
Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: “The original intent behind our dynasty’s establishment of laws was precisely this. That you can articulate it shows you to be a worthy scholar.”
Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “Here is someone who understands the affairs of the times.”
Examiner Zhou, Instructor, comments: “There is reasoned argument here.”

There are no laws in the world that cannot be put into practice. The reason they cannot be implemented is …

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
不善用法者也夫立法者酌古之制準今
之宜以爲天下後世慮者至悉也用法者
不惟其法惟其意而已矣意也者今之宜
也苟能有以推而行之以不失乎古之制
焉其有偏而不舉者吾未之信也愚蜀人
也嘗見水利鹽法屯田茶馬四者先後錯
出有槩於心久矣而未之敢言也今因執
事之問請究言之可乎自李水鑿離堆堰
都江而水利自兹始矣涸脛泛肩之誓沉
===
于犀浦深灘淺堰之諭紀于鷄臺洞開三
泊江辨雙流我
朝築堰之法大因若是而已壘石以築堰範
鍾以淘灘利水州縣如郫繁崇灌所出夫
匠歲不下千人而灌田亦幾萬計已而江
之順怒不常人之機械百出其中黠者欲
乘間以牟利乃倡爲鐵龍之議鑄冶垂成
而奔濤卒至蕩折已無餘矣又欲從而脩
之而不知利沒奸諛勞歸庶姓而旱澇卒
punctuated:
不善用法者也。夫立法者，酌古之制，準今之宜，以爲天下後世慮者至悉也。用法者，不惟其法，惟其意而已矣。意也者，今之宜也。苟能有以推而行之，以不失乎古之制焉，其有偏而不舉者，吾未之信也。愚，蜀人也，嘗見水利、鹽法、屯田、茶馬四者先後錯出，有槩於心久矣，而未之敢言也。今因執事之問，請究言之，可乎？
自李水鑿離堆、堰都江，而水利自兹始矣。涸脛泛肩之誓，沉于犀浦；深灘淺堰之諭，紀于鷄臺。洞開三泊，江辨雙流。我朝築堰之法，大因若是而已。壘石以築堰，範鍾以淘灘。利水州縣，如郫、繁、崇、灌，所出夫匠，歲不下千人，而灌田亦幾萬計。已而江之順怒不常，人之機械百出。其中黠者，欲乘間以牟利，乃倡爲鐵龍之議。鑄冶垂成，而奔濤卒至，蕩折已無餘矣。又欲從而脩之，而不知利沒奸諛，勞歸庶姓，而旱澇卒
translation_en:
…those who do not know how to apply the laws properly. Those who establish laws weigh ancient institutions against the needs of the present, considering most thoroughly the welfare of the realm and future generations. Those who apply laws must attend to their intent, rather than merely to their provisions. That intent is to meet the needs of the present. If one can extend and implement them without departing from ancient institutions, I cannot believe that any aspect would remain neglected or unimplemented. I am a man of Shu. I have long observed the successive and intermingled workings of four systems—water management, the salt administration, military agricultural colonies, and the tea-and-horse trade—and have long felt concern about them, but have not dared to speak. Now that you, sir, have posed this question, may I discuss them fully?
Water management here began when Li Shui [?] cut through Lidui and dammed the Dujiang. The injunction concerning dry shins and submerged shoulders [?] was sunk at Xipu; the instruction to dredge the shoals deeply and keep the weir low was recorded at Jitai. Three pools were opened up [?], and the river was divided into two streams. Our dynasty’s methods of building weirs have largely followed these precedents. Stones are piled up to build weirs, and bells are cast as guides for dredging the shoals [?]. Prefectures and counties benefiting from the water, such as Pi, Fan, Chong, and Guan, supply no fewer than a thousand laborers and artisans each year, while the fields irrigated likewise number in the tens of thousands.
Yet the river is sometimes placid and sometimes violent, and people devise all manner of contrivances. Some crafty men among them, seeking to exploit an opportunity for profit, proposed an “iron dragon.” Casting was nearly complete when raging waves suddenly arrived and swept away and broke everything, leaving nothing behind. They then wished to repair it, failing to recognize that the profits were swallowed up by crafty flatterers, while the toil fell upon the common people, and that, in the end, drought and flooding…

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
無補也是豈立法初意哉或者議曰昔之
遺法固在也因而飭之其誰曰不可故隨
内外以導沫江因淺深以通灌口力役則
計田疇以爲多寡雇役則度遠邇以爲重
輕而又相下澤以疏流慎司工以勸事其
庶矣乎或又曰鐵龍之議特因一時之卒
漲耳未可遽以爲非也嗟乎禹之治水水
之性也故深淘淺築正得其遺意而乃高
爲隄堰故與水闘幾何其不敗也昔文翁
===
守成都開煎湔口溉灌繁田人獲其饒是
亦不可爲法乎自管子謹正鹽筴而鹽法
由此興矣南鹽於海北鹽於池而蜀鹽於
井自贍一方於大農國計無與焉我
朝開中之法行之久矣有提課以督成有監
司以會要凡鹽州縣如順義長寧大者不
下數十萬小者亦不下數萬已而商之要
權不時竈之貼納無出其間黠者欲巧言
以奪正乃倡爲折納之議自此鹽額十萬
punctuated:
無補也，是豈立法初意哉？或者議曰：「昔之遺法固在也，因而飭之，其誰曰不可？故隨内外以導沫江，因淺深以通灌口；力役則計田疇以爲多寡，雇役則度遠邇以爲重輕；而又相下澤以疏流，慎司工以勸事，其庶矣乎？」或又曰：「鐵龍之議，特因一時之卒漲耳，未可遽以爲非也。」嗟乎！禹之治水，水之性也。故深淘淺築，正得其遺意，而乃高爲隄堰，故與水闘，幾何其不敗也？昔文翁守成都，開煎湔口，溉灌繁田，人獲其饒，是亦不可爲法乎？
自管子謹正鹽筴，而鹽法由此興矣。南鹽於海，北鹽於池，而蜀鹽於井，自贍一方，於大農國計無與焉。我朝開中之法，行之久矣。有提課以督成，有監司以會要。凡鹽州縣，如順義、長寧，大者不下數十萬，小者亦不下數萬。已而商之要權不時，竈之貼納無出，其間黠者欲巧言以奪正，乃倡爲折納之議。自此鹽額十萬
translation_en:
…offers no relief. Can this have been the original intention in establishing these regulations? Some argue: “The methods bequeathed by earlier generations certainly remain. Who could object to putting them in order on that basis? Guide the Mo River along its inner and outer channels, and keep Guankou open according to the varying depths. Assess labor service in proportion to the acreage of fields, and adjust the burden of hired labor according to distance. Further, survey the low-lying marshes to open drainage channels, and carefully select those overseeing the works to encourage their completion. Would this not come close to what is needed?” Others say: “The proposal for iron dragons merely encountered a sudden flood on one occasion; it cannot hastily be judged wrong.” Alas! Yu controlled the waters by following their nature. Thus, dredging deep and building weirs low precisely preserves his intention. Yet people instead build high dikes and weirs, thereby contending with the water. How could they avoid failure? Formerly, when Wen Weng governed Chengdu, he opened the Jianjian outlet [?], irrigating the fields of Guan and Fan, and the people enjoyed the resulting abundance. Could this not also serve as a model?
Salt regulations originated when Master Guan carefully put salt policy in order. In the south, salt comes from the sea; in the north, from salt ponds; and in Shu, from wells. Shu’s salt supplies its own region and contributes nothing to the central treasury’s national finances. Our dynasty’s system of issuing salt trading permits in return for deliveries of grain has long been in operation. There are tax collection officials to supervise fulfillment and surveillance officials to collate the essential accounts. Among the salt-producing subprefectures and counties, such as Shunyi and Changning, the larger yield no fewer than several hundred thousand, and even the smaller no fewer than several tens of thousands. Subsequently, merchants’ demands and exercise of influence became irregular [?], while salt producers had no means of making supplementary payments. Cunning men among them sought to overturn proper arrangements with specious arguments, and therefore advocated payment by commutation. From this point, the salt quota of one hundred thousand…

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
而今不及十千矣又欲從而議復其舊然
不知舊井既枯新井或淡出課微耿招之
不來而緩急卒無補也是豈立法初意哉
或者議曰昔之遺法固在也遵而行之其
誰曰不可故復開中而先寬其科條清埋
沒而不追其既往或棧閉廢井以蘇窮困
或覈出虛額以絕誅求而又稽井戶之逃
移禁客戶之占佃其庶矣乎或又曰牢盤
之法井戶具盤而納箄商人具引而納箄
則竈可免於追徵而商可免於開中矣是
===
又一說也昔楊輔總計四川收引稅錢井
戶稱便是又不可爲法乎屯田之制
國初專以養兵分田有限徵納有時或失則
多或失則寡莫不有畫一之法存焉歲月
既久奸究彌深遂使疊溪之屯徵於綿竹
廣利之屯徵於龍安不知而妄議者尤欲
爲清屯之令吁戶口不實占田官司不能
覆畝殆如漢之檢覆墾田然而河南南陽
punctuated:
而今不及十千矣。又欲從而議復其舊，然不知舊井既枯，新井或淡，出課微耿，招之不來，而緩急卒無補也。是豈立法初意哉？或者議曰：「昔之遺法固在也，遵而行之，其誰曰不可？」故復開中而先寬其科條，清埋沒而不追其既往，或棧閉廢井以蘇窮困，或覈出虛額以絕誅求，而又稽井戶之逃移，禁客戶之占佃，其庶矣乎？或又曰：「牢盤之法，井戶具盤而納箄，商人具引而納箄，則竈可免於追徵，而商可免於開中矣。」是又一說也。昔楊輔總計四川，收引稅錢，井戶稱便，是又不可爲法乎？

屯田之制，國初專以養兵，分田有限，徵納有時，或失則多，或失則寡，莫不有畫一之法存焉。歲月既久，奸究彌深，遂使疊溪之屯徵於綿竹，廣利之屯徵於龍安。不知而妄議者，尤欲爲清屯之令。吁！戶口不實，占田官司不能覆畝，殆如漢之檢覆墾田，然而河南南陽
translation_en:
…yet now it falls short of ten thousand. Some now wish to propose restoring the former arrangements. They do not realize, however, that the old wells have dried up, that some new wells yield weak brine, and that their tax yield is meager [?]. Those summoned do not come, and ultimately the arrangements offer no help in meeting urgent needs. Could this have been the original intention in establishing the system?

Some argue: “The regulations handed down from earlier times certainly still exist. Who could object to following and implementing them?” Thus, restore the system of exchanging grain deliveries for salt certificates, but first relax its regulations; investigate concealed holdings without pursuing past offenses; close abandoned wells to relieve those in hardship; or identify fictitious quotas to end oppressive exactions. In addition, investigate the flight and migration of well households and prohibit nonlocal households from taking possession of or leasing the wells. Might this come close to a solution?

Others say: “Under the salt-pan system [?], well households furnish pans and submit bi 箄 [?], while merchants furnish salt certificates and submit bi 箄 [?]. Salt producers can then be spared demands for arrears, and merchants can be spared the grain-delivery requirement.” This is another proposal. Formerly, when Yang Fu oversaw Sichuan’s finances, he collected monetary taxes on salt certificates, and the well households found this convenient. Could this, too, not serve as a model?

The military agricultural colony system was devoted exclusively to supporting the troops at the beginning of the dynasty. Land allotments had prescribed limits, and levies and payments had fixed times. Errors might result in too much or too little, but uniform regulations existed for all of these matters. As the years passed, fraudulent abuses [?] became ever more deeply entrenched, until levies for the Diexi military colonies were collected in Mianzhu, and those for the Guangli military colonies in Long’an. Those who discuss the matter recklessly, without understanding it, are especially eager to issue orders to investigate and rectify the military colonies. Alas! Household and population registers are inaccurate, and the authorities cannot verify the acreage of occupied land. This is much like the Han dynasty’s inspection and verification of cultivated fields; yet Henan and Nanyang…

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
至不可問其失寖遠矣或者議曰
紅牌之制賞罰固在也使能守其成法按魚
鱗之冊籍以稽隱界勾絕戶之田畝以授
餘夫明主保下田之禁正屯官徵輸之條
豪右侵奪有罰貧悴貸假有罰其孰曰非
初意也或又曰有田之屯可知也無屯之
田不可知也可不重加之意乎昔諸葛武
侯營屯渭濵軍有宿儲無亦存乎其人耳
國初茶法專以易馬與秦隴無異也歲遣巡
===
察一人凡私越境者刑無赦副是廢置不
常奸萌寖起遂使建始之茶私越沉黎武
岡之商擅抵蒙雅不知而妄議者猶欲利
其餘課十而稅一殊不知茶以引計不及
引者則謂之由殆如宋人之長短引然而
又可因以爲利乎其失益甚矣或者議曰
金牌之制差發固在也使能師其遺意稽截
引之目而繳報以限嚴互市之令而譏察
以時碉門之茶馬有司可復也黑水之批
punctuated:
至不可問，其失寖遠矣。或者議曰：「紅牌之制，賞罰固在也。使能守其成法，按魚鱗之冊籍以稽隱界，勾絕戶之田畝以授餘夫，明主保下田之禁，正屯官徵輸之條，豪右侵奪有罰，貧悴貸假有罰，其孰曰非初意也？」或又曰：「有田之屯可知也，無屯之田不可知也，可不重加之意乎？」昔諸葛武侯營屯渭濵，軍有宿儲，無亦存乎其人耳。
國初茶法，專以易馬，與秦隴無異也。歲遣巡察一人，凡私越境者，刑無赦。副是廢置不常，奸萌寖起，遂使建始之茶私越沉黎，武岡之商擅抵蒙雅。不知而妄議者，猶欲利其餘，課十而稅一。殊不知茶以引計，不及引者則謂之由，殆如宋人之長短引，然而又可因以爲利乎？其失益甚矣。或者議曰：「金牌之制，差發固在也。使能師其遺意，稽截引之目而繳報以限，嚴互市之令而譏察以時，碉門之茶馬有司可復也，黑水之批
translation_en:
…even became impossible to investigate; the departure from the original arrangements has grown ever greater. Some argue: “Under the red-plaque system, rewards and punishments are already provided for. If its established regulations could be maintained, the fish-scale cadastral registers consulted to investigate concealed boundaries, the acreage of extinct households identified and assigned to surplus adult males, the prohibition concerning guarantors and the taking of land clarified [?], and the rules governing collection and remittance by military agricultural colony officials rectified—with penalties for encroachment and seizure by powerful families, and penalties for loans to the impoverished [?]—who could say that this was not the original intent?” Others say: “Colonies with land can be identified, but land without colonies cannot. Should this not receive particular attention?” In former times, Zhuge Liang, Marquis of Wu, established agricultural colonies along the Wei River, and his army had provisions in reserve. Does this not ultimately depend upon the person in charge?
At the beginning of the dynasty, the tea regulations were devoted exclusively to exchanging tea for horses, no differently from those in Qin and Long. Each year one official was dispatched to conduct inspections; anyone crossing the frontier illicitly was punished without pardon. Subsequently [?], these arrangements were irregularly abolished and restored, and abuses gradually arose. As a result, tea from Jianshi was carried illicitly across into Chenli, and merchants from Wugang proceeded without authorization to Meng and Ya. Those who discuss the matter rashly, without understanding it, still wish to profit from the surplus by imposing a tax of one in ten. They fail entirely to understand that tea is reckoned by permits, and that an amount below that covered by a permit is covered by what is called a you certificate—much like the long and short permits of the Song. Yet can this, too, be made a source of profit? The departure from the original arrangements has become still more serious. Some argue: “Under the gold-plaque system, requisition obligations are already established. If its surviving principles could be followed, the records of canceled tea permits checked and their surrender reported within a fixed deadline, and the regulations for frontier trade strictly enforced with timely inspections, the tea-and-horse administrative office at Diaomen could be restored, and the permit-inspection establishment at Heishui…”

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
驗有所可復也番僧盜鬻有罰漢人私遞
有罰其誰曰非初意也或又曰無引之茶
可知也無茶之引不可知也是可不加之
意乎昔趙開判成都減額以蘇園戶輕價
以惠行商民到于今稱之無亦存乎其人
耳此四者皆裕國足邊之助也愚之所陳
皆就其補偏救弊者言之耳若其所以行
之之意則未之敢言也蓋古今言利者率
譬之飲食之人而人皆賤之也故多諱而
===
不言也嗟乎飲食之人人皆賤之然天下
豈有不飲不食之人耶故同一利也行之
而義雖利亦義也同一義也行之而利雖
利亦義也況於裕國足邊之助其可不之
講乎易曰天地之大德曰生聖人之大寶
曰位何以守位曰仁何以聚人曰財理財
正辭禁民為非曰義此又萬世理財之大
道也執事以為然否
第五問
punctuated:
驗有所可復也。番僧盜鬻有罰，漢人私遞有罰，其誰曰非初意也？或又曰：「無引之茶可知也，無茶之引不可知也，是可不加之意乎？」昔趙開判成都，減額以蘇園戶，輕價以惠行商，民到于今稱之。無亦存乎其人耳。此四者皆裕國足邊之助也。愚之所陳，皆就其補偏救弊者言之耳。若其所以行之之意，則未之敢言也。蓋古今言利者，率譬之飲食之人，而人皆賤之也，故多諱而不言也。嗟乎！飲食之人，人皆賤之，然天下豈有不飲不食之人耶？故同一利也，行之而義，雖利亦義也；同一義也，行之而利，雖利亦義也。況於裕國足邊之助，其可不之講乎？《易》曰：「天地之大德曰生，聖人之大寶曰位。何以守位？曰仁。何以聚人？曰財。理財正辭，禁民為非，曰義。」此又萬世理財之大道也。執事以為然否？

第五問
translation_en:
…the verification procedures could also be restored. If Tibetan monks are punished for illicit sales, and Han Chinese are punished for clandestine conveyance, who could say that this departs from the original intent? Others say: “Tea without permits can be detected, but permits without tea cannot. Can this fail to receive our attention?” Formerly, when Zhao Kai administered Chengdu, he reduced quotas to relieve tea growers and lowered prices to benefit traveling merchants. The people praise him to this day. Perhaps it simply depends upon having the right person.

These four measures all help enrich the state and adequately supply the frontier. What I have humbly presented concerns only their capacity to correct imbalances and remedy abuses. As for the guiding intent with which they should be implemented, I have not yet ventured to speak. Those who discuss material profit, past and present, are generally likened to people preoccupied with food and drink, whom everyone despises. Thus many avoid the subject and do not speak of it. Alas! Everyone despises those preoccupied with food and drink, yet is there anyone under Heaven who neither eats nor drinks? Thus, with the same pursuit of profit, if its implementation accords with righteousness, even profit is righteous. With the same pursuit of righteousness, if its implementation yields profit, even profit is righteous [?]. How much more necessary, then, is it to discuss measures that help enrich the state and adequately supply the frontier?

The Book of Changes says: “The great virtue of Heaven and Earth is called life; the great treasure of the sage is called position. How is position maintained? Through benevolence. How are people gathered? Through wealth. Regulating wealth, rectifying words, and forbidding the people to do wrong constitute righteousness.” This, moreover, is the great Way of managing wealth for all ages. Do you, honored examiners, consider this correct?

Fifth Question

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
羅玥
同考試官教諭文　批〔自古禦戎之機要具在方策子能歷歷言之是幸布而有天下之慮者也〕
考試官教諭李　批〔能知會要分合之意可嘉〕
考試官學正周　批〔憂深識遠〕
嘗謂善禦戎者貴有禦戎之實而名不與
焉甚矣名實之相眩也久矣有禦戎之實
而無其名則其實無不章矣有禦戎之名
而無其實則其名無不隳矣故君子非無
===
名之為患有名而實不足以副之斯為可
憂耳愚書生也其何足以知軍旅之事然
嘗習聞其說敢因明問而言之夫西戎之
為患其所由來遠矣粵自堯舜來王之後
以迄商周薄伐之餘英君誼辟屢以為心
謀臣智士各出所見語即敘者則曰非德
無以化要荒然不知無耀威之實則德有
時而詘矣語卒獲者則曰非兵無以服凶
獷然不知無脩德之實則兵有時而黷矣
punctuated:
羅玥

同考試官教諭文批〔自古禦戎之機要，具在方策。子能歷歷言之，是幸布而有天下之慮者也。〕
考試官教諭李批〔能知會要分合之意，可嘉。〕
考試官學正周批〔憂深識遠。〕

嘗謂善禦戎者，貴有禦戎之實，而名不與焉。甚矣，名實之相眩也！久矣！有禦戎之實而無其名，則其實無不章矣；有禦戎之名而無其實，則其名無不隳矣。故君子非無名之為患，有名而實不足以副之，斯為可憂耳。愚書生也，其何足以知軍旅之事？然嘗習聞其說，敢因明問而言之。夫西戎之為患，其所由來遠矣。粵自堯舜來王之後，以迄商周薄伐之餘，英君誼辟，屢以為心；謀臣智士，各出所見。語即敘者，則曰非德無以化要荒，然不知無耀威之實，則德有時而詘矣；語卒獲者，則曰非兵無以服凶獷，然不知無脩德之實，則兵有時而黷矣。
translation_en:
Luo Yue 羅玥

Comment by Associate Examiner Wen, Instructor: 〔The essential principles of defending against the Rong have all been recorded in writings since antiquity. You can explain them distinctly, one by one: you are someone who, though of humble station [?], concerns himself with all under Heaven.〕
Comment by Examiner Li, Instructor: 〔Your understanding of the intent behind bringing together the essentials and distinguishing and combining them [?] is commendable.〕
Comment by Examiner Zhou, School Instructor: 〔Deep concern and far-reaching insight.〕

I have often maintained that those skilled in defending against the Rong value actual achievement in such defense; reputation has no part in it. How greatly reputation and reality obscure one another! How long this has been so! Where there is actual achievement in defending against the Rong but no reputation for it, that achievement will assuredly become manifest. Where there is a reputation for defending against the Rong but no actual achievement, that reputation will assuredly collapse. Thus the gentleman does not regard the absence of reputation as a cause for concern. What warrants concern is possessing a reputation without sufficient actual achievement to match it.

I am merely an unlearned scholar: what qualification have I to understand military affairs? Yet I have often heard discussions of them, and venture to speak in response to your illuminating question. The troubles caused by the Western Rong have a long history. From their coming to acknowledge royal authority under Yao and Shun, down through the punitive expeditions of the Shang and Zhou, enlightened rulers and righteous sovereigns repeatedly took this matter to heart, while resourceful ministers and wise men each offered their views. Those who speak of bringing them into an ordered relationship say that only virtue can transform the distant outer domains. Yet they do not understand that without an actual display of might, virtue will sometimes be frustrated. Those who speak of finally subduing them say that only arms can bring the fierce and unruly to submission. Yet they do not understand that without the actual cultivation of virtue, arms will sometimes be used wantonly. …

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
語講盟者則曰要結可以來遠然不知無
制人之實則盟不可恃也語固守者則曰
設險可以守邦然不知無效死之實則險
不可恃也自昔封疆之臣吾於唐得二人
馬貞元之中韋臯節度劍南人皆曰傾内
資結和好是臯之所有事也而不知崔堯
臣之趨石門董振之徇維州王英俊之薄
松州則皆其實也豈但盟好已乎太和之
初李德裕節度川蜀人皆曰招梿邊肆攻
===
伐是裕之所有事也而不知城仗義以制
大渡城禦侮以控榮經城柔遠以阨西山
皆其實也豈直攻伐已乎議者曰盟之而
固則盟未必爲非攻之而叛則攻未必爲
是二子之在當時必有以也或者執其一
端而遽議其優劣恐非千古之定論也至
於維州之取舍吾於宋得二人焉司馬光
曰新與之盟而遽納其叛語利則維州小
而信大語害則維州緩而關中急德裕所
punctuated:
語講盟者則曰：「要結可以來遠。」然不知無制人之實，則盟不可恃也。語固守者則曰：「設險可以守邦。」然不知無效死之實，則險不可恃也。自昔封疆之臣，吾於唐得二人馬。貞元之中，韋臯節度劍南，人皆曰：「傾内資，結和好，是臯之所有事也。」而不知崔堯臣之趨石門、董振之徇維州、王英俊之薄松州，則皆其實也，豈但盟好已乎？太和之初，李德裕節度川蜀，人皆曰：「招梿邊，肆攻伐，是裕之所有事也。」而不知城仗義以制大渡，城禦侮以控榮經，城柔遠以阨西山，皆其實也，豈直攻伐已乎？議者曰：「盟之而固，則盟未必爲非；攻之而叛，則攻未必爲是。」二子之在當時，必有以也。或者執其一端，而遽議其優劣，恐非千古之定論也。

至於維州之取舍，吾於宋得二人焉。司馬光曰：「新與之盟，而遽納其叛，語利則維州小而信大，語害則維州緩而關中急。德裕所
translation_en:
Those who advocate negotiating alliances say: “Binding agreements can draw distant peoples to us.” Yet they do not realize that without the actual capacity to control others, alliances cannot be relied upon. Those who advocate firm defense say: “Establishing strategic defenses can safeguard the realm.” Yet they do not realize that without a real willingness to fight to the death, strategic defenses cannot be relied upon. Among the frontier officials of former times, I find two men in the Tang [?]. During the Zhenyuan era, Wei Gao served as Military Commissioner of Jiannan. People all said: “Exhausting domestic resources to establish friendly relations—this is what Gao devotes himself to.” Yet they did not recognize that Cui Yaochen’s advance toward Shimen, Dong Zhen’s campaign through Weizhou, and Wang Yingjun’s advance against Songzhou all provided the practical substance behind his policy. Was it merely a matter of alliances and friendship? At the beginning of the Taihe era, Li Deyu served as Military Commissioner in Sichuan. People all said: “Stirring up the frontier [?] and freely launching attacks—this is what Deyu devotes himself to.” Yet they did not recognize that fortifying Zhangyi to command the Dadu, fortifying Yuwu to control Rongjing, and fortifying Rouyuan to block the Western Mountains all provided the practical substance behind his policy. Was it merely a matter of attack and conquest? Commentators say: “If an alliance with them brings stability, making an alliance is not necessarily wrong; if attacking them brings rebellion, attacking is not necessarily right.” These two men must each have had reasons for their actions at the time. Some seize upon a single aspect and hastily pronounce one superior and the other inferior; I fear that such judgments cannot stand as definitive verdicts for all ages.

As for whether to retain or relinquish Weizhou, I find two men in the Song. Sima Guang said: “Having just made an alliance with them, one suddenly accepts their rebels. In terms of advantage, Weizhou is a small matter, while good faith is a great one; in terms of danger, Weizhou is a less urgent concern, while Guanzhong is an immediate one. What Deyu …

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
言徇利而忘義矣胡寅曰維州本唐故㙜
取我故地以刷前日之耻正以大義謀國
事者而乃以爲利可乎議者又曰使德裕
當時具其事而請之朝可也或留其人而
歸其地亦可也乃不出此致使僧孺借信
以報讎則裕亦不能無咎也其然豈其然
哉我
朝開設松潘東綴安綿南控威茂譬如人之
一身松潘其首也安綿威茂其股肱也番
===
酋比附於外村官控禦於中
聖謨神武淵乎盛矣嗣後五寨塞而威茂分三
溪叛而安綿出致使手足頭目各不相顧
其何以聯屬而成身乎此所以有白草之
變而屢執事之問也愚嘗讀申孝友會要
而有感於松潘之事其言曰西南諸番雖
衆且微然而勢合則强力分則弱必離其
黨使不得親分其勢使不得不弱斯可也
由此觀之則我當合而彼當分也亦明矣
punctuated:
言，徇利而忘義矣。」胡寅曰：「維州本唐故㙜，取我故地以刷前日之耻，正以大義謀國事者，而乃以爲利，可乎？」議者又曰：「使德裕當時具其事而請之朝，可也；或留其人而歸其地，亦可也。乃不出此，致使僧孺借信以報讎，則裕亦不能無咎也。」其然？豈其然哉？
我朝開設松潘，東綴安綿，南控威茂。譬如人之一身，松潘其首也，安綿威茂其股肱也。番酋比附於外，村官控禦於中，聖謨神武，淵乎盛矣！嗣後五寨塞而威茂分，三溪叛而安綿出，致使手足頭目各不相顧，其何以聯屬而成身乎？此所以有白草之變，而屢執事之問也。愚嘗讀申孝友會要，而有感於松潘之事。其言曰：「西南諸番雖衆且微，然而勢合則强，力分則弱。必離其黨，使不得親；分其勢，使不得不弱，斯可也。」由此觀之，則我當合而彼當分也，亦明矣。
translation_en:
…what [Li Deyu] said pursued advantage and forgot righteousness.” Hu Yin said: “Weizhou was originally an old Tang possession [?]. To recover our former territory and wipe away our earlier humiliation was precisely to plan affairs of state according to great righteousness. Can one instead call this the pursuit of advantage?” Critics further said: “Had Deyu at that time fully reported the circumstances and sought the court’s decision, that would have been acceptable. Alternatively, he could have retained the people and returned the territory. Yet he adopted neither course, allowing [Niu] Sengru to use good faith as a pretext for settling a grudge. Thus Deyu, too, cannot be free of blame.” Is that so? Can it really be so?
Our dynasty established Songpan, linking it eastward with Anzhou and Mianzhou and securing Weizhou and Maozhou to the south. To compare it to a human body, Songpan is its head, while Anzhou, Mianzhou, Weizhou, and Maozhou are its limbs. Tribal chieftains attach themselves to us on the outside, while village officials [?] maintain control within. How profound and magnificent are the sage imperial plans and divine martial prowess! Subsequently, the five stockades became obstructed and Weizhou and Maozhou were cut off; Sanxi rebelled, and Anzhou and Mianzhou were left outside [?]. Consequently, hands, feet, head, and eyes could no longer attend to one another. How could they remain connected and constitute a body? This is why the Baicao uprising occurred and why you, honored officials, have repeatedly raised the question.
I once read Shen Xiaoyou’s Collected Essentials (Huiyao) and was moved to reflect on the affairs of Songpan. It says: “Although the various southwestern tribes are numerous, they are individually weak. Nevertheless, when their power is united, they are strong; when their strength is divided, they are weak. We must separate their factions so that they cannot maintain close ties, and divide their power so that they cannot but become weak. Only then will matters be satisfactory.” Viewed in this light, it is also clear that we should be united and they should be divided.

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
胡今之不然也故松潘之勢似合而其中
背蕪越以相視實則分也白草之寨似分
而其黨皆患難以相死實則合也豈不尤
爲可異哉至於軍旅名實之間尤有未易
言者軍儲曰充積矣而實則無挾纊之惠
兵械曰犀利矣而實則無攻堅之用號爲
智將矣豈無小勇而大怯者乎號爲精兵
矣豈無中乾而外强者乎鄉勇可以爲守
而實則强雜不一也熟番可用爲間而實
===
則向背無常也然則爲今日之計其將如
之何哉亦惟反前日之所爲而循名以責
實斯可耳陸贄曰脩封疆守要害斬蹊隧
壘軍營謹禁防明斥堠務農以足食練卒
以蓄威非萬全不謀非百克不鬬寇小至
則張聲勢以遏其入寇大至則謀其大以
邀其歸據險以乘之多方以誤之使其勇
無所加衆無所用掠則靡獲攻則不能進
有腹背受敵之虞退有首尾難救之患此
punctuated:
胡今之不然也？故松潘之勢似合，而其中背蕪越以相視，實則分也；白草之寨似分，而其黨皆患難以相死，實則合也。豈不尤爲可異哉！至於軍旅名實之間，尤有未易言者。軍儲曰充積矣，而實則無挾纊之惠；兵械曰犀利矣，而實則無攻堅之用。號爲智將矣，豈無小勇而大怯者乎？號爲精兵矣，豈無中乾而外强者乎？鄉勇可以爲守，而實則强雜不一也；熟番可用爲間，而實則向背無常也。

然則爲今日之計，其將如之何哉？亦惟反前日之所爲，而循名以責實，斯可耳。陸贄曰：「脩封疆，守要害，斬蹊隧，壘軍營，謹禁防，明斥堠，務農以足食，練卒以蓄威。非萬全不謀，非百克不鬬。寇小至，則張聲勢以遏其入；寇大至，則謀其大以邀其歸。據險以乘之，多方以誤之，使其勇無所加，衆無所用，掠則靡獲，攻則不能，進有腹背受敵之虞，退有首尾難救之患。」此
translation_en:
Why is this not so today? The forces at Songpan thus appear united, but within their ranks they turn away from one another and regard each other as strangers [?]; in reality they are divided. The stockades of Baicao appear divided, yet their confederates will die for one another in adversity; in reality they are united. Is this not especially extraordinary? As for the discrepancy between reputation and reality in military affairs, there is still more that is not easy to discuss. Military provisions are said to be amply stocked, yet the soldiers receive no kindness that makes them feel as though clad in padded silk. Weapons are said to be sharp and effective, yet in practice they are of no use in attacking fortified positions. Among those called wise generals, are there none who show courage in small matters but cowardice in great ones? Among those called elite troops, are there none who are hollow within but outwardly strong? Local militia can serve for defense, yet in reality their strength and composition are uneven [?]. The acculturated indigenous peoples can be employed as spies, yet in reality their allegiance is inconstant.

What, then, should our plan be today? We need only reverse what was done before and demand that reality match the claims. Lu Zhi said: “Put the frontier defenses in order, hold strategic positions, cut off paths and passages, fortify military camps, maintain strict security, make reconnaissance effective, promote agriculture to ensure sufficient food, and train soldiers to build up military strength. Undertake no plan unless it is completely secure; engage in no battle unless victory is certain. When raiders come in small numbers, make a show of force to prevent their entry; when they come in great numbers, devise a major strategy to intercept their return. Occupy difficult terrain to take advantage of them, and mislead them by many devices. Ensure that their courage has no scope and their numbers are of no use: let them gain nothing by plundering and accomplish nothing by attacking. Advancing, they should fear being attacked from front and rear; retreating, they should face the danger that the head and tail of their column cannot come to each other’s aid.” This …

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
固責實之道也然勢有難易事有後先機
有緩急時有利害又不可以一言盡也故
權不可預設變不可先圖可懷則懷脩德
明刑柔遠能邇以明天地之紀以別華夷
之限此懷之之實也可攻則攻批亢擣虛
形格勢禁搗其會而後動慮其勝而後進
此攻之之實也可守則守高城深池堅甲
利兵以養士卒之氣以息兆人之勤此守
之之實也可盟則盟以束牲歃血爲權宜
===
以選將厲兵爲實事以紓歲時之禍以堅
和好之心此盟之之實也此則又在爲將
者致審於難易先後緩急利害之間而求
其實耳非人所能與亦非人所能言也昔
武子十三篇利害相權奇正相生戰守攻
圍之法蓋以百數期於使人趨利而避害
而不知兵無常形而逆爲之形勝無常處
而多爲之地故君子尤或議其不知所以
用智而有取於宣王之詩曰綿綿翼翼不
punctuated:
固責實之道也。然勢有難易，事有後先，機有緩急，時有利害，又不可以一言盡也。故權不可預設，變不可先圖。可懷則懷，脩德明刑，柔遠能邇，以明天地之紀，以別華夷之限，此懷之之實也。可攻則攻，批亢擣虛，形格勢禁，搗其會而後動，慮其勝而後進，此攻之之實也。可守則守，高城深池，堅甲利兵，以養士卒之氣，以息兆人之勤，此守之之實也。可盟則盟，以束牲歃血爲權宜，以選將厲兵爲實事，以紓歲時之禍，以堅和好之心，此盟之之實也。此則又在爲將者致審於難易、先後、緩急、利害之間，而求其實耳，非人所能與，亦非人所能言也。
昔武子十三篇，利害相權，奇正相生，戰守攻圍之法，蓋以百數，期於使人趨利而避害。而不知兵無常形，而逆爲之形；勝無常處，而多爲之地。故君子尤或議其不知所以用智，而有取於宣王之詩曰：「綿綿翼翼，不
translation_en:
…is indeed the way to demand practical results. Yet circumstances may be difficult or easy; affairs have their proper sequence; opportunities may allow delay or demand haste; and the times may bring advantages or dangers. These cannot all be encompassed in a single statement. Thus expedient measures cannot be prescribed beforehand, nor can responses to change be planned in advance. When conciliation is possible, conciliate: cultivate virtue and make punishments clear, soothe those far away and bring those nearby into concord, thereby making manifest the order of Heaven and Earth and distinguishing the boundary between the Chinese and the foreign peoples. This is the substance of conciliation. When attack is possible, attack: strike at vital points and undefended places, constrain the enemy’s dispositions and check his momentum, strike at his points of convergence before making a move, and consider the prospects of victory before advancing. This is the substance of attack. When defense is possible, defend: build high walls and deep moats, make armor stout and weapons sharp, thereby nurturing the soldiers’ morale and relieving the toil of the multitude. This is the substance of defense. When a covenant is possible, conclude one: regard binding sacrificial animals and smearing the lips with blood as temporary expedients, while treating the selection of generals and the sharpening of weapons as the substantive work, thereby alleviating recurring calamities and strengthening the commitment to peaceful relations. This is the substance of making a covenant. All this, moreover, depends on the commander’s carefully weighing difficulty and ease, priorities, urgency, and advantage and harm, and seeking practical results. It is not something others can participate in or express for him.
In former times, the thirteen chapters of Master Wu [?] weighed advantage against harm and showed how unconventional and conventional operations generate one another. Their methods for battle, defense, attack, and siege numbered in the hundreds, aiming to lead people toward advantage and away from harm. Yet they failed to recognize that warfare has no fixed configuration, prescribing configurations in advance, and that victory has no fixed location, specifying numerous grounds for it. Thus gentlemen have sometimes criticized the work for failing to understand how to exercise wisdom, and have instead found merit in the poem concerning King Xuan, which says: “Unremitting and vigilant, not…”

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
測不克夫綿綿以爲奇而使敵不測翼翼
以爲正而使敵不克此萬古禦戎之心法
也不知執事以爲何如
punctuated: 測不克。夫綿綿以爲奇，而使敵不測；翼翼以爲正，而使敵不克。此萬古禦戎之心法也。不知執事以爲何如？
translation_en: …unfathomable and unconquerable. Indeed, sustained effort supplies the unorthodox tactics, making one unfathomable to the enemy; vigilant care supplies the orthodox tactics, making one unconquerable by the enemy. This is the essential principle for defending against hostile peoples for all time. I wonder what you, sir, think of it?

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
四川鄉試錄後序
四川鄉試錄成是日也歌鹿
鳴以昭
盛典叙酧禮行御史〔鳳鳴〕謂〔鴻〕
漸宜中一言以諗多士嘗聞
之夫士莫重乎其始進尤莫
先乎辨志志也者士之鵠也
===
鵠之中否射者定勝負而觀
德焉矧操道德以爲弓矢士
之鵠之遠且大也若是而志
弗之辨可乎志弗辨而可謂
之士乎然其辨也孰先於義
利名實人已之間昔宋儒周
敦頤曰實勝善也名勝耻也
