punctuated:
四川鄉試錄後序

四川鄉試錄成，是日也，歌鹿鳴以昭盛典，叙酧禮行。御史〔鳳鳴〕謂〔鴻〕漸：「宜中一言，以諗多士。」嘗聞之，夫士莫重乎其始進，尤莫先乎辨志。志也者，士之鵠也。鵠之中否，射者定勝負而觀德焉。矧操道德以爲弓矢，士之鵠之遠且大也若是，而志弗之辨，可乎？志弗辨，而可謂之士乎？然其辨也，孰先於義利、名實、人已之間？昔宋儒周敦頤曰：「實勝，善也；名勝，耻也。」
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Sichuan Provincial Examination

The Record of the Sichuan Provincial Examination was completed. On that day, “Deer Calling” was sung to give lustre to the grand ceremony, and the ritual of offering and returning wine cups in due order was performed. The censor, Fengming, said to Hongjian: “You should offer a few words [?] to instruct the assembled scholars.”

I have heard that nothing matters more for a scholar than his first entry into official life, and that above all he must distinguish clearly what he aspires to. Aspiration is the scholar’s target. Whether archers hit the target determines victory or defeat, and through this their virtue is observed. How much more so when one takes the Way and virtue as bow and arrows! When the scholar’s target is so distant and so great, can he fail to distinguish clearly his aspiration? If his aspiration is not clearly distinguished, can he be called a scholar? Yet in making these distinctions, what takes precedence over righteousness and profit, reputation and substance, and others and oneself [?]? The Song Confucian Zhou Dunyi once said: “When substance surpasses reputation, it is good; when reputation surpasses substance, it is shameful.”

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
張栻曰無所爲而爲者義也
有所爲而爲者利也及誦孔
子曰古之學者爲己今之學
者爲人則知二子名實義利
之辨大較自聖人之言始夫
士知所以爲己則志乎義而
實勝之矣否則徇夫人也其
===
不啗慾干譽者鮮矣其於爲
己乎玆氏名入錄者舉蜀之
選也方其講業之初慱觀載
籍則必以六經爲鵠而一切
詭經畔道詖詞衺說者弗繇
焉式軌前脩則必以賢若聖
爲鵠而凡片善寸長遺行可
punctuated:
張栻曰：「無所爲而爲者，義也；有所爲而爲者，利也。」及誦孔子曰：「古之學者爲己，今之學者爲人。」則知二子名實義利之辨，大較自聖人之言始。夫士知所以爲己，則志乎義而實勝之矣；否則徇夫人也，其不啗慾干譽者鮮矣。其於爲己乎？
玆氏名入錄者，舉蜀之選也。方其講業之初，慱觀載籍，則必以六經爲鵠，而一切詭經畔道、詖詞衺說者弗繇焉；式軌前脩，則必以賢若聖爲鵠，而凡片善寸長、遺行可
translation_en:
Zhang Shi said: “To act without an ulterior purpose is righteousness; to act with an ulterior purpose is the pursuit of profit.” And when we recite Confucius’s words, “Scholars of antiquity learned for their own sake; scholars today learn for the sake of others,” we recognize that the two masters’ distinctions between reputation and substance, and between righteousness and profit, originated in broad outline in the Sage’s words. If a scholar understands how to learn for his own sake, he sets his resolve upon righteousness, and substance prevails. Otherwise, he caters to others, and few such men refrain from indulging their desires and seeking acclaim. How could this amount to learning for one’s own sake?
Those whose names are entered in this record are the chosen men of Shu. When they first undertook their studies and read widely in the written records, they surely took the Six Classics as their target, refusing to follow anything that distorted the Classics or departed from the Way, or any biased rhetoric or perverse teachings. In taking their worthy predecessors as models, they surely took worthies and sages as their target, refusing to follow those with merely a scrap of goodness or a trifling strength, whose failings of conduct might …

title: 嘉靖二十五年四川鄉試錄
text:
訾者弗繇焉其志之所嚮前
無與禦後無與挽蓋萬夫之
特操而千仞之立壁也然一
弗之售則薾然沮抑自視不
勝其小視人不勝其大實者
名之義者利之若出二人然
嘻何淺之乎識也是故于士
===
進之始必辨志先焉以今之
進也達也達則志行然非有
所加也夫順飈而呼則響必
洪秉膏而植則獲必倍審固
正直發彼有的辨之精矣而
鵠之者我也其德業有不成
於天下哉嘗〻蜀事睹之萬
punctuated: 訾者弗繇焉。其志之所嚮，前無與禦，後無與挽，蓋萬夫之特操，而千仞之立壁也。然一弗之售，則薾然沮抑，自視不勝其小，視人不勝其大；實者名之，義者利之，若出二人然。嘻！何淺之乎識也！是故于士進之始，必辨志先焉。以今之進也，達也；達則志行，然非有所加也。夫順飈而呼，則響必洪；秉膏而植，則獲必倍。審固正直，發彼有的，辨之精矣，而鵠之者我也。其德業有不成於天下哉？嘗〻蜀事睹之萬
translation_en: …open to censure, they will not follow. Wherever their resolve is directed, none ahead can obstruct them, and none behind can pull them back. Such is integrity outstanding among ten thousand men, like a sheer cliff rising a thousand fathoms. Yet once they fail to gain recognition, they become dispirited and dejected: they regard themselves as utterly insignificant and others as immeasurably great. What was substance they turn into reputation; what was righteousness they turn into profit—as though they had become different men. Alas! How shallow their understanding! Thus, when a scholar first advances toward office, he must above all distinguish clearly the purpose of his resolve. Advancement now means attaining a position; attaining a position enables his resolve to be put into practice, yet adds nothing to it. If one calls with the wind, the sound will surely carry powerfully; if one plants in fertile soil [?], the harvest will surely double. Take careful aim, stand firm and upright, and shoot at a definite target: the distinctions have been drawn precisely, but it is I who must make that target my aim. How could one's virtue and achievements then fail to come to fruition in the world? Once … the affairs of Shu … witnessed … ten thousand [?] …
